# glib_macros - Rust

Source: https://gtk-rs.org/gtk-rs-core/stable/latest/docs/glib_macros/

## Macros[§](https://gtk-rs.org#macros)

- [clone](https://gtk-rs.org/macro.clone.html)
- Macro for passing variables as strong or weak references into a closure.
- [closure](https://gtk-rs.org/macro.closure.html)
- Macro for creating a `Closure``Closure::new`
- [closure_](https://gtk-rs.org/macro.closure_local.html)- local
- The same as `closure!``Closure::new_local``closure!`
- [cstr_](https://gtk-rs.org/macro.cstr_bytes.html)- bytes

## Attribute Macros[§](https://gtk-rs.org#attributes)

- [async_](https://gtk-rs.org/attr.async_test.html)- test
- An attribute macro for writing asynchronous test functions.
- [derived_](https://gtk-rs.org/attr.derived_properties.html)- properties
- When applied to `ObjectImpl`
- [flags](https://gtk-rs.org/attr.flags.html)
- Attribute macro for defining flags using the `bitflags`crate. This macro will also define a`GFlags::type_`function and the`glib::Value`
- [object_](https://gtk-rs.org/attr.object_interface.html)- interface
- Macro for boilerplate of `ObjectInterface`
- [object_](https://gtk-rs.org/attr.object_subclass.html)- subclass
- Macro for boilerplate of `ObjectSubclass`

## Derive Macros[§](https://gtk-rs.org#derives)

- [Boxed](https://gtk-rs.org/derive.Boxed.html)
- Derive macro for defining a `BoxedType``::type_`function and the`glib::Value``nullable`to get an implementation of`glib::value::ToValueOptional`.
- [Downgrade](https://gtk-rs.org/derive.Downgrade.html)
- Macro for deriving implementations of `glib::clone::Downgrade``glib::clone::Upgrade`
- [Enum](https://gtk-rs.org/derive.Enum.html)
- Derive macro to register a Rust enum in the GLib type system and derive the
`glib::Value`
- [Error](https://gtk-rs.org/derive.ErrorDomain.html)- Domain
- Derive macro for defining a GLib error domain and its associated
`ErrorDomain`
- [Properties](https://gtk-rs.org/derive.Properties.html)
- This macro enables you to derive object properties in a quick way.
- [Shared](https://gtk-rs.org/derive.SharedBoxed.html)- Boxed
- Derive macro for defining a `SharedType``::get_type`function and the`glib::Value``nullable`to get an implementation of`glib::value::ToValueOptional`.
- [Value](https://gtk-rs.org/derive.ValueDelegate.html)- Delegate
- Example
- [Variant](https://gtk-rs.org/derive.Variant.html)
- Derive macro for serializing/deserializing custom structs/enums as `glib::Variant`

[25](https://gtk-rs.org#25)
[26](https://gtk-rs.org#26)/// Macro for passing variables as strong or weak references into a closure.
[27](https://gtk-rs.org#27)///
[28](https://gtk-rs.org#28)/// This macro can be useful in combination with closures, e.g. signal handlers, to reduce the
[29](https://gtk-rs.org#29)/// boilerplate required for passing strong or weak references into the closure. It will
[30](https://gtk-rs.org#30)/// automatically create the new reference and pass it with the same name into the closure.
[31](https://gtk-rs.org#31)///
[32](https://gtk-rs.org#32)/// If upgrading the weak reference to a strong reference inside the closure is failing, the
[33](https://gtk-rs.org#33)/// closure is immediately returning an optional default return value. If none is provided, `()` is
[34](https://gtk-rs.org#34)/// returned.
[35](https://gtk-rs.org#35)///
[36](https://gtk-rs.org#36)/// **⚠️ IMPORTANT ⚠️**
[37](https://gtk-rs.org#37)///
[38](https://gtk-rs.org#38)/// `glib` needs to be in scope, so unless it's one of the direct crate dependencies, you need to
[39](https://gtk-rs.org#39)/// import it because `clone!` is using it. For example:
[40](https://gtk-rs.org#40)///
[41](https://gtk-rs.org#41)/// ```rust,ignore
[42](https://gtk-rs.org#42)/// use gtk::glib;
[43](https://gtk-rs.org#43)/// ```
[44](https://gtk-rs.org#44)///
[45](https://gtk-rs.org#45)/// ### Debugging
[46](https://gtk-rs.org#46)///
[47](https://gtk-rs.org#47)/// In case something goes wrong inside the `clone!` macro, we use the [`g_debug`] macro. Meaning
[48](https://gtk-rs.org#48)/// that if you want to see these debug messages, you'll have to set the `G_MESSAGES_DEBUG`
[49](https://gtk-rs.org#49)/// environment variable when running your code (either in the code directly or when running the
[50](https://gtk-rs.org#50)/// binary) to either "all" or [`CLONE_MACRO_LOG_DOMAIN`]:
[51](https://gtk-rs.org#51)///
[52](https://gtk-rs.org#52)/// [`g_debug`]: ../glib/macro.g_debug.html
[53](https://gtk-rs.org#53)/// [`CLONE_MACRO_LOG_DOMAIN`]: ../glib/constant.CLONE_MACRO_LOG_DOMAIN.html
[54](https://gtk-rs.org#54)///
[55](https://gtk-rs.org#55)/// ```rust,ignore
[56](https://gtk-rs.org#56)/// use glib::CLONE_MACRO_LOG_DOMAIN;
[57](https://gtk-rs.org#57)///
[58](https://gtk-rs.org#58)/// std::env::set_var("G_MESSAGES_DEBUG", CLONE_MACRO_LOG_DOMAIN);
[59](https://gtk-rs.org#59)/// std::env::set_var("G_MESSAGES_DEBUG", "all");
[60](https://gtk-rs.org#60)/// ```
[61](https://gtk-rs.org#61)///
[62](https://gtk-rs.org#62)/// Or:
[63](https://gtk-rs.org#63)///
[64](https://gtk-rs.org#64)/// ```bash
[65](https://gtk-rs.org#65)/// $ G_MESSAGES_DEBUG=all ./binary
[66](https://gtk-rs.org#66)/// ```
[67](https://gtk-rs.org#67)///
[68](https://gtk-rs.org#68)/// ### Passing a strong reference
[69](https://gtk-rs.org#69)///
[70](https://gtk-rs.org#70)/// ```
[71](https://gtk-rs.org#71)/// use glib;
[72](https://gtk-rs.org#72)/// use glib_macros::clone;
[73](https://gtk-rs.org#73)/// use std::rc::Rc;
[74](https://gtk-rs.org#74)///
[75](https://gtk-rs.org#75)/// let v = Rc::new(1);
[76](https://gtk-rs.org#76)/// let closure = clone!(
[77](https://gtk-rs.org#77)///     #[strong] v,
[78](https://gtk-rs.org#78)///     move |x| {
[79](https://gtk-rs.org#79)///         println!("v: {}, x: {}", v, x);
[80](https://gtk-rs.org#80)///     },
[81](https://gtk-rs.org#81)/// );
[82](https://gtk-rs.org#82)///
[83](https://gtk-rs.org#83)/// closure(2);
[84](https://gtk-rs.org#84)/// ```
[85](https://gtk-rs.org#85)///
[86](https://gtk-rs.org#86)/// ### Passing a weak reference
[87](https://gtk-rs.org#87)///
[88](https://gtk-rs.org#88)/// ```
[89](https://gtk-rs.org#89)/// use glib;
[90](https://gtk-rs.org#90)/// use glib_macros::clone;
[91](https://gtk-rs.org#91)/// use std::rc::Rc;
[92](https://gtk-rs.org#92)///
[93](https://gtk-rs.org#93)/// let u = Rc::new(2);
[94](https://gtk-rs.org#94)/// let closure = clone!(
[95](https://gtk-rs.org#95)///     #[weak]
[96](https://gtk-rs.org#96)///     u,
[97](https://gtk-rs.org#97)///     move |x| {
[98](https://gtk-rs.org#98)///         println!("u: {}, x: {}", u, x);
[99](https://gtk-rs.org#99)///     },
[100](https://gtk-rs.org#100)/// );
[101](https://gtk-rs.org#101)///
[102](https://gtk-rs.org#102)/// closure(3);
[103](https://gtk-rs.org#103)/// ```
[104](https://gtk-rs.org#104)///
[105](https://gtk-rs.org#105)/// #### Allowing a nullable weak reference
[106](https://gtk-rs.org#106)///
[107](https://gtk-rs.org#107)/// In some cases, even if the weak references can't be retrieved, you might want to still have
[108](https://gtk-rs.org#108)/// your closure called. In this case, you need to use `#[weak_allow_none]` instead of `#[weak]`:
[109](https://gtk-rs.org#109)///
[110](https://gtk-rs.org#110)/// ```
[111](https://gtk-rs.org#111)/// use glib;
[112](https://gtk-rs.org#112)/// use glib_macros::clone;
[113](https://gtk-rs.org#113)/// use std::rc::Rc;
[114](https://gtk-rs.org#114)///
[115](https://gtk-rs.org#115)/// let closure = {
[116](https://gtk-rs.org#116)///     // This `Rc` won't be available in the closure because it's dropped at the end of the
[117](https://gtk-rs.org#117)///     // current block
[118](https://gtk-rs.org#118)///     let u = Rc::new(2);
[119](https://gtk-rs.org#119)///     clone!(
[120](https://gtk-rs.org#120)///         #[weak_allow_none]
[121](https://gtk-rs.org#121)///         u,
[122](https://gtk-rs.org#122)///         move |x| {
[123](https://gtk-rs.org#123)///             // We need to use a Debug print for `u` because it'll be an `Option`.
[124](https://gtk-rs.org#124)///             println!("u: {:?}, x: {}", u, x);
[125](https://gtk-rs.org#125)///             true
[126](https://gtk-rs.org#126)///         },
[127](https://gtk-rs.org#127)///     )
[128](https://gtk-rs.org#128)/// };
[129](https://gtk-rs.org#129)///
[130](https://gtk-rs.org#130)/// assert_eq!(closure(3), true);
[131](https://gtk-rs.org#131)/// ```
[132](https://gtk-rs.org#132)///
[133](https://gtk-rs.org#133)/// ### Creating owned values from references (`ToOwned`)
[134](https://gtk-rs.org#134)///
[135](https://gtk-rs.org#135)/// ```
[136](https://gtk-rs.org#136)/// use glib;
[137](https://gtk-rs.org#137)/// use glib_macros::clone;
[138](https://gtk-rs.org#138)///
[139](https://gtk-rs.org#139)/// let v = "123";
[140](https://gtk-rs.org#140)/// let closure = clone!(
[141](https://gtk-rs.org#141)///     #[to_owned] v,
[142](https://gtk-rs.org#142)///     move |x| {
[143](https://gtk-rs.org#143)///         // v is passed as `String` here
[144](https://gtk-rs.org#144)///         println!("v: {}, x: {}", v, x);
[145](https://gtk-rs.org#145)///     },
[146](https://gtk-rs.org#146)/// );
[147](https://gtk-rs.org#147)///
[148](https://gtk-rs.org#148)/// closure(2);
[149](https://gtk-rs.org#149)/// ```
[150](https://gtk-rs.org#150)///
[151](https://gtk-rs.org#151)/// ### Renaming variables
[152](https://gtk-rs.org#152)///
[153](https://gtk-rs.org#153)/// ```
[154](https://gtk-rs.org#154)/// use glib;
[155](https://gtk-rs.org#155)/// use glib_macros::clone;
[156](https://gtk-rs.org#156)/// use std::rc::Rc;
[157](https://gtk-rs.org#157)///
[158](https://gtk-rs.org#158)/// let v = Rc::new(1);
[159](https://gtk-rs.org#159)/// let u = Rc::new(2);
[160](https://gtk-rs.org#160)/// let closure = clone!(
[161](https://gtk-rs.org#161)///     #[strong(rename_to = y)]
[162](https://gtk-rs.org#162)///     v,
[163](https://gtk-rs.org#163)///     #[weak] u,
[164](https://gtk-rs.org#164)///     move |x| {
[165](https://gtk-rs.org#165)///         println!("v as y: {}, u: {}, x: {}", y, u, x);
[166](https://gtk-rs.org#166)///     },
[167](https://gtk-rs.org#167)/// );
[168](https://gtk-rs.org#168)///
[169](https://gtk-rs.org#169)/// closure(3);
[170](https://gtk-rs.org#170)/// ```
[171](https://gtk-rs.org#171)///
[172](https://gtk-rs.org#172)/// ### Providing a return value if upgrading a weak reference fails
[173](https://gtk-rs.org#173)///
[174](https://gtk-rs.org#174)/// By default, `()` is returned if upgrading a weak reference fails. This behaviour can be
[175](https://gtk-rs.org#175)/// adjusted in two different ways:
[176](https://gtk-rs.org#176)///
[177](https://gtk-rs.org#177)/// Either by providing the value yourself using one of
[178](https://gtk-rs.org#178)///
[179](https://gtk-rs.org#179)///   * `#[upgrade_or]`: Requires an expression that returns a `Copy` value of the expected return type,
[180](https://gtk-rs.org#180)///   * `#[upgrade_or_else]`: Requires a closure that returns a value of the expected return type,
[181](https://gtk-rs.org#181)///   * `#[upgrade_or_default]`: Requires that the return type implements `Default` and returns that.
[182](https://gtk-rs.org#182)///
[183](https://gtk-rs.org#183)/// ```
[184](https://gtk-rs.org#184)/// use glib;
[185](https://gtk-rs.org#185)/// use glib_macros::clone;
[186](https://gtk-rs.org#186)/// use std::rc::Rc;
[187](https://gtk-rs.org#187)///
[188](https://gtk-rs.org#188)/// let v = Rc::new(1);
[189](https://gtk-rs.org#189)/// let closure = clone!(
[190](https://gtk-rs.org#190)///     #[weak] v,
[191](https://gtk-rs.org#191)///     #[upgrade_or]
[192](https://gtk-rs.org#192)///     false,
[193](https://gtk-rs.org#193)///     move |x| {
[194](https://gtk-rs.org#194)///         println!("v: {}, x: {}", v, x);
[195](https://gtk-rs.org#195)///         true
[196](https://gtk-rs.org#196)///     },
[197](https://gtk-rs.org#197)/// );
[198](https://gtk-rs.org#198)///
[199](https://gtk-rs.org#199)/// // Drop value so that the weak reference can't be upgraded.
[200](https://gtk-rs.org#200)/// drop(v);
[201](https://gtk-rs.org#201)///
[202](https://gtk-rs.org#202)/// assert_eq!(closure(2), false);
[203](https://gtk-rs.org#203)/// ```
[204](https://gtk-rs.org#204)///
[205](https://gtk-rs.org#205)/// Or by using `#[upgrade_or_panic]`: If the value fails to get upgraded, it'll panic.
[206](https://gtk-rs.org#206)///
[207](https://gtk-rs.org#207)/// ```should_panic
[208](https://gtk-rs.org#208)/// # use glib;
[209](https://gtk-rs.org#209)/// # use glib_macros::clone;
[210](https://gtk-rs.org#210)/// # use std::rc::Rc;
[211](https://gtk-rs.org#211)/// # let v = Rc::new(1);
[212](https://gtk-rs.org#212)/// let closure = clone!(
[213](https://gtk-rs.org#213)///     #[weak] v,
[214](https://gtk-rs.org#214)///     #[upgrade_or_panic]
[215](https://gtk-rs.org#215)///     move |x| {
[216](https://gtk-rs.org#216)///         println!("v: {}, x: {}", v, x);
[217](https://gtk-rs.org#217)///         true
[218](https://gtk-rs.org#218)///     },
[219](https://gtk-rs.org#219)/// );
[220](https://gtk-rs.org#220)/// # drop(v);
[221](https://gtk-rs.org#221)/// # assert_eq!(closure(2), false);
[222](https://gtk-rs.org#222)/// ```
[223](https://gtk-rs.org#223)///
[224](https://gtk-rs.org#224)/// ### Errors
[225](https://gtk-rs.org#225)///
[226](https://gtk-rs.org#226)/// Here is a list of errors you might encounter:
[227](https://gtk-rs.org#227)///
[228](https://gtk-rs.org#228)/// **Missing `#[weak]` or `#[strong]`**:
[229](https://gtk-rs.org#229)///
[230](https://gtk-rs.org#230)/// ```compile_fail
[231](https://gtk-rs.org#231)/// # use glib;
[232](https://gtk-rs.org#232)/// # use glib_macros::clone;
[233](https://gtk-rs.org#233)/// # use std::rc::Rc;
[234](https://gtk-rs.org#234)/// let v = Rc::new(1);
[235](https://gtk-rs.org#235)///
[236](https://gtk-rs.org#236)/// let closure = clone!(
[237](https://gtk-rs.org#237)///     v,
[238](https://gtk-rs.org#238)///     move |x| println!("v: {}, x: {}", v, x),
[239](https://gtk-rs.org#239)/// );
[240](https://gtk-rs.org#240)/// # drop(v);
[241](https://gtk-rs.org#241)/// # closure(2);
[242](https://gtk-rs.org#242)/// ```
[243](https://gtk-rs.org#243)///
[244](https://gtk-rs.org#244)/// **Passing `self` as an argument**:
[245](https://gtk-rs.org#245)///
[246](https://gtk-rs.org#246)/// ```compile_fail
[247](https://gtk-rs.org#247)/// # use glib;
[248](https://gtk-rs.org#248)/// # use glib_macros::clone;
[249](https://gtk-rs.org#249)/// # use std::rc::Rc;
[250](https://gtk-rs.org#250)/// #[derive(Debug)]
[251](https://gtk-rs.org#251)/// struct Foo;
[252](https://gtk-rs.org#252)///
[253](https://gtk-rs.org#253)/// impl Foo {
[254](https://gtk-rs.org#254)///     fn foo(&self) {
[255](https://gtk-rs.org#255)///         let closure = clone!(
[256](https://gtk-rs.org#256)///             #[strong] self,
[257](https://gtk-rs.org#257)///             move |x| {
[258](https://gtk-rs.org#258)///                 println!("self: {:?}", self);
[259](https://gtk-rs.org#259)///             },
[260](https://gtk-rs.org#260)///         );
[261](https://gtk-rs.org#261)///         # closure(2);
[262](https://gtk-rs.org#262)///     }
[263](https://gtk-rs.org#263)/// }
[264](https://gtk-rs.org#264)/// ```
[265](https://gtk-rs.org#265)///
[266](https://gtk-rs.org#266)/// If you want to use `self` directly, you'll need to rename it:
[267](https://gtk-rs.org#267)///
[268](https://gtk-rs.org#268)/// ```
[269](https://gtk-rs.org#269)/// # use glib;
[270](https://gtk-rs.org#270)/// # use glib_macros::clone;
[271](https://gtk-rs.org#271)/// # use std::rc::Rc;
[272](https://gtk-rs.org#272)/// #[derive(Debug)]
[273](https://gtk-rs.org#273)/// struct Foo;
[274](https://gtk-rs.org#274)///
[275](https://gtk-rs.org#275)/// impl Foo {
[276](https://gtk-rs.org#276)///     fn foo(&self) {
[277](https://gtk-rs.org#277)///         let closure = clone!(
[278](https://gtk-rs.org#278)///             #[strong(rename_to = this)]
[279](https://gtk-rs.org#279)///             self,
[280](https://gtk-rs.org#280)///             move |x| {
[281](https://gtk-rs.org#281)///                 println!("self: {:?}", this);
[282](https://gtk-rs.org#282)///             },
[283](https://gtk-rs.org#283)///         );
[284](https://gtk-rs.org#284)///         # closure(2);
[285](https://gtk-rs.org#285)///     }
[286](https://gtk-rs.org#286)/// }
[287](https://gtk-rs.org#287)/// ```
[288](https://gtk-rs.org#288)///
[289](https://gtk-rs.org#289)/// **Passing fields directly**
[290](https://gtk-rs.org#290)///
[291](https://gtk-rs.org#291)/// ```compile_fail
[292](https://gtk-rs.org#292)/// # use glib;
[293](https://gtk-rs.org#293)/// # use glib_macros::clone;
[294](https://gtk-rs.org#294)/// # use std::rc::Rc;
[295](https://gtk-rs.org#295)/// #[derive(Debug)]
[296](https://gtk-rs.org#296)/// struct Foo {
[297](https://gtk-rs.org#297)///     v: Rc<usize>,
[298](https://gtk-rs.org#298)/// }
[299](https://gtk-rs.org#299)///
[300](https://gtk-rs.org#300)/// impl Foo {
[301](https://gtk-rs.org#301)///     fn foo(&self) {
[302](https://gtk-rs.org#302)///         let closure = clone!(
[303](https://gtk-rs.org#303)///             #[strong] self.v,
[304](https://gtk-rs.org#304)///             move |x| {
[305](https://gtk-rs.org#305)///                 println!("self.v: {:?}", v);
[306](https://gtk-rs.org#306)///             },
[307](https://gtk-rs.org#307)///         );
[308](https://gtk-rs.org#308)///         # closure(2);
[309](https://gtk-rs.org#309)///     }
[310](https://gtk-rs.org#310)/// }
[311](https://gtk-rs.org#311)/// ```
[312](https://gtk-rs.org#312)///
[313](https://gtk-rs.org#313)/// You can do it by renaming it:
[314](https://gtk-rs.org#314)///
[315](https://gtk-rs.org#315)/// ```
[316](https://gtk-rs.org#316)/// # use glib;
[317](https://gtk-rs.org#317)/// # use glib_macros::clone;
[318](https://gtk-rs.org#318)/// # use std::rc::Rc;
[319](https://gtk-rs.org#319)/// # struct Foo {
[320](https://gtk-rs.org#320)/// #     v: Rc<usize>,
[321](https://gtk-rs.org#321)/// # }
[322](https://gtk-rs.org#322)/// impl Foo {
[323](https://gtk-rs.org#323)///     fn foo(&self) {
[324](https://gtk-rs.org#324)///         let closure = clone!(
[325](https://gtk-rs.org#325)///             #[strong(rename_to = v)]
[326](https://gtk-rs.org#326)///             self.v,
[327](https://gtk-rs.org#327)///             move |x| {
[328](https://gtk-rs.org#328)///                 println!("self.v: {}", v);
[329](https://gtk-rs.org#329)///             },
[330](https://gtk-rs.org#330)///         );
[331](https://gtk-rs.org#331)///         # closure(2);
[332](https://gtk-rs.org#332)///     }
[333](https://gtk-rs.org#333)/// }
[334](https://gtk-rs.org#334)/// ```
[335](https://gtk-rs.org#335)#[proc_macro]
[336](https://gtk-rs.org#336)pub fn [clone](https://gtk-rs.org/glib_macros/macro.clone.html)(item: [TokenStream](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/proc_macro/struct.TokenStream.html)) -> [TokenStream](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/proc_macro/struct.TokenStream.html) {
[337](https://gtk-rs.org#337)    clone::[clone_inner](https://gtk-rs.org/clone.rs.html#565-568)([item](https://gtk-rs.org#336))
[338](https://gtk-rs.org#338)}
[339](https://gtk-rs.org#339)
[340](https://gtk-rs.org#340)/// Macro for creating a [`Closure`] object. This is a wrapper around [`Closure::new`] that
[341](https://gtk-rs.org#341)/// automatically type checks its arguments at run-time.
[342](https://gtk-rs.org#342)///
[343](https://gtk-rs.org#343)/// A `Closure` takes [`Value`] objects as inputs and output. This macro will automatically convert
[344](https://gtk-rs.org#344)/// the inputs to Rust types when invoking its callback, and then will convert the output back to a
[345](https://gtk-rs.org#345)/// `Value`. All inputs must implement the [`FromValue`] trait, and outputs must either implement
[346](https://gtk-rs.org#346)/// the [`ToValue`] trait or be the unit type `()`. Type-checking of inputs is done at run-time; if
[347](https://gtk-rs.org#347)/// incorrect types are passed via [`Closure::invoke`] then the closure will panic. Note that when
[348](https://gtk-rs.org#348)/// passing input types derived from [`Object`] or [`Interface`], you must take care to upcast to
[349](https://gtk-rs.org#349)/// the exact object or interface type that is being received.
[350](https://gtk-rs.org#350)///
[351](https://gtk-rs.org#351)/// Similarly to [`clone!`](crate::clone!), this macro can be useful in combination with signal
[352](https://gtk-rs.org#352)/// handlers to reduce boilerplate when passing references. Unique to `Closure` objects is the
[353](https://gtk-rs.org#353)/// ability to watch an object using the `#[watch]` attribute. Only an [`Object`] value can be
[354](https://gtk-rs.org#354)/// passed to `#[watch]`, and only one object can be watched per closure. When an object is watched,
[355](https://gtk-rs.org#355)/// a weak reference to the object is held in the closure. When the object is destroyed, the
[356](https://gtk-rs.org#356)/// closure will become invalidated: all signal handlers connected to the closure will become
[357](https://gtk-rs.org#357)/// disconnected, and any calls to [`Closure::invoke`] on the closure will be silently ignored.
[358](https://gtk-rs.org#358)/// Internally, this is accomplished using [`Object::watch_closure`] on the watched object.
[359](https://gtk-rs.org#359)///
[360](https://gtk-rs.org#360)/// The `#[weak]`, `#[weak_allow_none]`, `#[strong]`, `#[to_owned]` captures are also supported and
[361](https://gtk-rs.org#361)/// behave the same as in [`clone!`](crate::clone!), as is aliasing captures via `rename_to`.
[362](https://gtk-rs.org#362)/// Similarly, upgrade failure of weak references can be adjusted via `#[upgrade_or]`,
[363](https://gtk-rs.org#363)/// `#[upgrade_or_else]`, `#[upgrade_or_default]` and `#[upgrade_or_panic]`.
[364](https://gtk-rs.org#364)///
[365](https://gtk-rs.org#365)/// Notably, these captures are able to reference `Rc` and `Arc` values in addition to `Object`
[366](https://gtk-rs.org#366)/// values.
[367](https://gtk-rs.org#367)///
[368](https://gtk-rs.org#368)/// [`Closure`]: ../glib/closure/struct.Closure.html
[369](https://gtk-rs.org#369)/// [`Closure::new`]: ../glib/closure/struct.Closure.html#method.new
[370](https://gtk-rs.org#370)/// [`Closure::new_local`]: ../glib/closure/struct.Closure.html#method.new_local
[371](https://gtk-rs.org#371)/// [`Closure::invoke`]: ../glib/closure/struct.Closure.html#method.invoke
[372](https://gtk-rs.org#372)/// [`Value`]: ../glib/value/struct.Value.html
[373](https://gtk-rs.org#373)/// [`FromValue`]: ../glib/value/trait.FromValue.html
[374](https://gtk-rs.org#374)/// [`ToValue`]: ../glib/value/trait.ToValue.html
[375](https://gtk-rs.org#375)/// [`Interface`]: ../glib/object/struct.Interface.html
[376](https://gtk-rs.org#376)/// [`Object`]: ../glib/object/struct.Object.html
[377](https://gtk-rs.org#377)/// [`Object::watch_closure`]: ../glib/object/trait.ObjectExt.html#tymethod.watch_closure
[378](https://gtk-rs.org#378)/// **⚠️ IMPORTANT ⚠️**
[379](https://gtk-rs.org#379)///
[380](https://gtk-rs.org#380)/// `glib` needs to be in scope, so unless it's one of the direct crate dependencies, you need to
[381](https://gtk-rs.org#381)/// import it because `closure!` is using it. For example:
[382](https://gtk-rs.org#382)///
[383](https://gtk-rs.org#383)/// ```rust,ignore
[384](https://gtk-rs.org#384)/// use gtk::glib;
[385](https://gtk-rs.org#385)/// ```
[386](https://gtk-rs.org#386)///
[387](https://gtk-rs.org#387)/// ### Using as a closure object
[388](https://gtk-rs.org#388)///
[389](https://gtk-rs.org#389)/// ```
[390](https://gtk-rs.org#390)/// use glib_macros::closure;
[391](https://gtk-rs.org#391)///
[392](https://gtk-rs.org#392)/// let concat_str = closure!(|s: &str| s.to_owned() + " World");
[393](https://gtk-rs.org#393)/// let result = concat_str.invoke::<String>(&[&"Hello"]);
[394](https://gtk-rs.org#394)/// assert_eq!(result, "Hello World");
[395](https://gtk-rs.org#395)/// ```
[396](https://gtk-rs.org#396)///
[397](https://gtk-rs.org#397)/// ### Connecting to a signal
[398](https://gtk-rs.org#398)///
[399](https://gtk-rs.org#399)/// For wrapping closures that can't be sent across threads, the
[400](https://gtk-rs.org#400)/// [`closure_local!`](crate::closure_local!) macro can be used. It has the same syntax as
[401](https://gtk-rs.org#401)/// `closure!`, but instead uses [`Closure::new_local`] internally.
[402](https://gtk-rs.org#402)///
[403](https://gtk-rs.org#403)/// ```
[404](https://gtk-rs.org#404)/// use glib;
[405](https://gtk-rs.org#405)/// use glib::prelude::*;
[406](https://gtk-rs.org#406)/// use glib_macros::closure_local;
[407](https://gtk-rs.org#407)///
[408](https://gtk-rs.org#408)/// let obj = glib::Object::new::<glib::Object>();
[409](https://gtk-rs.org#409)/// obj.connect_closure(
[410](https://gtk-rs.org#410)///     "notify", false,
[411](https://gtk-rs.org#411)///     closure_local!(|_obj: glib::Object, pspec: glib::ParamSpec| {
[412](https://gtk-rs.org#412)///         println!("property notify: {}", pspec.name());
[413](https://gtk-rs.org#413)///     }));
[414](https://gtk-rs.org#414)/// ```
[415](https://gtk-rs.org#415)///
[416](https://gtk-rs.org#416)/// ### Object Watching
[417](https://gtk-rs.org#417)///
[418](https://gtk-rs.org#418)/// ```
[419](https://gtk-rs.org#419)/// use glib;
[420](https://gtk-rs.org#420)/// use glib::prelude::*;
[421](https://gtk-rs.org#421)/// use glib_macros::closure_local;
[422](https://gtk-rs.org#422)///
[423](https://gtk-rs.org#423)/// let closure = {
[424](https://gtk-rs.org#424)///     let obj = glib::Object::new::<glib::Object>();
[425](https://gtk-rs.org#425)///     let closure = closure_local!(
[426](https://gtk-rs.org#426)///         #[watch] obj,
[427](https://gtk-rs.org#427)///         move || {
[428](https://gtk-rs.org#428)///             obj.type_().name()
[429](https://gtk-rs.org#429)///         },
[430](https://gtk-rs.org#430)///     );
[431](https://gtk-rs.org#431)///     assert_eq!(closure.invoke::<String>(&[]), "GObject");
[432](https://gtk-rs.org#432)///     closure
[433](https://gtk-rs.org#433)/// };
[434](https://gtk-rs.org#434)/// // `obj` is dropped, closure invalidated so it always does nothing and returns None
[435](https://gtk-rs.org#435)/// closure.invoke::<()>(&[]);
[436](https://gtk-rs.org#436)/// ```
[437](https://gtk-rs.org#437)///
[438](https://gtk-rs.org#438)/// `#[watch]` has special behavior when connected to a signal:
[439](https://gtk-rs.org#439)///
[440](https://gtk-rs.org#440)/// ```
[441](https://gtk-rs.org#441)/// use glib;
[442](https://gtk-rs.org#442)/// use glib::prelude::*;
[443](https://gtk-rs.org#443)/// use glib_macros::closure_local;
[444](https://gtk-rs.org#444)///
[445](https://gtk-rs.org#445)/// let obj = glib::Object::new::<glib::Object>();
[446](https://gtk-rs.org#446)/// {
[447](https://gtk-rs.org#447)///     let other = glib::Object::new::<glib::Object>();
[448](https://gtk-rs.org#448)///     obj.connect_closure(
[449](https://gtk-rs.org#449)///         "notify", false,
[450](https://gtk-rs.org#450)///         closure_local!(
[451](https://gtk-rs.org#451)///             #[watch(rename_to = b)]
[452](https://gtk-rs.org#452)///             other,
[453](https://gtk-rs.org#453)///             move |a: glib::Object, pspec: glib::ParamSpec| {
[454](https://gtk-rs.org#454)///                 let value = a.property_value(pspec.name());
[455](https://gtk-rs.org#455)///                 b.set_property(pspec.name(), &value);
[456](https://gtk-rs.org#456)///             },
[457](https://gtk-rs.org#457)///         ),
[458](https://gtk-rs.org#458)///     );
[459](https://gtk-rs.org#459)///     // The signal handler will disconnect automatically at the end of this
[460](https://gtk-rs.org#460)///     // block when `other` is dropped.
[461](https://gtk-rs.org#461)/// }
[462](https://gtk-rs.org#462)/// ```
[463](https://gtk-rs.org#463)///
[464](https://gtk-rs.org#464)/// ### Weak and Strong References
[465](https://gtk-rs.org#465)///
[466](https://gtk-rs.org#466)/// ```
[467](https://gtk-rs.org#467)/// use glib;
[468](https://gtk-rs.org#468)/// use glib::prelude::*;
[469](https://gtk-rs.org#469)/// use glib_macros::closure;
[470](https://gtk-rs.org#470)/// use std::sync::Arc;
[471](https://gtk-rs.org#471)///
[472](https://gtk-rs.org#472)/// let closure = {
[473](https://gtk-rs.org#473)///     let a = Arc::new(String::from("Hello"));
[474](https://gtk-rs.org#474)///     let b = Arc::new(String::from("World"));
[475](https://gtk-rs.org#475)///     let c = "!";
[476](https://gtk-rs.org#476)///     let closure = closure!(
[477](https://gtk-rs.org#477)///         #[strong] a,
[478](https://gtk-rs.org#478)///         #[weak_allow_none]
[479](https://gtk-rs.org#479)///         b,
[480](https://gtk-rs.org#480)///         #[to_owned]
[481](https://gtk-rs.org#481)///         c,
[482](https://gtk-rs.org#482)///         move || {
[483](https://gtk-rs.org#483)///             // `a` is Arc<String>, `b` is Option<Arc<String>>, `c` is a `String`
[484](https://gtk-rs.org#484)///             format!("{} {}{}", a, b.as_ref().map(|b| b.as_str()).unwrap_or_else(|| "Moon"), c)
[485](https://gtk-rs.org#485)///         },
[486](https://gtk-rs.org#486)///     );
[487](https://gtk-rs.org#487)///     assert_eq!(closure.invoke::<String>(&[]), "Hello World!");
[488](https://gtk-rs.org#488)///     closure
[489](https://gtk-rs.org#489)/// };
[490](https://gtk-rs.org#490)/// // `a`, `c` still kept alive, `b` is dropped
[491](https://gtk-rs.org#491)/// assert_eq!(closure.invoke::<String>(&[]), "Hello Moon!");
[492](https://gtk-rs.org#492)/// ```
[493](https://gtk-rs.org#493)#[proc_macro]
[494](https://gtk-rs.org#494)pub fn [closure](https://gtk-rs.org/glib_macros/macro.closure.html)(item: [TokenStream](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/proc_macro/struct.TokenStream.html)) -> [TokenStream](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/proc_macro/struct.TokenStream.html) {
[495](https://gtk-rs.org#495)    closure::[closure_inner](https://gtk-rs.org/closure.rs.html#249-256)([item](https://gtk-rs.org#494), "new")
[496](https://gtk-rs.org#496)}

[498](https://gtk-rs.org#498)/// The same as [`closure!`](crate::closure!) but uses [`Closure::new_local`] as a constructor.
[499](https://gtk-rs.org#499)/// This is useful for closures which can't be sent across threads. See the documentation of
[500](https://gtk-rs.org#500)/// [`closure!`](crate::closure!) for details.
[501](https://gtk-rs.org#501)///
[502](https://gtk-rs.org#502)/// [`Closure::new_local`]: ../glib/closure/struct.Closure.html#method.new_local

[506](https://gtk-rs.org#506)}
[507](https://gtk-rs.org#507)
[508](https://gtk-rs.org#508)/// Derive macro to register a Rust enum in the GLib type system and derive the
[509](https://gtk-rs.org#509)/// [`glib::Value`] traits.
[510](https://gtk-rs.org#510)///
[511](https://gtk-rs.org#511)/// # Example
[512](https://gtk-rs.org#512)///
[513](https://gtk-rs.org#513)/// ```
[514](https://gtk-rs.org#514)/// use glib::prelude::*;
[515](https://gtk-rs.org#515)/// use glib::subclass::prelude::*;
[516](https://gtk-rs.org#516)///
[517](https://gtk-rs.org#517)/// #[derive(Debug, Copy, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, glib::Enum)]
[518](https://gtk-rs.org#518)/// #[enum_type(name = "MyEnum")]
[519](https://gtk-rs.org#519)/// enum MyEnum {
[520](https://gtk-rs.org#520)///     Val,
[521](https://gtk-rs.org#521)///     #[enum_value(name = "My Val")]
[522](https://gtk-rs.org#522)///     ValWithCustomName,
[523](https://gtk-rs.org#523)///     #[enum_value(name = "My Other Val", nick = "other")]
[524](https://gtk-rs.org#524)///     ValWithCustomNameAndNick,
[525](https://gtk-rs.org#525)/// }
[526](https://gtk-rs.org#526)/// ```
[527](https://gtk-rs.org#527)///
[528](https://gtk-rs.org#528)/// When using the [`Properties`] macro with enums that derive [`Enum`], the
[529](https://gtk-rs.org#529)/// default value can be explicitly set via the `builder` parameter of the
[530](https://gtk-rs.org#530)/// `#[property]` attribute. If the enum implements or derives
[531](https://gtk-rs.org#531)/// `Default`, you can specify that should be the default value
[532](https://gtk-rs.org#532)/// via the `default` parameter. See [here](Properties#supported-types) for
[533](https://gtk-rs.org#533)/// details.
[534](https://gtk-rs.org#534)///
[535](https://gtk-rs.org#535)/// An enum can be registered as a dynamic type by setting the derive macro
[536](https://gtk-rs.org#536)/// helper attribute `enum_dynamic`:
[537](https://gtk-rs.org#537)///
[538](https://gtk-rs.org#538)/// ```ignore
[539](https://gtk-rs.org#539)/// use glib::prelude::*;
[540](https://gtk-rs.org#540)/// use glib::subclass::prelude::*;
[541](https://gtk-rs.org#541)///
[542](https://gtk-rs.org#542)/// #[derive(Debug, Copy, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, glib::Enum)]
[543](https://gtk-rs.org#543)/// #[enum_type(name = "MyEnum")]
[544](https://gtk-rs.org#544)/// #[enum_dynamic]
[545](https://gtk-rs.org#545)/// enum MyEnum {
[546](https://gtk-rs.org#546)///     ...
[547](https://gtk-rs.org#547)/// }
[548](https://gtk-rs.org#548)/// ```
[549](https://gtk-rs.org#549)///
[550](https://gtk-rs.org#550)/// As a dynamic type, an enum must be explicitly registered when the system
[551](https://gtk-rs.org#551)/// loads the implementation (see [`TypePlugin`] and [`TypeModule`]).
[552](https://gtk-rs.org#552)/// Therefore, whereas an enum can be registered only once as a static type,
[553](https://gtk-rs.org#553)/// it can be registered several times as a dynamic type.
[554](https://gtk-rs.org#554)///
[555](https://gtk-rs.org#555)/// An enum registered as a dynamic type is never unregistered. The system
[556](https://gtk-rs.org#556)/// calls [`TypePluginExt::unuse`] to unload the implementation. If the
[557](https://gtk-rs.org#557)/// [`TypePlugin`] subclass is a [`TypeModule`], the enum registered as a
[558](https://gtk-rs.org#558)/// dynamic type is marked as unloaded and must be registered again when the
[559](https://gtk-rs.org#559)/// module is reloaded.
[560](https://gtk-rs.org#560)///
[561](https://gtk-rs.org#561)/// The derive macro helper attribute `enum_dynamic` provides two behaviors
[562](https://gtk-rs.org#562)/// when registering an enum as a dynamic type:
[563](https://gtk-rs.org#563)///
[564](https://gtk-rs.org#564)/// - lazy registration: by default an enum is registered as a dynamic type
[565](https://gtk-rs.org#565)///   when the system loads the implementation (e.g. when the module is loaded).
[566](https://gtk-rs.org#566)///   Optionally setting `lazy_registration` to `true` postpones registration on
[567](https://gtk-rs.org#567)///   the first use (when `static_type()` is called for the first time):
[568](https://gtk-rs.org#568)///
[569](https://gtk-rs.org#569)/// ```ignore
[570](https://gtk-rs.org#570)/// #[derive(Debug, Copy, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, glib::Enum)]
[571](https://gtk-rs.org#571)/// #[enum_type(name = "MyEnum")]
[572](https://gtk-rs.org#572)/// #[enum_dynamic(lazy_registration = true)]
[573](https://gtk-rs.org#573)/// enum MyEnum {
[574](https://gtk-rs.org#574)///     ...
[575](https://gtk-rs.org#575)/// }
[576](https://gtk-rs.org#576)/// ```
[577](https://gtk-rs.org#577)///
[578](https://gtk-rs.org#578)/// - registration within [`TypeModule`] subclass or within [`TypePlugin`]
[579](https://gtk-rs.org#579)///   subclass: an enum is usually registered as a dynamic type within a
[580](https://gtk-rs.org#580)///   [`TypeModule`] subclass:
[581](https://gtk-rs.org#581)///
[582](https://gtk-rs.org#582)/// ```ignore
[583](https://gtk-rs.org#583)/// #[derive(Debug, Copy, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, glib::Enum)]
[584](https://gtk-rs.org#584)/// #[enum_type(name = "MyModuleEnum")]
[585](https://gtk-rs.org#585)/// #[enum_dynamic]
[586](https://gtk-rs.org#586)/// enum MyModuleEnum {
[587](https://gtk-rs.org#587)///     ...
[588](https://gtk-rs.org#588)/// }
[589](https://gtk-rs.org#589)/// ...
[590](https://gtk-rs.org#590)/// #[derive(Default)]
[591](https://gtk-rs.org#591)/// pub struct MyModule;
[592](https://gtk-rs.org#592)/// ...
[593](https://gtk-rs.org#593)/// impl TypeModuleImpl for MyModule {
[594](https://gtk-rs.org#594)///     fn load(&self) -> bool {
[595](https://gtk-rs.org#595)///         // registers enums as dynamic types.
[596](https://gtk-rs.org#596)///         let my_module = self.obj();
[597](https://gtk-rs.org#597)///         let type_module: &glib::TypeModule = my_module.upcast_ref();
[598](https://gtk-rs.org#598)///         MyModuleEnum::on_implementation_load(type_module)
[599](https://gtk-rs.org#599)///     }
[600](https://gtk-rs.org#600)///     ...
[601](https://gtk-rs.org#601)/// }
[602](https://gtk-rs.org#602)/// ```
[603](https://gtk-rs.org#603)///
[604](https://gtk-rs.org#604)/// Optionally setting `plugin_type` allows to register an enum as a dynamic
[605](https://gtk-rs.org#605)/// type within a [`TypePlugin`] subclass that is not a [`TypeModule`]:
[606](https://gtk-rs.org#606)///
[607](https://gtk-rs.org#607)/// ```ignore
[608](https://gtk-rs.org#608)/// #[derive(Debug, Copy, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, glib::Enum)]
[609](https://gtk-rs.org#609)/// #[enum_type(name = "MyPluginEnum")]
[610](https://gtk-rs.org#610)/// #[enum_dynamic(plugin_type = MyPlugin)]
[611](https://gtk-rs.org#611)/// enum MyPluginEnum {
[612](https://gtk-rs.org#612)///     ...
[613](https://gtk-rs.org#613)/// }
[614](https://gtk-rs.org#614)/// ...
[615](https://gtk-rs.org#615)/// #[derive(Default)]
[616](https://gtk-rs.org#616)/// pub struct MyPlugin;
[617](https://gtk-rs.org#617)/// ...
[618](https://gtk-rs.org#618)/// impl TypePluginImpl for MyPlugin {
[619](https://gtk-rs.org#619)///     fn use_plugin(&self) {
[620](https://gtk-rs.org#620)///         // register enums as dynamic types.
[621](https://gtk-rs.org#621)///         let my_plugin = self.obj();
[622](https://gtk-rs.org#622)///         MyPluginEnum::on_implementation_load(my_plugin.as_ref());
[623](https://gtk-rs.org#623)///     }
[624](https://gtk-rs.org#624)///     ...
[625](https://gtk-rs.org#625)/// }
[626](https://gtk-rs.org#626)/// ```
[627](https://gtk-rs.org#627)///
[628](https://gtk-rs.org#628)/// [`glib::Value`]: ../glib/value/struct.Value.html
[629](https://gtk-rs.org#629)/// [`TypePlugin`]: ../glib/gobject/type_plugin/struct.TypePlugin.html
[630](https://gtk-rs.org#630)/// [`TypeModule`]: ../glib/gobject/type_module/struct.TypeModule.html
[631](https://gtk-rs.org#631)/// [`TypePluginExt::unuse`]: ../glib/gobject/type_plugin/trait.TypePluginExt.

[640](https://gtk-rs.org#640)/// Attribute macro for defining flags using the `bitflags` crate.
[641](https://gtk-rs.org#641)/// This macro will also define a `GFlags::type_` function and
[642](https://gtk-rs.org#642)/// the [`glib::Value`] traits.
[643](https://gtk-rs.org#643)///
[644](https://gtk-rs.org#644)/// The expected `GType` name has to be passed as macro attribute.
[645](https://gtk-rs.org#645)/// The name and nick of each flag can also be optionally defined.
[646](https://gtk-rs.org#646)/// Default name is the flag identifier in CamelCase and default nick
[647](https://gtk-rs.org#647)/// is the identifier in kebab-case.
[648](https://gtk-rs.org#648)/// Combined flags should not be registered with the `GType` system
[649](https://gtk-rs.org#649)/// and so need to be tagged with the `#[flags_value(skip)]` attribute.
[650](https://gtk-rs.org#650)///
[651](https://gtk-rs.org#651)/// # Example
[652](https://gtk-rs.org#652)///
[653](https://gtk-rs.org#653)/// ```
[654](https://gtk-rs.org#654)/// use glib::prelude::*;
[655](https://gtk-rs.org#655)/// use glib::subclass::prelude::*;
[656](https://gtk-rs.org#656)///
[657](https://gtk-rs.org#657)/// #[glib::flags(name = "MyFlags")]
[658](https://gtk-rs.org#658)/// enum MyFlags {
[659](https://gtk-rs.org#659)///     #[flags_value(name = "Flag A", nick = "nick-a")]
[660](https://gtk-rs.org#660)///     A = 0b00000001,
[661](https://gtk-rs.org#661)///     #[flags_value(name = "Flag B")]
[662](https://gtk-rs.org#662)///     B = 0b00000010,
[663](https://gtk-rs.org#663)///     #[flags_value(skip)]
[664](https://gtk-rs.org#664)///     AB = Self::A.bits() | Self::B.bits(),
[665](https://gtk-rs.org#665)///     C = 0b00000100,
[666](https://gtk-rs.org#666)/// }
[667](https://gtk-rs.org#667)/// ```
[668](https://gtk-rs.org#668)///
[669](https://gtk-rs.org#669)/// The flags can be registered as a dynamic type by setting the macro helper
[670](https://gtk-rs.org#670)/// attribute `flags_dynamic`:
[671](https://gtk-rs.org#671)/// ```ignore
[672](https://gtk-rs.org#672)/// use glib::prelude::*;
[673](https://gtk-rs.org#673)/// use glib::subclass::prelude::*;
[674](https://gtk-rs.org#674)///
[675](https://gtk-rs.org#675)/// #[glib::flags(name = "MyFlags")]
[676](https://gtk-rs.org#676)/// #[flags_dynamic]
[677](https://gtk-rs.org#677)/// enum MyFlags {
[678](https://gtk-rs.org#678)///     ...
[679](https://gtk-rs.org#679)/// }
[680](https://gtk-rs.org#680)/// ```
[681](https://gtk-rs.org#681)///
[682](https://gtk-rs.org#682)/// As a dynamic type, the flags must be explicitly registered when the system
[683](https://gtk-rs.org#683)/// loads the implementation (see [`TypePlugin`] and [`TypeModule`]).
[684](https://gtk-rs.org#684)/// Therefore, whereas the flags can be registered only once as a static type,
[685](https://gtk-rs.org#685)/// they can be registered several times as a dynamic type.
[686](https://gtk-rs.org#686)///
[687](https://gtk-rs.org#687)/// The flags registered as a dynamic type are never unregistered. The system
[688](https://gtk-rs.org#688)/// calls [`TypePluginExt::unuse`] to unload the implementation. If the
[689](https://gtk-rs.org#689)/// [`TypePlugin`] subclass is a [`TypeModule`], the flags registered as a
[690](https://gtk-rs.org#690)/// dynamic type are marked as unloaded and must be registered again when the
[691](https://gtk-rs.org#691)/// module is reloaded.
[692](https://gtk-rs.org#692)///
[693](https://gtk-rs.org#693)/// The macro helper attribute `flags_dynamic` provides two behaviors when
[694](https://gtk-rs.org#694)/// registering the flags as a dynamic type:
[695](https://gtk-rs.org#695)///
[696](https://gtk-rs.org#696)/// - lazy registration: by default the flags are registered as a dynamic type
[697](https://gtk-rs.org#697)///   when the system loads the implementation (e.g. when the module is loaded).
[698](https://gtk-rs.org#698)///   Optionally setting `lazy_registration` to `true` postpones registration on
[699](https://gtk-rs.org#699)///   the first use (when `static_type()` is called for the first time):
[700](https://gtk-rs.org#700)///
[701](https://gtk-rs.org#701)/// ```ignore
[702](https://gtk-rs.org#702)/// #[glib::flags(name = "MyFlags")]
[703](https://gtk-rs.org#703)/// #[flags_dynamic(lazy_registration = true)]
[704](https://gtk-rs.org#704)/// enum MyFlags {
[705](https://gtk-rs.org#705)///     ...
[706](https://gtk-rs.org#706)/// }
[707](https://gtk-rs.org#707)/// ```
[708](https://gtk-rs.org#708)///
[709](https://gtk-rs.org#709)/// - registration within [`TypeModule`] subclass or within [`TypePlugin`]
[710](https://gtk-rs.org#710)///   subclass: the flags are usually registered as a dynamic type within a
[711](https://gtk-rs.org#711)///   [`TypeModule`] subclass:
[712](https://gtk-rs.org#712)///
[713](https://gtk-rs.org#713)/// ```ignore
[714](https://gtk-rs.org#714)/// #[glib::flags(name = "MyModuleFlags")]
[715](https://gtk-rs.org#715)/// #[flags_dynamic]
[716](https://gtk-rs.org#716)/// enum MyModuleFlags {
[717](https://gtk-rs.org#717)///     ...
[718](https://gtk-rs.org#718)/// }
[719](https://gtk-rs.org#719)/// ...
[720](https://gtk-rs.org#720)/// #[derive(Default)]
[721](https://gtk-rs.org#721)/// pub struct MyModule;
[722](https://gtk-rs.org#722)/// ...
[723](https://gtk-rs.org#723)/// impl TypeModuleImpl for MyModule {
[724](https://gtk-rs.org#724)///     fn load(&self) -> bool {
[725](https://gtk-rs.org#725)///         // registers flags as dynamic types.
[726](https://gtk-rs.org#726)///         let my_module = self.obj();
[727](https://gtk-rs.org#727)///         let type_module: &glib::TypeModule = my_module.upcast_ref();
[728](https://gtk-rs.org#728)///         MyModuleFlags::on_implementation_load(type_module)
[729](https://gtk-rs.org#729)///     }
[730](https://gtk-rs.org#730)///     ...
[731](https://gtk-rs.org#731)/// }
[732](https://gtk-rs.org#732)/// ```
[733](https://gtk-rs.org#733)///
[734](https://gtk-rs.org#734)/// Optionally setting `plugin_type` allows to register the flags as a dynamic
[735](https://gtk-rs.org#735)/// type within a [`TypePlugin`] subclass that is not a [`TypeModule`]:
[736](https://gtk-rs.org#736)/// ```ignore
[737](https://gtk-rs.org#737)/// #[glib::flags(name = "MyModuleFlags")]
[738](https://gtk-rs.org#738)/// #[flags_dynamic(plugin_type = MyPlugin)]
[739](https://gtk-rs.org#739)/// enum MyModuleFlags {
[740](https://gtk-rs.org#740)///     ...
[741](https://gtk-rs.org#741)/// }
[742](https://gtk-rs.org#742)/// ...
[743](https://gtk-rs.org#743)/// #[derive(Default)]
[744](https://gtk-rs.org#744)/// pub struct MyPlugin;
[745](https://gtk-rs.org#745)/// ...
[746](https://gtk-rs.org#746)/// impl TypePluginImpl for MyPlugin {
[747](https://gtk-rs.org#747)///     fn use_plugin(&self) {
[748](https://gtk-rs.org#748)///         // register flags as dynamic types.
[749](https://gtk-rs.org#749)///         let my_plugin = self.obj();
[750](https://gtk-rs.org#750)///         MyPluginFlags::on_implementation_load(my_plugin.as_ref());
[751](https://gtk-rs.org#751)///     }
[752](https://gtk-rs.org#752)///     ...
[753](https://gtk-rs.org#753)/// }
[754](https://gtk-rs.org#754)/// ```
[755](https://gtk-rs.org#755)///
[756](https://gtk-rs.org#756)/// [`glib::Value`]: ../glib/value/struct.Value.html
[757](https://gtk-rs.org#757)/// [`TypePlugin`]: ../glib/gobject/type_plugin/struct.TypePlugin.html
[758](https://gtk-rs.org#758)/// [`TypeModule`]: ../glib/gobject/type_module/struct.TypeModule.html
[759](https://gtk-rs.org#759)/// [`TypePluginExt::unuse`]: ../glib/gobject/type_plugin/trait.TypePluginExt.

[819](https://gtk-rs.org#819)/// Derive macro for defining a [`BoxedType`]`::type_` function and
[820](https://gtk-rs.org#820)/// the [`glib::Value`] traits. Optionally, the type can be marked as
[821](https://gtk-rs.org#821)/// `nullable` to get an implementation of `glib::value::ToValueOptional`.
[822](https://gtk-rs.org#822)///
[823](https://gtk-rs.org#823)/// # Example
[824](https://gtk-rs.org#824)///
[825](https://gtk-rs.org#825)/// ```
[826](https://gtk-rs.org#826)/// use glib::prelude::*;
[827](https://gtk-rs.org#827)/// use glib::subclass::prelude::*;
[828](https://gtk-rs.org#828)///
[829](https://gtk-rs.org#829)/// #[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, glib::Boxed)]
[830](https://gtk-rs.org#830)/// #[boxed_type(name = "MyBoxed")]
[831](https://gtk-rs.org#831)/// struct MyBoxed(String);
[832](https://gtk-rs.org#832)///
[833](https://gtk-rs.org#833)/// #[derive(Clone, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, glib::Boxed)]
[834](https://gtk-rs.org#834)/// #[boxed_type(name = "MyNullableBoxed", nullable)]
[835](https://gtk-rs.org#835)/// struct MyNullableBoxed(String);
[836](https://gtk-rs.org#836)/// ```
[837](https://gtk-rs.org#837)///
[838](https://gtk-rs.org#838)/// [`BoxedType`]: ../glib/subclass/boxed/trait.BoxedType.html

[853](https://gtk-rs.org#853)///

[866](https://gtk-rs.org#866)///

[868](https://gtk-rs.org#868)/// #[shared_boxed_type(name = "MyNullableSharedBoxed", nullable)]

[870](https://gtk-rs.org#870)/// ```

[882](https://gtk-rs.org#882)/// Macro for boilerplate of [`ObjectSubclass`] implementations.
[883](https://gtk-rs.org#883)///
[884](https://gtk-rs.org#884)/// This adds implementations for the `type_data()` and `type_()` methods,
[885](https://gtk-rs.org#885)/// which should probably never be defined differently.
[886](https://gtk-rs.org#886)///
[887](https://gtk-rs.org#887)/// It provides default values for the `Instance`, `Class`, and `Interfaces`
[888](https://gtk-rs.org#888)/// type parameters. If these are present, the macro will use the provided value
[889](https://gtk-rs.org#889)/// instead of the default.
[890](https://gtk-rs.org#890)///
[891](https://gtk-rs.org#891)/// Usually the defaults for `Instance` and `Class` will work. `Interfaces` is
[892](https://gtk-rs.org#892)/// necessary for types that implement interfaces.
[893](https://gtk-rs.org#893)///
[894](https://gtk-rs.org#894)/// ```ignore
[895](https://gtk-rs.org#895)/// type Instance = glib::subclass::basic::InstanceStruct<Self>;
[896](https://gtk-rs.org#896)/// type Class = glib::subclass::basic::ClassStruct<Self>;
[897](https://gtk-rs.org#897)/// type Interfaces = ();
[898](https://gtk-rs.org#898)/// ```
[899](https://gtk-rs.org#899)///
[900](https://gtk-rs.org#900)/// If no `new()` or `with_class()` method is provided, the macro adds a `new()`
[901](https://gtk-rs.org#901)/// implementation calling `Default::default()`. So the type needs to implement
[902](https://gtk-rs.org#902)/// `Default`, or this should be overridden.
[903](https://gtk-rs.org#903)///
[904](https://gtk-rs.org#904)/// ```ignore
[905](https://gtk-rs.org#905)/// fn new() -> Self {
[906](https://gtk-rs.org#906)///     Default::default()
[907](https://gtk-rs.org#907)/// }
[908](https://gtk-rs.org#908)/// ```
[909](https://gtk-rs.org#909)///
[910](https://gtk-rs.org#910)/// An object subclass can be registered as a dynamic type by setting the macro
[911](https://gtk-rs.org#911)/// helper attribute `object_class_dynamic`:
[912](https://gtk-rs.org#912)///
[913](https://gtk-rs.org#913)/// ```ignore
[914](https://gtk-rs.org#914)/// #[derive(Default)]
[915](https://gtk-rs.org#915)/// pub struct MyType;
[916](https://gtk-rs.org#916)///
[917](https://gtk-rs.org#917)/// #[glib::object_subclass]
[918](https://gtk-rs.org#918)/// #[object_subclass_dynamic]
[919](https://gtk-rs.org#919)/// impl ObjectSubclass for MyType { ... }
[920](https://gtk-rs.org#920)/// ```
[921](https://gtk-rs.org#921)///
[922](https://gtk-rs.org#922)/// As a dynamic type, an object subclass must be explicitly registered when
[923](https://gtk-rs.org#923)/// the system loads the implementation (see [`TypePlugin`] and [`TypeModule`]).
[924](https://gtk-rs.org#924)/// Therefore, whereas an object subclass can be registered only once as a
[925](https://gtk-rs.org#925)/// static type, it can be registered several times as a dynamic type.
[926](https://gtk-rs.org#926)///
[927](https://gtk-rs.org#927)/// An object subclass registered as a dynamic type is never unregistered. The
[928](https://gtk-rs.org#928)/// system calls [`TypePluginExt::unuse`] to unload the implementation. If the
[929](https://gtk-rs.org#929)/// [`TypePlugin`] subclass is a [`TypeModule`], the object subclass registered
[930](https://gtk-rs.org#930)/// as a dynamic type is marked as unloaded and must be registered again when
[931](https://gtk-rs.org#931)/// the module is reloaded.
[932](https://gtk-rs.org#932)///
[933](https://gtk-rs.org#933)/// The macro helper attribute `object_class_dynamic` provides two behaviors
[934](https://gtk-rs.org#934)/// when registering an object subclass as a dynamic type:
[935](https://gtk-rs.org#935)///
[936](https://gtk-rs.org#936)/// - lazy registration: by default an object subclass is registered as a
[937](https://gtk-rs.org#937)///   dynamic type when the system loads the implementation (e.g. when the module
[938](https://gtk-rs.org#938)///   is loaded). Optionally setting `lazy_registration` to `true` postpones
[939](https://gtk-rs.org#939)///   registration on the first use (when `static_type()` is called for the first
[940](https://gtk-rs.org#940)///   time):
[941](https://gtk-rs.org#941)///
[942](https://gtk-rs.org#942)/// ```ignore
[943](https://gtk-rs.org#943)/// #[derive(Default)]
[944](https://gtk-rs.org#944)/// pub struct MyType;
[945](https://gtk-rs.org#945)///
[946](https://gtk-rs.org#946)/// #[glib::object_subclass]
[947](https://gtk-rs.org#947)/// #[object_subclass_dynamic(lazy_registration = true)]
[948](https://gtk-rs.org#948)/// impl ObjectSubclass for MyType { ... }
[949](https://gtk-rs.org#949)/// ```
[950](https://gtk-rs.org#950)///
[951](https://gtk-rs.org#951)/// - registration within [`TypeModule`] subclass or within [`TypePlugin`]
[952](https://gtk-rs.org#952)///   subclass: an object subclass is usually registered as a dynamic type within
[953](https://gtk-rs.org#953)///   a [`TypeModule`] subclass:
[954](https://gtk-rs.org#954)///
[955](https://gtk-rs.org#955)/// ```ignore
[956](https://gtk-rs.org#956)/// #[derive(Default)]
[957](https://gtk-rs.org#957)/// pub struct MyModuleType;
[958](https://gtk-rs.org#958)///
[959](https://gtk-rs.org#959)/// #[glib::object_subclass]
[960](https://gtk-rs.org#960)/// #[object_subclass_dynamic]
[961](https://gtk-rs.org#961)/// impl ObjectSubclass for MyModuleType { ... }
[962](https://gtk-rs.org#962)/// ...
[963](https://gtk-rs.org#963)/// #[derive(Default)]
[964](https://gtk-rs.org#964)/// pub struct MyModule;
[965](https://gtk-rs.org#965)/// ...
[966](https://gtk-rs.org#966)/// impl TypeModuleImpl for MyModule {
[967](https://gtk-rs.org#967)///     fn load(&self) -> bool {
[968](https://gtk-rs.org#968)///         // registers object subclasses as dynamic types.
[969](https://gtk-rs.org#969)///         let my_module = self.obj();
[970](https://gtk-rs.org#970)///         let type_module: &glib::TypeModule = my_module.upcast_ref();
[971](https://gtk-rs.org#971)///         MyModuleType::on_implementation_load(type_module)
[972](https://gtk-rs.org#972)///     }
[973](https://gtk-rs.org#973)///     ...
[974](https://gtk-rs.org#974)/// }
[975](https://gtk-rs.org#975)/// ```
[976](https://gtk-rs.org#976)///
[977](https://gtk-rs.org#977)/// Optionally setting `plugin_type` allows to register an object subclass as a
[978](https://gtk-rs.org#978)/// dynamic type within a [`TypePlugin`] subclass that is not a [`TypeModule`]:
[979](https://gtk-rs.org#979)///
[980](https://gtk-rs.org#980)/// ```ignore
[981](https://gtk-rs.org#981)/// #[derive(Default)]
[982](https://gtk-rs.org#982)/// pub struct MyPluginType;
[983](https://gtk-rs.org#983)///
[984](https://gtk-rs.org#984)/// #[glib::object_subclass]
[985](https://gtk-rs.org#985)/// #[object_subclass_dynamic(plugin_type = MyPlugin)]
[986](https://gtk-rs.org#986)/// impl ObjectSubclass for MyPluginType { ... }
[987](https://gtk-rs.org#987)/// ...
[988](https://gtk-rs.org#988)/// #[derive(Default)]
[989](https://gtk-rs.org#989)/// pub struct MyPlugin;
[990](https://gtk-rs.org#990)/// ...
[991](https://gtk-rs.org#991)/// impl TypePluginImpl for MyPlugin {
[992](https://gtk-rs.org#992)///     fn use_plugin(&self) {
[993](https://gtk-rs.org#993)///         // register object subclasses as dynamic types.
[994](https://gtk-rs.org#994)///         let my_plugin = self.obj();
[995](https://gtk-rs.org#995)///         MyPluginType::on_implementation_load(my_plugin.as_ref());
[996](https://gtk-rs.org#996)///     }
[997](https://gtk-rs.org#997)///     ...
[998](https://gtk-rs.org#998)/// }
[999](https://gtk-rs.org#999)/// ```
[1000](https://gtk-rs.org#1000)///
[1001](https://gtk-rs.org#1001)/// [`ObjectSubclass`]: ../glib/subclass/types/trait.ObjectSubclass.html
[1002](https://gtk-rs.org#1002)/// [`TypePlugin`]: ../glib/gobject/type_plugin/struct.TypePlugin.html
[1003](https://gtk-rs.org#1003)/// [`TypeModule`]: ../glib/gobject/type_module/struct.TypeModule.html
[1004](https://gtk-rs.org#1004)/// [`TypePluginExt::unuse`]: ../glib/gobject/type_plugin/trait.TypePluginExt.html#method.unuse
[1005](https://gtk-rs.org#1005)#[proc_macro_attribute]
[1006](https://gtk-rs.org#1006)pub fn [object_subclass](https://gtk-rs.org/glib_macros/attr.object_subclass.html)(_attr: [TokenStream](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/proc_macro/struct.TokenStream.html), item: [TokenStream](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/proc_macro/struct.TokenStream.html)) -> [TokenStream](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/proc_macro/struct.TokenStream.html) {
[1007](https://gtk-rs.org#1007)    let input = [parse_macro_input!](https://docs.rs/syn/2.0.118/syn/macro.parse_macro_input.html)(item with object_impl_attributes::Input::parse_subclass);
[1008](https://gtk-rs.org#1008)    object_impl_attributes::subclass::[impl_object_subclass](https://gtk-rs.org/object_impl_attributes/subclass.rs.html#7-169)([input](https://gtk-rs.org#1007)).[into](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/convert/trait.Into.html#tymethod.into)()

[1011](https://gtk-rs.org#1011)/// Macro for boilerplate of [`ObjectInterface`] implementations.
[1012](https://gtk-rs.org#1012)///
[1013](https://gtk-rs.org#1013)/// This adds implementations for the `get_type()` method, which should probably never be defined
[1014](https://gtk-rs.org#1014)/// differently.
[1015](https://gtk-rs.org#1015)///
[1016](https://gtk-rs.org#1016)/// It provides default values for the `Prerequisites` type parameter. If this is present, the macro
[1017](https://gtk-rs.org#1017)/// will use the provided value instead of the default.
[1018](https://gtk-rs.org#1018)///
[1019](https://gtk-rs.org#1019)/// `Prerequisites` are interfaces for types that require a specific base class or interfaces.
[1020](https://gtk-rs.org#1020)///
[1021](https://gtk-rs.org#1021)/// ```ignore
[1022](https://gtk-rs.org#1022)/// type Prerequisites = ();
[1023](https://gtk-rs.org#1023)/// ```
[1024](https://gtk-rs.org#1024)///
[1025](https://gtk-rs.org#1025)/// An object interface can be registered as a dynamic type by setting the
[1026](https://gtk-rs.org#1026)/// macro helper attribute `object_interface_dynamic`:
[1027](https://gtk-rs.org#1027)/// ```ignore
[1028](https://gtk-rs.org#1028)/// pub struct MyInterface {
[1029](https://gtk-rs.org#1029)///     parent: glib::gobject_ffi::GTypeInterface,
[1030](https://gtk-rs.org#1030)/// }
[1031](https://gtk-rs.org#1031)/// #[glib::object_interface]
[1032](https://gtk-rs.org#1032)/// #[object_interface_dynamic]
[1033](https://gtk-rs.org#1033)/// unsafe impl ObjectInterface for MyInterface { ... }
[1034](https://gtk-rs.org#1034)/// ```
[1035](https://gtk-rs.org#1035)///
[1036](https://gtk-rs.org#1036)/// As a dynamic type, an object interface must be explicitly registered when
[1037](https://gtk-rs.org#1037)/// the system loads the implementation (see [`TypePlugin`] and [`TypeModule`]).
[1038](https://gtk-rs.org#1038)/// Therefore, whereas an object interface can be registered only once as a
[1039](https://gtk-rs.org#1039)/// static type, it can be registered several times as a dynamic type.
[1040](https://gtk-rs.org#1040)///
[1041](https://gtk-rs.org#1041)/// An object interface registered as a dynamic type is never unregistered. The
[1042](https://gtk-rs.org#1042)/// system calls [`TypePluginExt::unuse`] to unload the implementation. If the
[1043](https://gtk-rs.org#1043)/// [`TypePlugin`] subclass is a [`TypeModule`], the object interface
[1044](https://gtk-rs.org#1044)/// registered as a dynamic type is marked as unloaded and must be registered
[1045](https://gtk-rs.org#1045)/// again when the module is reloaded.
[1046](https://gtk-rs.org#1046)///
[1047](https://gtk-rs.org#1047)/// The macro helper attribute `object_interface_dynamic` provides two
[1048](https://gtk-rs.org#1048)/// behaviors when registering an object interface as a dynamic type:
[1049](https://gtk-rs.org#1049)///
[1050](https://gtk-rs.org#1050)/// - lazy registration: by default an object interface is registered as a
[1051](https://gtk-rs.org#1051)///   dynamic type when the system loads the implementation (e.g. when the module

[1057](https://gtk-rs.org#1057)///     parent: glib::gobject_ffi::GTypeInterface,
[1058](https://gtk-rs.org#1058)/// }
[1059](https://gtk-rs.org#1059)/// #[glib::object_interface]
[1060](https://gtk-rs.org#1060)/// #[object_interface_dynamic(lazy_registration = true)]
[1061](https://gtk-rs.org#1061)/// unsafe impl ObjectInterface for MyInterface { ... }
[1062](https://gtk-rs.org#1062)/// ```
[1063](https://gtk-rs.org#1063)///
[1064](https://gtk-rs.org#1064)/// - registration within [`TypeModule`] subclass or within [`TypePlugin`]
[1065](https://gtk-rs.org#1065)///   subclass: an object interface is usually registered as a dynamic type
[1066](https://gtk-rs.org#1066)///   within a [`TypeModule`] subclass:
[1067](https://gtk-rs.org#1067)///

[1070](https://gtk-rs.org#1070)///     parent: glib::gobject_ffi::GTypeInterface,
[1071](https://gtk-rs.org#1071)/// }
[1072](https://gtk-rs.org#1072)/// #[glib::object_interface]

[1116](https://gtk-rs.org#1116)/// [`TypeModule`]: ../glib/gobject/type_module/struct.TypeModule.html

[1124](https://gtk-rs.org#1124)/// Macro for deriving implementations of [`glib::clone::Downgrade`] and

[1195](https://gtk-rs.org#1195)/// Derive macro for serializing/deserializing custom structs/enums as [`glib::Variant`]s.
[1196](https://gtk-rs.org#1196)///
[1197](https://gtk-rs.org#1197)/// # Example
[1198](https://gtk-rs.org#1198)///
[1199](https://gtk-rs.org#1199)/// ```
[1200](https://gtk-rs.org#1200)/// use glib::prelude::*;
[1201](https://gtk-rs.org#1201)///
[1202](https://gtk-rs.org#1202)/// #[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Eq, glib::Variant)]
[1203](https://gtk-rs.org#1203)/// struct Foo {
[1204](https://gtk-rs.org#1204)///     some_string: String,
[1205](https://gtk-rs.org#1205)///     some_int: i32,
[1206](https://gtk-rs.org#1206)/// }
[1207](https://gtk-rs.org#1207)///
[1208](https://gtk-rs.org#1208)/// let v = Foo { some_string: String::from("bar"), some_int: 1 };
[1209](https://gtk-rs.org#1209)/// let var = v.to_variant();
[1210](https://gtk-rs.org#1210)/// assert_eq!(var.get::<Foo>(), Some(v));
[1211](https://gtk-rs.org#1211)/// ```
[1212](https://gtk-rs.org#1212)///
[1213](https://gtk-rs.org#1213)/// When storing `Vec`s of fixed size types it is a good idea to wrap these in
[1214](https://gtk-rs.org#1214)/// `glib::FixedSizeVariantArray` as serialization/deserialization will be more efficient.
[1215](https://gtk-rs.org#1215)///
[1216](https://gtk-rs.org#1216)/// # Example
[1217](https://gtk-rs.org#1217)///
[1218](https://gtk-rs.org#1218)/// ```
[1219](https://gtk-rs.org#1219)/// use glib::prelude::*;
[1220](https://gtk-rs.org#1220)///
[1221](https://gtk-rs.org#1221)/// #[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Eq, glib::Variant)]
[1222](https://gtk-rs.org#1222)/// struct Foo {
[1223](https://gtk-rs.org#1223)///     some_vec: glib::FixedSizeVariantArray<Vec<u32>, u32>,
[1224](https://gtk-rs.org#1224)///     some_int: i32,
[1225](https://gtk-rs.org#1225)/// }
[1226](https://gtk-rs.org#1226)///
[1227](https://gtk-rs.org#1227)/// let v = Foo { some_vec: vec![1u32, 2u32].into(), some_int: 1 };
[1228](https://gtk-rs.org#1228)/// let var = v.to_variant();
[1229](https://gtk-rs.org#1229)/// assert_eq!(var.get::<Foo>(), Some(v));
[1230](https://gtk-rs.org#1230)/// ```
[1231](https://gtk-rs.org#1231)///
[1232](https://gtk-rs.org#1232)/// Enums are serialized as a tuple `(sv)` with the first value as a [kebab case] string for the
[1233](https://gtk-rs.org#1233)/// enum variant, or just `s` if this is a C-style enum. Some additional attributes are supported
[1234](https://gtk-rs.org#1234)/// for enums:
[1235](https://gtk-rs.org#1235)/// - `#[variant_enum(repr)]` to serialize the enum variant as an integer type instead of `s`.  The
[1236](https://gtk-rs.org#1236)///   `#[repr]` attribute must also be specified on the enum with a sized integer type, and the type
[1237](https://gtk-rs.org#1237)///   must implement `Copy`.
[1238](https://gtk-rs.org#1238)/// - `#[variant_enum(enum)]` uses [`EnumClass`] to serialize/deserialize as nicks. Meant for use
[1239](https://gtk-rs.org#1239)///   with [`glib::Enum`](Enum).
[1240](https://gtk-rs.org#1240)/// - `#[variant_enum(flags)]` uses [`FlagsClass`] to serialize/deserialize as nicks. Meant for use
[1241](https://gtk-rs.org#1241)///   with [`glib::flags`](macro@flags).
[1242](https://gtk-rs.org#1242)/// - `#[variant_enum(enum, repr)]` serializes as `i32`. Meant for use with [`glib::Enum`](Enum).
[1243](https://gtk-rs.org#1243)///   The type must also implement `Copy`.
[1244](https://gtk-rs.org#1244)/// - `#[variant_enum(flags, repr)]` serializes as `u32`. Meant for use with
[1245](https://gtk-rs.org#1245)///   [`glib::flags`](macro@flags).
[1246](https://gtk-rs.org#1246)///
[1247](https://gtk-rs.org#1247)/// # Example
[1248](https://gtk-rs.org#1248)///
[1249](https://gtk-rs.org#1249)/// ```
[1250](https://gtk-rs.org#1250)/// use glib::prelude::*;
[1251](https://gtk-rs.org#1251)///
[1252](https://gtk-rs.org#1252)/// #[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Eq, glib::Variant)]
[1253](https://gtk-rs.org#1253)/// enum Foo {
[1254](https://gtk-rs.org#1254)///     MyA,
[1255](https://gtk-rs.org#1255)///     MyB(i32),
[1256](https://gtk-rs.org#1256)///     MyC { some_int: u32, some_string: String }
[1257](https://gtk-rs.org#1257)/// }
[1258](https://gtk-rs.org#1258)///
[1259](https://gtk-rs.org#1259)/// let v = Foo::MyC { some_int: 1, some_string: String::from("bar") };
[1260](https://gtk-rs.org#1260)/// let var = v.to_variant();
[1261](https://gtk-rs.org#1261)/// assert_eq!(var.child_value(0).str(), Some("my-c"));
[1262](https://gtk-rs.org#1262)/// assert_eq!(var.get::<Foo>(), Some(v));
[1263](https://gtk-rs.org#1263)///
[1264](https://gtk-rs.org#1264)/// #[derive(Debug, Copy, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, glib::Variant)]
[1265](https://gtk-rs.org#1265)/// #[variant_enum(repr)]
[1266](https://gtk-rs.org#1266)/// #[repr(u8)]
[1267](https://gtk-rs.org#1267)/// enum Bar {
[1268](https://gtk-rs.org#1268)///     A,
[1269](https://gtk-rs.org#1269)///     B = 3,
[1270](https://gtk-rs.org#1270)///     C = 7
[1271](https://gtk-rs.org#1271)/// }
[1272](https://gtk-rs.org#1272)///
[1273](https://gtk-rs.org#1273)/// let v = Bar::B;
[1274](https://gtk-rs.org#1274)/// let var = v.to_variant();
[1275](https://gtk-rs.org#1275)/// assert_eq!(var.get::<u8>(), Some(3));
[1276](https://gtk-rs.org#1276)/// assert_eq!(var.get::<Bar>(), Some(v));
[1277](https://gtk-rs.org#1277)///
[1278](https://gtk-rs.org#1278)/// #[derive(Debug, Copy, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, glib::Enum, glib::Variant)]
[1279](https://gtk-rs.org#1279)/// #[variant_enum(enum)]
[1280](https://gtk-rs.org#1280)/// #[enum_type(name = "MyEnum")]
[1281](https://gtk-rs.org#1281)/// enum MyEnum {
[1282](https://gtk-rs.org#1282)///     Val,
[1283](https://gtk-rs.org#1283)///     #[enum_value(name = "My Val")]
[1284](https://gtk-rs.org#1284)///     ValWithCustomName,
[1285](https://gtk-rs.org#1285)///     #[enum_value(name = "My Other Val", nick = "other")]
[1286](https://gtk-rs.org#1286)///     ValWithCustomNameAndNick,
[1287](https://gtk-rs.org#1287)/// }
[1288](https://gtk-rs.org#1288)///
[1289](https://gtk-rs.org#1289)/// let v = MyEnum::ValWithCustomNameAndNick;
[1290](https://gtk-rs.org#1290)/// let var = v.to_variant();
[1291](https://gtk-rs.org#1291)/// assert_eq!(var.str(), Some("other"));
[1292](https://gtk-rs.org#1292)/// assert_eq!(var.get::<MyEnum>(), Some(v));
[1293](https://gtk-rs.org#1293)/// ```
[1294](https://gtk-rs.org#1294)///
[1295](https://gtk-rs.org#1295)/// [`glib::Variant`]: ../glib/variant/struct.Variant.html
[1296](https://gtk-rs.org#1296)/// [`EnumClass`]: ../glib/struct.EnumClass.html
[1297](https://gtk-rs.org#1297)/// [`FlagsClass`]: ../glib/struct.FlagsClass.html
[1298](https://gtk-rs.org#1298)/// [kebab case]: https://docs.rs/heck/0.4.0/heck/trait.ToKebabCase.html
[1299](https://gtk-rs.org#1299)#[proc_macro_derive(Variant, attributes(variant_enum))]
[1300](https://gtk-rs.org#1300)pub fn [variant_derive](https://gtk-rs.org/glib_macros/derive.Variant.html)(input: [TokenStream](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/proc_macro/struct.TokenStream.html)) -> [TokenStream](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/proc_macro/struct.TokenStream.html) {
[1301](https://gtk-rs.org#1301)    let input = [parse_macro_input!](https://docs.rs/syn/2.0.118/syn/macro.parse_macro_input.html)(input as DeriveInput);
[1302](https://gtk-rs.org#1302)    variant_derive::[impl_variant](https://gtk-rs.org/variant_derive.rs.html#10-39)([input](https://gtk-rs.org#1301))

[1323](https://gtk-rs.org#1323)/// This macro enables you to derive object properties in a quick way.
[1324](https://gtk-rs.org#1324)///
[1325](https://gtk-rs.org#1325)/// # Supported `#[property]` attributes
[1326](https://gtk-rs.org#1326)/// | Attribute | Description | Default | Example |
[1327](https://gtk-rs.org#1327)/// | --- | --- | --- | --- |
[1328](https://gtk-rs.org#1328)/// | `name = "literal"` | The name of the property | field ident where `_` (leading and trailing `_` are trimmed) is replaced into `-` | `#[property(name = "prop-name")]` |
[1329](https://gtk-rs.org#1329)/// | `type = expr` | The type of the property | inferred | `#[property(type = i32)]` |
[1330](https://gtk-rs.org#1330)/// | `get [= expr]` | Specify that the property is readable and use [`PropertyGet::get`] [or optionally set a custom internal getter] | | `#[property(get)]`, `#[property(get = get_prop)]`, or `[property(get = \|_\| 2)]` |
[1331](https://gtk-rs.org#1331)/// | `set [= expr]` | Specify that the property is writable and use [`PropertySet::set`] [or optionally set a custom internal setter] | | `#[property(set)]`, `#[property(set = set_prop)]`, or `[property(set = \|_, val\| {})]` |
[1332](https://gtk-rs.org#1332)/// | `override_class = expr` | The type of class of which to override the property from | | `#[property(override_class = SomeClass)]` |
[1333](https://gtk-rs.org#1333)/// | `override_interface = expr` | The type of interface of which to override the property from | | `#[property(override_interface = SomeInterface)]` |
[1334](https://gtk-rs.org#1334)/// | `nullable` | Whether to use `Option<T>` in the generated setter method |  | `#[property(nullable)]` |
[1335](https://gtk-rs.org#1335)/// | `member = ident` | Field of the nested type where property is retrieved and set | | `#[property(member = author)]` |
[1336](https://gtk-rs.org#1336)/// | `construct` | Specify that the property is construct property. Ensures that the property is always set during construction (if not explicitly then the default value is used). The use of a custom internal setter is supported. | | `#[property(get, construct)]` or `#[property(get, set = set_prop, construct)]` |
[1337](https://gtk-rs.org#1337)/// | `construct_only` | Specify that the property is construct only. This will not generate a public setter and only allow the property to be set during object construction. The use of a custom internal setter is supported. | | `#[property(get, construct_only)]` or `#[property(get, set = set_prop, construct_only)]` |
[1338](https://gtk-rs.org#1338)/// | `builder(<required-params>)[.ident]*` | Used to input required params or add optional Param Spec builder fields | | `#[property(builder(SomeEnum::default()))]`, `#[builder().default_value(1).minimum(0).maximum(5)]`, etc.  |
[1339](https://gtk-rs.org#1339)/// | `default` | Sets the param spec builder field to the default value | | `#[property(default)]` |
[1340](https://gtk-rs.org#1340)/// | `default = expr` | Sets the `default_value` field of the Param Spec builder | | `#[property(default = 1)]` |
[1341](https://gtk-rs.org#1341)/// | `<optional-pspec-builder-fields> = expr` | Used to add optional Param Spec builder fields | | `#[property(minimum = 0)` , `#[property(minimum = 0, maximum = 1)]`, etc. |
[1342](https://gtk-rs.org#1342)/// | `<optional-pspec-builder-fields>` | Used to add optional Param Spec builder fields | | `#[property(explicit_notify)]` , `#[property(construct_only)]`, etc. |
[1343](https://gtk-rs.org#1343)///
[1344](https://gtk-rs.org#1344)/// ## Using Rust keywords as property names
[1345](https://gtk-rs.org#1345)/// You might hit a roadblock when declaring properties with this macro because you want to use a name that happens to be a Rust keyword. This may happen with names like `loop`, which is a pretty common name when creating things like animation handlers.
[1346](https://gtk-rs.org#1346)/// To use those names, you can make use of the raw identifier feature of Rust. Simply prefix the identifier name with `r#` in the struct declaration. Internally, those `r#`s are stripped so you can use its expected name in [`ObjectExt::property`] or within GtkBuilder template files.
[1347](https://gtk-rs.org#1347)///
[1348](https://gtk-rs.org#1348)/// # Generated methods
[1349](https://gtk-rs.org#1349)/// The following methods are generated on the wrapper type specified on `#[properties(wrapper_type = ...)]`:
[1350](https://gtk-rs.org#1350)/// * `$property()`, when the property is readable
[1351](https://gtk-rs.org#1351)/// * `set_$property()`, when the property is writable and not construct-only
[1352](https://gtk-rs.org#1352)/// * `connect_$property_notify()`
[1353](https://gtk-rs.org#1353)/// * `notify_$property()`
[1354](https://gtk-rs.org#1354)///
[1355](https://gtk-rs.org#1355)/// # Documentation
[1356](https://gtk-rs.org#1356)///
[1357](https://gtk-rs.org#1357)/// Doc comments preceding a `#[property]` attribute will be copied to the generated getter and setter methods. You can specify different comments by the getter and setter by using `# Getter` and `# Setter` headings. The text under the header will be copied to the respective method.
[1358](https://gtk-rs.org#1358)///
[1359](https://gtk-rs.org#1359)/// ## Extension trait
[1360](https://gtk-rs.org#1360)/// You can choose to move the method definitions to a trait by using `#[properties(wrapper_type = super::MyType, ext_trait = MyTypePropertiesExt)]`.
[1361](https://gtk-rs.org#1361)/// The trait name is optional, and defaults to `MyTypePropertiesExt`, where `MyType` is extracted from the wrapper type.
[1362](https://gtk-rs.org#1362)/// Note: The trait is defined in the same module where the `#[derive(Properties)]` call happens, and is implemented on the wrapper type.
[1363](https://gtk-rs.org#1363)///
[1364](https://gtk-rs.org#1364)/// Notice: You can't reimplement the generated methods on the wrapper type, unless you move them to a trait.
[1365](https://gtk-rs.org#1365)/// You can change the behavior of the generated getter/setter methods by using a custom internal getter/setter.
[1366](https://gtk-rs.org#1366)///
[1367](https://gtk-rs.org#1367)/// # Internal getters and setters
[1368](https://gtk-rs.org#1368)/// By default, they are generated for you. However, you can use a custom getter/setter
[1369](https://gtk-rs.org#1369)/// by assigning an expression to `get`/`set` `#[property]` attributes: `#[property(get = |_| 2, set)]` or `#[property(get, set = custom_setter_func)]`.
[1370](https://gtk-rs.org#1370)///
[1371](https://gtk-rs.org#1371)/// # Supported types
[1372](https://gtk-rs.org#1372)/// Every type implementing the trait [`Property`] is supported.
[1373](https://gtk-rs.org#1373)/// The type `Option<T>` is supported as a property only if `Option<T>` implements [`ToValueOptional`].
[1374](https://gtk-rs.org#1374)/// Optional types also require the `nullable` attribute: without it, the generated setter on the wrapper type
[1375](https://gtk-rs.org#1375)/// will take `T` instead of `Option<T>`, preventing the user from ever calling the setter with a `None` value.
[1376](https://gtk-rs.org#1376)///
[1377](https://gtk-rs.org#1377)/// Notice: For enums that derive [`Enum`] or are C-style enums, you must explicitly specify the
[1378](https://gtk-rs.org#1378)/// default value of the enum using the `builder` parameter in the `#[property]` attribute.
[1379](https://gtk-rs.org#1379)///
[1380](https://gtk-rs.org#1380)/// ## Adding support for custom types
[1381](https://gtk-rs.org#1381)/// ### Types wrapping an existing <code>T: [ToValue] + [HasParamSpec]</code>
[1382](https://gtk-rs.org#1382)/// If you have declared a newtype as
[1383](https://gtk-rs.org#1383)/// ```rust
[1384](https://gtk-rs.org#1384)/// struct MyInt(i32);
[1385](https://gtk-rs.org#1385)/// ```
[1386](https://gtk-rs.org#1386)/// you can use it as a property by deriving [`ValueDelegate`].
[1387](https://gtk-rs.org#1387)///
[1388](https://gtk-rs.org#1388)/// ### Types with inner mutability
[1389](https://gtk-rs.org#1389)/// The trait [`Property`] must be implemented.
[1390](https://gtk-rs.org#1390)/// The traits [`PropertyGet`] and [`PropertySet`] should be implemented to enable the Properties macro
[1391](https://gtk-rs.org#1391)/// to generate a default internal getter/setter.
[1392](https://gtk-rs.org#1392)/// If possible, implementing [`PropertySetNested`] is preferred over `PropertySet`, because it
[1393](https://gtk-rs.org#1393)/// enables this macro to access the contained type and provide access to its fields,
[1394](https://gtk-rs.org#1394)/// using the `member = $structfield` syntax.
[1395](https://gtk-rs.org#1395)///
[1396](https://gtk-rs.org#1396)/// ### Types without [`HasParamSpec`][HasParamSpec]
[1397](https://gtk-rs.org#1397)/// If you have encountered a type <code>T: [ToValue]</code>, inside the gtk-rs crate, which doesn't implement [`HasParamSpec`][HasParamSpec],
[1398](https://gtk-rs.org#1398)/// then it's a bug and you should report it.
[1399](https://gtk-rs.org#1399)/// If you need to support a `ToValue` type with a [`ParamSpec`] not provided by gtk-rs, then you need to
[1400](https://gtk-rs.org#1400)/// implement `HasParamSpec` on that type.
[1401](https://gtk-rs.org#1401)///
[1402](https://gtk-rs.org#1402)/// # Example
[1403](https://gtk-rs.org#1403)/// ```
[1404](https://gtk-rs.org#1404)/// use std::cell::{Cell, RefCell};
[1405](https://gtk-rs.org#1405)/// use glib::prelude::*;
[1406](https://gtk-rs.org#1406)/// use glib::subclass::prelude::*;
[1407](https://gtk-rs.org#1407)/// use glib_macros::Properties;
[1408](https://gtk-rs.org#1408)///

[1410](https://gtk-rs.org#1410)/// struct Author {

[1412](https://gtk-rs.org#1412)///     nick: String,

[1417](https://gtk-rs.org#1417)/// enum MyEnum {
[1418](https://gtk-rs.org#1418)///     #[default]

[1420](https://gtk-rs.org#1420)///     OtherVal
[1421](https://gtk-rs.org#1421)/// }

[1451](https://gtk-rs.org#1451)///         my_enum_with_default: Cell<MyEnum>,
[1452](https://gtk-rs.org#1452)///         /// # Getter
[1453](https://gtk-rs.org#1453)///         ///

[1609](https://gtk-rs.org#1609)
[1610](https://gtk-rs.org#1610)/// An attribute macro for writing asynchronous test functions.
[1611](https://gtk-rs.org#1611)///
[1612](https://gtk-rs.org#1612)/// This macro is designed to wrap an asynchronous test function and ensure that
[1613](https://gtk-rs.org#1613)/// it runs within a `glib::MainContext`. It helps in writing async tests that
[1614](https://gtk-rs.org#1614)/// require the use of an event loop for the asynchronous execution.
[1615](https://gtk-rs.org#1615)///
[1616](https://gtk-rs.org#1616)/// # Example
[1617](https://gtk-rs.org#1617)///
[1618](https://gtk-rs.org#1618)/// ```
