[Source](https://gtk-rs.org/src/glib/variant.rs.html#1418-1430)#### pub fn [array_iter_str](https://gtk-rs.org#method.array_iter_str)(
    &self,
) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<[VariantStrIter](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.VariantStrIter.html)<'_>, [VariantTypeMismatchError](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.VariantTypeMismatchError.html)>

[Source](https://gtk-rs.org/src/glib/variant.rs.html#1418-1430)

#### pub fn [array_iter_str](https://gtk-rs.org#method.array_iter_str)(
    &self,
) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<[VariantStrIter](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.VariantStrIter.html)<'_>, [VariantTypeMismatchError](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.VariantTypeMismatchError.html)>

Create an iterator over borrowed strings from a GVariant of type `as` (array of string).

This will fail if the variant is not an array of with the expected child type.

A benefit of this API over [ Self::iter()](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.Variant.html#method.iter) is that it
minimizes allocation, and provides strongly typed access.

```
let strs = &["foo", "bar"];
let strs_variant: glib::Variant = strs.to_variant();
for s in strs_variant.array_iter_str()? {
    println!("{}", s);
}
```
[Source](https://gtk-rs.org/src/glib/variant.rs.html#1466-1468)#### pub fn [is_normal_form](https://gtk-rs.org#method.is_normal_form)(&self) -> [bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html)

[Source](https://gtk-rs.org/src/glib/variant.rs.html#1466-1468)

#### pub fn [is_normal_form](https://gtk-rs.org#method.is_normal_form)(&self) -> [bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html)

Return whether this Variant is in normal form. Checks if @self is in normal form.

The main reason to do this is to detect if a given chunk of serialized data is in normal form: load the data into a #GVariant using g_variant_new_from_data() and then use this function to check.

If @self is found to be in normal form then it will be marked as
being trusted.  If the value was already marked as being trusted then
this function will immediately return [ true](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html).

There may be implementation specific restrictions on deeply nested values. GVariant is guaranteed to handle nesting up to at least 64 levels.

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#returns-14)Returns

[ true](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html) if @self is in normal form

Return whether input string is a valid `VariantClass::ObjectPath`.
Determines if a given string is a valid D-Bus object path.  You
should ensure that a string is a valid D-Bus object path before
passing it to g_variant_new_object_path().

A valid object path starts with `/` followed by zero or more
sequences of characters separated by `/` characters.  Each sequence
must contain only the characters `[A-Z][a-z][0-9]_`.  No sequence
(including the one following the final `/` character) may be empty.

a normal C nul-terminated string

#### fn [from](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/convert/trait.From.html#tymethod.from)(d: [VariantDict](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.VariantDict.html)) -> Self

Consume a given `VariantDict` and call [ VariantDict::end](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.VariantDict.html#method.end) on it.

Note: While this method consumes the `VariantDict`, the underlying
object could still be accessed through other clones because of the
reference counted clone semantics.

[598](#598)fn arrange_property_comments(comments: &[[Attribute](https://docs.rs/syn/2.0.118/syn/attr/struct.Attribute.html)]) -> ([Vec](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/vec/struct.Vec.html)<&[Attribute](https://docs.rs/syn/2.0.118/syn/attr/struct.Attribute.html)>, [Vec](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/vec/struct.Vec.html)<&[Attribute](https://docs.rs/syn/2.0.118/syn/attr/struct.Attribute.html)>) {
[603](#603)    let mut untagged = [vec!](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/macro.vec.html)[];
[604](#604)    let mut getter = [vec!](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/macro.vec.html)[];
[605](#605)    let mut setter = [vec!](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/macro.vec.html)[];
[606](#606)    let mut saw_section = false;
[607](#607)
[608](#608)    let mut current_section = &mut [untagged](#603);
[610](#610)    for attr in comments {
[611](#611)        if let syn::Meta::NameValue(meta) = &attr.meta
[612](#612)            && let syn::Expr::Lit(expr) = &meta.value
[613](#613)            && let syn::Lit::Str(lit_str) = &expr.lit
[614](#614)        {
[615](#615)            match lit_str.value().trim() {
[620](#620)                "# Getter" => {
[621](#621)                    current_section = &mut getter;
[622](#622)                    saw_section = true;
[623](#623)                }
[624](#624)                "# Setter" => {
[625](#625)                    current_section = &mut setter;
[626](#626)                    saw_section = true;
[627](#627)                }
[628](#628)                _ => current_section.push(attr),
[629](#629)            }
[630](#630)        }
[631](#631)    }
[632](#632)
[633](#633)    if ![saw_section](#606) {
[635](#635)        return ([untagged](#603).[clone](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/clone/trait.Clone.html#tymethod.clone)(), [untagged](#603));
[636](#636)    }
[637](#637)
[638](#638)    ([getter](#604), [setter](#605))
[639](#639)}

[262](#262)        match [self](#261) {
[263](#263)            EnumMode::[String](#254) => 's',
[264](#264)            EnumMode::[Repr](#255)(repr) => match [repr](#264).[to_string](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/trait.ToString.html#tymethod.to_string)().[as_str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html#method.as_str)() {
[265](#265)                "i8" | "i16" => 'n',
[266](#266)                "i32" => 'i',
[267](#267)                "i64" => 'x',
[268](#268)                "u8" => 'y',
[269](#269)                "u16" => 'q',
[270](#270)                "u32" => 'u',
[271](#271)                "u64" => 't',
[272](#272)                _ => [unimplemented!](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/macro.unimplemented.html)(),
[273](#273)            },
[274](#274)            EnumMode::[Enum](#256) { repr } => {
[275](#275)                if *[repr](#274) {
[276](#276)                    'i'
[277](#277)                } else {
[278](#278)                    's'
[279](#279)                }
[280](#280)            }
[281](#281)            EnumMode::[Flags](#257) { repr } => {
[282](#282)                if *[repr](#281) {
[283](#283)                    'u'
[284](#284)                } else {
[285](#285)                    's'
[286](#286)                }
[287](#287)            }
[288](#288)        }
[289](#289)    }

[194](https://gtk-rs.org#194)fn register_object_subclass_as_dynamic(
[195](https://gtk-rs.org#195)    crate_ident: &[TokenStream](https://docs.rs/proc-macro2/1.0.106/proc_macro2/struct.TokenStream.html),

[200](https://gtk-rs.org#200)    // The following implementations follows the lifecycle of plugins and of dynamic types (see [`TypePluginExt`] and [`TypeModuleExt`]).
[201](https://gtk-rs.org#201)    // An object subclass can be reregistered as a dynamic type.
[202](https://gtk-rs.org#202)    if [lazy_registration](https://gtk-rs.org#198) {
[203](https://gtk-rs.org#203)        // registers the object subclass as a dynamic type on the first use (lazy registration).
[204](https://gtk-rs.org#204)        // a weak reference on the plugin is stored and will be used later on the first use of the object subclass.
[205](https://gtk-rs.org#205)        // this implementation relies on a static storage of a weak reference on the plugin and of the GLib type to know if the object subclass has been registered.
[206](https://gtk-rs.org#206)
[207](https://gtk-rs.org#207)        // the registration status type.
[208](https://gtk-rs.org#208)        let registration_status_type = [format_ident!](https://docs.rs/quote/1.0.46/quote/macro.format_ident.html)("{}RegistrationStatus", self_ty);
[209](https://gtk-rs.org#209)        // name of the static variable to store the registration status.
[210](https://gtk-rs.org#210)        let registration_status = [format_ident!](https://docs.rs/quote/1.0.46/quote/macro.format_ident.html)(
[211](https://gtk-rs.org#211)            "{}",
[212](https://gtk-rs.org#212)            registration_status_type.to_string().to_shouty_snake_case()
[213](https://gtk-rs.org#213)        );
[214](https://gtk-rs.org#214)
[215](https://gtk-rs.org#215)        [quote!](https://docs.rs/quote/1.0.46/quote/macro.quote.html) {
[216](https://gtk-rs.org#216)            /// The registration status type: a tuple of the weak reference on the plugin and of the GLib type.
[217](https://gtk-rs.org#217)            struct #registration_status_type(<#plugin_ty as #crate_ident::clone::Downgrade>::Weak, #crate_ident::Type);
[218](https://gtk-rs.org#218)            unsafe impl Send for #registration_status_type {}
[219](https://gtk-rs.org#219)
[220](https://gtk-rs.org#220)            /// The registration status protected by a mutex guarantees so that no other threads are concurrently accessing the data.
[221](https://gtk-rs.org#221)            static #registration_status: ::std::sync::Mutex<Option<#registration_status_type>> = ::std::sync::Mutex::new(None);
[222](https://gtk-rs.org#222)
[223](https://gtk-rs.org#223)            impl #self_ty {
[224](https://gtk-rs.org#224)                /// Registers the object subclass as a dynamic type within the plugin only once.
[225](https://gtk-rs.org#225)                /// Plugin must have been used at least once.
[226](https://gtk-rs.org#226)                /// Do nothing if plugin has never been used or if the object subclass is already registered as a dynamic type.
[227](https://gtk-rs.org#227)                #[inline]
[228](https://gtk-rs.org#228)                fn register_type() {
[229](https://gtk-rs.org#229)                    let mut registration_status = #registration_status.lock().unwrap();
[230](https://gtk-rs.org#230)                    match ::std::ops::DerefMut::deref_mut(&mut registration_status) {
[231](https://gtk-rs.org#231)                        // plugin has never been used, so the object subclass cannot be registered as a dynamic type.
[232](https://gtk-rs.org#232)                        None => (),
[233](https://gtk-rs.org#233)                        // plugin has been used and the object subclass has not been registered yet, so registers it as a dynamic type.
[234](https://gtk-rs.org#234)                        Some(#registration_status_type(type_plugin, type_)) if !type_.is_valid() => {
[235](https://gtk-rs.org#235)                            *type_ = #crate_ident::subclass::register_dynamic_type::<#plugin_ty, Self>(&(type_plugin.upgrade().unwrap()));
[236](https://gtk-rs.org#236)                        },
[237](https://gtk-rs.org#237)                        // plugin has been used and the object subclass has already been registered as a dynamic type.
[238](https://gtk-rs.org#238)                        Some(_) => ()
[239](https://gtk-rs.org#239)                    }
[240](https://gtk-rs.org#240)                }
[241](https://gtk-rs.org#241)
[242](https://gtk-rs.org#242)                /// Depending on the plugin lifecycle state and on the registration status of the object subclass:
[243](https://gtk-rs.org#243)                /// If plugin is used (and has loaded the implementation) for the first time, postpones the registration and stores a weak reference on the plugin.
[244](https://gtk-rs.org#244)                /// If plugin is reused (and has reloaded the implementation) and the object subclass has been already registered as a dynamic type, reregisters it.
[245](https://gtk-rs.org#245)                /// An object subclass can be reregistered several times as a dynamic type.
[246](https://gtk-rs.org#246)                /// If plugin is reused (and has reloaded the implementation) and the object subclass has not been registered yet as a dynamic type, do nothing.
[247](https://gtk-rs.org#247)                #[inline]
[248](https://gtk-rs.org#248)                pub fn on_implementation_load(type_plugin: &#plugin_ty) -> bool {
[249](https://gtk-rs.org#249)                    let mut registration_status = #registration_status.lock().unwrap();
[250](https://gtk-rs.org#250)                    match ::std::ops::DerefMut::deref_mut(&mut registration_status) {
[251](https://gtk-rs.org#251)                        // plugin has never been used (this is the first time), so postpones registration of the object subclass as a dynamic type on the first use.
[252](https://gtk-rs.org#252)                        None => {
[253](https://gtk-rs.org#253)                            *registration_status = Some(#registration_status_type(#crate_ident::clone::Downgrade::downgrade(type_plugin), #crate_ident::Type::INVALID));
[254](https://gtk-rs.org#254)                            true
[255](https://gtk-rs.org#255)                        },
[256](https://gtk-rs.org#256)                        // plugin has been used at least one time and the object subclass has been registered as a dynamic type at least one time, so re-registers it.
[257](https://gtk-rs.org#257)                        Some(#registration_status_type(_, type_)) if type_.is_valid() => {
[258](https://gtk-rs.org#258)                            *type_ = #crate_ident::subclass::register_dynamic_type::<#plugin_ty, Self>(type_plugin);
[259](https://gtk-rs.org#259)                            type_.is_valid()
[260](https://gtk-rs.org#260)                        },
[261](https://gtk-rs.org#261)                        // plugin has been used at least one time but the object subclass has not been registered yet as a dynamic type, so keeps postponed registration.
[262](https://gtk-rs.org#262)                        Some(_) => {
[263](https://gtk-rs.org#263)                            true
[264](https://gtk-rs.org#264)                        }
[265](https://gtk-rs.org#265)                    }
[266](https://gtk-rs.org#266)                }
[267](https://gtk-rs.org#267)
[268](https://gtk-rs.org#268)                /// Depending on the plugin lifecycle state and on the registration status of the object subclass:
[269](https://gtk-rs.org#269)                /// If plugin has been used (or reused) but the object subclass has not been registered yet as a dynamic type, cancels the postponed registration by deleting the weak reference on the plugin.
[270](https://gtk-rs.org#270)                /// Else do nothing.
[271](https://gtk-rs.org#271)                #[inline]
[272](https://gtk-rs.org#272)                pub fn on_implementation_unload(type_plugin_: &#plugin_ty) -> bool {
[273](https://gtk-rs.org#273)                    let mut registration_status = #registration_status.lock().unwrap();
[274](https://gtk-rs.org#274)                    match ::std::ops::DerefMut::deref_mut(&mut registration_status) {
[275](https://gtk-rs.org#275)                        // plugin has never been used, so unload implementation is unexpected.
[276](https://gtk-rs.org#276)                        None => false,
[277](https://gtk-rs.org#277)                        // plugin has been used at least one time and the object subclass has been registered as a dynamic type at least one time.
[278](https://gtk-rs.org#278)                        Some(#registration_status_type(_, type_)) if type_.is_valid() => true,
[279](https://gtk-rs.org#279)                        // plugin has been used at least one time but the object subclass has not been registered yet as a dynamic type, so cancels the postponed registration.
[280](https://gtk-rs.org#280)                        Some(_) => {
[281](https://gtk-rs.org#281)                            *registration_status = None;
[282](https://gtk-rs.org#282)                            true
[283](https://gtk-rs.org#283)                        }
[284](https://gtk-rs.org#284)                    }
[285](https://gtk-rs.org#285)                }
[286](https://gtk-rs.org#286)            }
[287](https://gtk-rs.org#287)        }
[288](https://gtk-rs.org#288)    } else {
[289](https://gtk-rs.org#289)        // registers immediately the object subclass as a dynamic type.
[290](https://gtk-rs.org#290)
[291](https://gtk-rs.org#291)        [quote!](https://docs.rs/quote/1.0.46/quote/macro.quote.html) {
[292](https://gtk-rs.org#292)            impl #self_ty {
[293](https://gtk-rs.org#293)                /// Do nothing as the object subclass has been registered on implementation load.
[294](https://gtk-rs.org#294)                #[inline]
[295](https://gtk-rs.org#295)                fn register_type() { }
[296](https://gtk-rs.org#296)
[297](https://gtk-rs.org#297)                /// Registers the object subclass as a dynamic type within the plugin.
[298](https://gtk-rs.org#298)                /// The object subclass can be registered several times as a dynamic type.
[299](https://gtk-rs.org#299)                #[inline]
[300](https://gtk-rs.org#300)                pub fn on_implementation_load(type_plugin: &#plugin_ty) -> bool {
[301](https://gtk-rs.org#301)                    let type_ = #crate_ident::subclass::register_dynamic_type::<#plugin_ty, Self>(type_plugin);
[302](https://gtk-rs.org#302)                    type_ != #crate_ident::Type::INVALID
[303](https://gtk-rs.org#303)                }
[304](https://gtk-rs.org#304)

[306](https://gtk-rs.org#306)                #[inline]
[307](https://gtk-rs.org#307)                pub fn on_implementation_unload(type_plugin_: &#plugin_ty) -> bool {
[308](https://gtk-rs.org#308)                    true
[309](https://gtk-rs.org#309)                }
[310](https://gtk-rs.org#310)            }
[311](https://gtk-rs.org#311)        }

[112](https://gtk-rs.org#112)    if [lazy_registration](https://gtk-rs.org#108) {
[113](https://gtk-rs.org#113)        // registers the object interface as a dynamic type on the first use (lazy registration).
[114](https://gtk-rs.org#114)        // a weak reference on the plugin is stored and will be used later on the first use of the object interface.
[115](https://gtk-rs.org#115)        // this implementation relies on a static storage of a weak reference on the plugin and of the GLib type to know if the object interface has been registered.
[116](https://gtk-rs.org#116)
[117](https://gtk-rs.org#117)        // the registration status type.
[118](https://gtk-rs.org#118)        let registration_status_type = [format_ident!](https://docs.rs/quote/1.0.46/quote/macro.format_ident.html)("{}RegistrationStatus", self_ty);
[119](https://gtk-rs.org#119)        // name of the static variable to store the registration status.
[120](https://gtk-rs.org#120)        let registration_status = [format_ident!](https://docs.rs/quote/1.0.46/quote/macro.format_ident.html)(
[121](https://gtk-rs.org#121)            "{}",
[122](https://gtk-rs.org#122)            registration_status_type.to_string().to_shouty_snake_case()
[123](https://gtk-rs.org#123)        );
[124](https://gtk-rs.org#124)
[125](https://gtk-rs.org#125)        [quote!](https://docs.rs/quote/1.0.46/quote/macro.quote.html) {
[126](https://gtk-rs.org#126)            /// The registration status type: a tuple of the weak reference on the plugin and of the GLib type.
[127](https://gtk-rs.org#127)            struct #registration_status_type(<#plugin_ty as #crate_ident::clone::Downgrade>::Weak, #crate_ident::Type);
[128](https://gtk-rs.org#128)            unsafe impl Send for #registration_status_type {}
[129](https://gtk-rs.org#129)
[130](https://gtk-rs.org#130)            /// The registration status protected by a mutex guarantees so that no other threads are concurrently accessing the data.
[131](https://gtk-rs.org#131)            static #registration_status: ::std::sync::Mutex<Option<#registration_status_type>> = ::std::sync::Mutex::new(None);
[132](https://gtk-rs.org#132)
[133](https://gtk-rs.org#133)            impl #self_ty {
[134](https://gtk-rs.org#134)                /// Registers the object interface as a dynamic type within the plugin only once.
[135](https://gtk-rs.org#135)                /// Plugin must have been used at least once.
[136](https://gtk-rs.org#136)                /// Do nothing if plugin has never been used or if the object interface is already registered as a dynamic type.
[137](https://gtk-rs.org#137)                #[inline]
[138](https://gtk-rs.org#138)                fn register_interface() -> #crate_ident::Type {
[139](https://gtk-rs.org#139)                    let mut registration_status = #registration_status.lock().unwrap();
[140](https://gtk-rs.org#140)                    match ::std::ops::DerefMut::deref_mut(&mut registration_status) {
[141](https://gtk-rs.org#141)                        // plugin has never been used, so the object interface cannot be registered as a dynamic type.
[142](https://gtk-rs.org#142)                        None => #crate_ident::Type::INVALID,
[143](https://gtk-rs.org#143)                        // plugin has been used and the object interface has not been registered yet, so registers it as a dynamic type.
[144](https://gtk-rs.org#144)                        Some(#registration_status_type(type_plugin, type_)) if !type_.is_valid() => {
[145](https://gtk-rs.org#145)                            *type_ = #crate_ident::subclass::register_dynamic_interface::<#plugin_ty, Self>(&(type_plugin.upgrade().unwrap()));
[146](https://gtk-rs.org#146)                            *type_
[147](https://gtk-rs.org#147)                        },
[148](https://gtk-rs.org#148)                        // plugin has been used and the object interface has already been registered as a dynamic type.
[149](https://gtk-rs.org#149)                        Some(#registration_status_type(_, type_)) => *type_
[150](https://gtk-rs.org#150)                    }
[151](https://gtk-rs.org#151)                }
[152](https://gtk-rs.org#152)
[153](https://gtk-rs.org#153)                /// Depending on the plugin lifecycle state and on the registration status of the object interface:
[154](https://gtk-rs.org#154)                /// If plugin is used (and has loaded the implementation) for the first time, postpones the registration and stores a weak reference on the plugin.
[155](https://gtk-rs.org#155)                /// If plugin is reused (and has reloaded the implementation) and the object interface has been already registered as a dynamic type, reregisters it.
[156](https://gtk-rs.org#156)                /// An object interface can be reregistered several times as a dynamic type.
[157](https://gtk-rs.org#157)                /// If plugin is reused (and has reloaded the implementation) and the object interface has not been registered yet as a dynamic type, do nothing.
[158](https://gtk-rs.org#158)                #[inline]
[159](https://gtk-rs.org#159)                pub fn on_implementation_load(type_plugin: &#plugin_ty) -> bool {
[160](https://gtk-rs.org#160)                    let mut registration_status = #registration_status.lock().unwrap();
[161](https://gtk-rs.org#161)                    match ::std::ops::DerefMut::deref_mut(&mut registration_status) {
[162](https://gtk-rs.org#162)                        // plugin has never been used (this is the first time), so postpones registration of the object interface as a dynamic type on the first use.
[163](https://gtk-rs.org#163)                        None => {
[164](https://gtk-rs.org#164)                            *registration_status = Some(#registration_status_type(#crate_ident::clone::Downgrade::downgrade(type_plugin), #crate_ident::Type::INVALID));
[165](https://gtk-rs.org#165)                            true
[166](https://gtk-rs.org#166)                        },
[167](https://gtk-rs.org#167)                        // plugin has been used at least one time and the object interface has been registered as a dynamic type at least one time, so re-registers it.
[168](https://gtk-rs.org#168)                        Some(#registration_status_type(_, type_)) if type_.is_valid() => {
[169](https://gtk-rs.org#169)                            *type_ = #crate_ident::subclass::register_dynamic_interface::<#plugin_ty, Self>(type_plugin);
[170](https://gtk-rs.org#170)                            type_.is_valid()
[171](https://gtk-rs.org#171)                        },
[172](https://gtk-rs.org#172)                        // plugin has been used at least one time but the object interface has not been registered yet as a dynamic type, so keeps postponed registration.
[173](https://gtk-rs.org#173)                        Some(_) => {
[174](https://gtk-rs.org#174)                            true
[175](https://gtk-rs.org#175)                        }
[176](https://gtk-rs.org#176)                    }
[177](https://gtk-rs.org#177)                }
[178](https://gtk-rs.org#178)
[179](https://gtk-rs.org#179)                /// Depending on the plugin lifecycle state and on the registration status of the object interface:
[180](https://gtk-rs.org#180)                /// If plugin has been used (or reused) but the object interface has not been registered yet as a dynamic type, cancels the postponed registration by deleting the weak reference on the plugin.
[181](https://gtk-rs.org#181)                /// Else do nothing.
[182](https://gtk-rs.org#182)                #[inline]
[183](https://gtk-rs.org#183)                pub fn on_implementation_unload(type_plugin_: &#plugin_ty) -> bool {
[184](https://gtk-rs.org#184)                    let mut registration_status = #registration_status.lock().unwrap();
[185](https://gtk-rs.org#185)                    match ::std::ops::DerefMut::deref_mut(&mut registration_status) {
[186](https://gtk-rs.org#186)                        // plugin has never been used, so unload implementation is unexpected.
[187](https://gtk-rs.org#187)                        None => false,
[188](https://gtk-rs.org#188)                        // plugin has been used at least one time and the object interface has been registered as a dynamic type at least one time.
[189](https://gtk-rs.org#189)                        Some(#registration_status_type(_, type_)) if type_.is_valid() => true,
[190](https://gtk-rs.org#190)                        // plugin has been used at least one time but the object interface has not been registered yet as a dynamic type, so cancels the postponed registration.
[191](https://gtk-rs.org#191)                        Some(_) => {
[192](https://gtk-rs.org#192)                            *registration_status = None;
[193](https://gtk-rs.org#193)                            true
[194](https://gtk-rs.org#194)                        }
[195](https://gtk-rs.org#195)                    }
[196](https://gtk-rs.org#196)                }
[197](https://gtk-rs.org#197)            }
[198](https://gtk-rs.org#198)        }
[199](https://gtk-rs.org#199)    } else {
[200](https://gtk-rs.org#200)        // registers immediately the object interface as a dynamic type.
[201](https://gtk-rs.org#201)
[202](https://gtk-rs.org#202)        // name of the static variable to store the GLib type.
[203](https://gtk-rs.org#203)        let gtype_status = [format_ident!](https://docs.rs/quote/1.0.46/quote/macro.format_ident.html)("{}_G_TYPE", self_ty.to_string().to_shouty_snake_case());
[204](https://gtk-rs.org#204)
[205](https://gtk-rs.org#205)        [quote!](https://docs.rs/quote/1.0.46/quote/macro.quote.html) {
[206](https://gtk-rs.org#206)            /// The GLib type which can be safely shared between threads.
[207](https://gtk-rs.org#207)            static #gtype_status: ::std::sync::atomic::AtomicUsize = ::std::sync::atomic::AtomicUsize::new(#crate_ident::gobject_ffi::G_TYPE_INVALID);
[208](https://gtk-rs.org#208)
[209](https://gtk-rs.org#209)            impl #self_ty {

# g_debug in glib - Rust

Source: https://gtk-rs.org/gtk-rs-core/stable/latest/docs/glib/macro.g_debug.html

```
macro_rules! g_debug {
    ($log_domain:expr, $format:literal, $($arg:expr),* $(,)?) => { ... };
    ($log_domain:expr, $format:literal $(,)?) => { ... };
}
```
## Expand description

Macro used to log using GLib logging system. It uses [g_log](https://docs.gtk.org/glib/func.log.html).

It is the same as calling the [ g_log!](https://gtk-rs.org/macro.g_log.html) macro with

[.](https://gtk-rs.org/enum.LogLevel.html#variant.Debug)

`LogLevel::Debug`Example:

```
use glib::g_debug;
g_debug!("test", "test");
// Equivalent to:
use glib::{g_log, LogLevel};
g_log!("test", LogLevel::Debug, "test");
// trailing commas work as well:
g_debug!("test", "test",);
// You can also pass arguments like in format! or println!:
let x = 12;
g_debug!("test", "test: {}", x);
g_debug!("test", "test: {} {}", x, "a");
// trailing commas work as well:
g_debug!("test", "test: {} {}", x, "a",);
```

---

# CLONE_MACRO_LOG_DOMAIN in glib - Rust

Source: https://gtk-rs.org/gtk-rs-core/stable/latest/docs/glib/constant.CLONE_MACRO_LOG_DOMAIN.html

This is the log domain used by the clone! macro. If you want to use a custom
logger (it prints to stdout by default), you can set your own logger using the corresponding
log functions.

# ToValue in glib::value - Rust

Source: https://gtk-rs.org/gtk-rs-core/stable/latest/docs/glib/value/trait.ToValue.html

```
pub trait ToValue {
    // Required methods
    fn
```
[to_value](https://gtk-rs.org#tymethod.to_value)(&self) -> [Value](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.Value.html);
[value_type](https://gtk-rs.org#tymethod.value_type)(&self) -> [Type](https://gtk-rs.org/types/struct.Type.html);
}## Expand description

Trait to convert a value to a `Value`.

Similar to other common conversion traits, the following invariants are guaranteed:

- **Invertibility**:- `x.to_value().get().unwrap() == x`. In words,- `FromValue`- `ToValue`.
- **Idempotence**:- `x.to_value() == x.to_value().to_value()`. In words, applying- `ToValue`multiple times yields the same result as applying it once. Idempotence also applies the other way around:- `value.get::<Value>()`is a no-op.

There is also the possibility to wrap values within values, see [ BoxedValue](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.BoxedValue.html). All (un-)boxing needs to be done
manually, and will be preserved under the conversion methods.

The conversion methods may cause values to be cloned, which may result in reference counter changes or heap allocations depending on the source and target type.

## Required Methods[§](https://gtk-rs.org#required-methods)

## Dyn Compatibility[§](https://gtk-rs.org#dyn-compatibility)

This trait **is** [dyn compatible](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/reference/items/traits.html#dyn-compatibility).

*In older versions of Rust, dyn compatibility was called "object safety".*

# Object in glib::object - Rust

Source: https://gtk-rs.org/gtk-rs-core/stable/latest/docs/glib/object/struct.Object.html

`pub struct Object { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

The base class in the object hierarchy.

GLib type: GObject with reference counted clone semantics.

## Implementations[§](https://gtk-rs.org#implementations)

[Source](https://gtk-rs.org/src/glib/object.rs.html#1402)

Create a new instance of an object of the given type with the given properties as mutable values.

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#panics-2)Panics

This panics if the object is not instantiable, doesn’t have all the given properties or property values of the wrong type are provided.

Create a new instance of an object of the given type with the given properties.

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#panics-3)Panics

This panics if the object is not instantiable, doesn’t have all the given properties or property values of the wrong type are provided.

Unlike the other constructors this does not panic if the object is implementing
`gio::Initable` or `gio::AsyncInitable` and it might be unsafe to use the returned object
without using the API of those interfaces first.

#### fn [is](https://gtk-rs.org#tymethod.is)<T: [StaticType](https://gtk-rs.org/types/trait.StaticType.html)>(&self) -> [bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html)

Returns `true` if the object is an instance of (can be cast to) `T`.

Returns the class of the object in the given type `T`.

`None` is returned if the object is not a subclass of `T`.

#### fn [bind_property](https://gtk-rs.org#tymethod.bind_property)<'a, 'f, 't, O: [ObjectType](https://gtk-rs.org/trait.ObjectType.html)>(
    &'a self,
    source_property: &'a [str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html),
    target: [&'a O](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.reference.html),
    target_property: &'a [str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html),

Bind property `source_property` on this object to the `target_property` on the `target` object.

This allows keeping the properties of both objects in sync.

The binding can be unidirectional or bidirectional and optionally it is possible to transform the property values before they’re passed to the other object.

[Source](https://gtk-rs.org/src/glib/object.rs.html#2287)#### unsafe fn [run_dispose](https://gtk-rs.org#tymethod.run_dispose)(&self)

[Source](https://gtk-rs.org/src/glib/object.rs.html#2287)

#### unsafe fn [run_dispose](https://gtk-rs.org#tymethod.run_dispose)(&self)

Runs the dispose mechanism of the object.

This will dispose of any references the object has to other objects, and among other things will disconnect all signal handlers.

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#safety-9)Safety

Theoretically this is safe to run and afterwards the object is simply in a non-functional state, however many object implementations in C end up with memory safety issues if the object is used after disposal.

## Dyn Compatibility[§](https://gtk-rs.org#dyn-compatibility)

This trait is **not** [dyn compatible](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/reference/items/traits.html#dyn-compatibility).

*In older versions of Rust, dyn compatibility was called "object safety".*

# glib - Rust

Source: https://gtk-rs.org/gtk-rs-core/stable/latest/docs/glib/index.html

## Expand description

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#rust-glib-and-gobject-bindings)Rust GLib and GObject bindings

**Rust** bindings and wrappers for [GLib](https://docs.gtk.org/glib/), part of [gtk-rs-core](https://github.com/gtk-rs/gtk-rs-core).

GLib **2.56** is the lowest supported version for the underlying library.

This library contains bindings to GLib and GObject types and APIs as well as common building blocks used in both handmade and machine generated bindings to GTK and other GLib-based libraries.

It is the foundation for higher level libraries with uniform Rusty (safe and strongly typed) APIs. It avoids exposing GLib-specific data types where possible and is not meant to provide comprehensive GLib bindings, which would often amount to duplicating the Rust Standard Library or other utility crates.

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#minimum-supported-rust-version)Minimum supported Rust version

Currently, the minimum supported Rust version is `1.83.0`.

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#dynamic-typing)Dynamic typing

Most types in the GLib family have [ Type](https://gtk-rs.org/types/struct.Type.html) identifiers.
Their corresponding Rust types implement the

[trait.](https://gtk-rs.org/types/trait.StaticType.html)

`StaticType`A dynamically typed [ Value](https://gtk-rs.org/value/struct.Value.html) can carry values of any

`StaticType`.
[Variants](https://gtk-rs.org/gtk-rs-core/stable/latest/docs/glib/variant/struct.Variant.html)can carry values of

[.](https://gtk-rs.org/variant/trait.StaticVariantType.html)

`StaticVariantType`[§](https://gtk-rs.org#errors)Errors

Errors are represented by [ Error](https://gtk-rs.org/error/struct.Error.html), which can
carry values from various

[error domains](https://gtk-rs.org/error/trait.ErrorDomain.html)such as

[.](https://gtk-rs.org/enum.FileError.html)

`FileError`[§](https://gtk-rs.org#objects)Objects

Each class and interface has a corresponding smart pointer struct
representing an instance of that type (e.g. [ Object](https://gtk-rs.org/object/struct.Object.html) for

[or](https://docs.gtk.org/gobject/class.Object.html)

`GObject`[for](https://gtk-rs.org/gtk4-rs/stable/latest/docs/gtk4/struct.Widget.html)

`gtk4::Widget`[). They are reference counted and feature interior mutability similarly to Rust’s](https://docs.gtk.org/gtk4/class.Widget.html)

`GtkWidget`[idiom. Consequently, cloning objects is cheap and their methods never require mutable borrows. Two smart pointers are equal if they point to the same object.](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/cell/index.html#introducing-mutability-inside-of-something-immutable)

`Rc<RefCell<T>>`The root of the object hierarchy is [ Object](https://gtk-rs.org/object/struct.Object.html).
Inheritance and subtyping is denoted with the

[marker trait. The](https://gtk-rs.org/object/trait.IsA.html)

`IsA`[trait enables upcasting and downcasting.](https://gtk-rs.org/object/trait.Cast.html)

`Cast`Interfaces and non-leaf classes also have corresponding traits (e.g.
[ ObjectExt](https://gtk-rs.org/object/trait.ObjectExt.html) or

[), which are blanketly implemented for all their subtypes.](https://gtk-rs.org/gtk4-rs/stable/latest/docs/gtk4/prelude/trait.WidgetExt.html)

`WidgetExt`You can create new subclasses of [ Object](https://gtk-rs.org/object/struct.Object.html) or other object types. Look at
the module’s documentation for further details and a code example.

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#under-the-hood)Under the hood

GLib-based libraries largely operate on pointers to various boxed or
reference counted structures so the bindings have to implement corresponding
smart pointers (wrappers), which encapsulate resource management and safety
checks. Such wrappers are defined via the
[ wrapper!](https://gtk-rs.org/macro.wrapper.html) macro, which uses abstractions
defined in the

[,](https://gtk-rs.org/wrapper/index.html)

`wrapper`[,](https://gtk-rs.org/boxed/index.html)

`boxed`[and](https://gtk-rs.org/shared/index.html)

`shared`[modules. The](https://gtk-rs.org/object/index.html)

`object`[module defines and partly implements conversions between high level Rust types (including the aforementioned wrappers) and their FFI counterparts.](https://gtk-rs.org/translate/index.html)

`translate`[§](https://gtk-rs.org#documentation)Documentation

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#using)Using

We recommend using [crates from crates.io](https://crates.io/keywords/gtk-rs),
as [demonstrated here](https://gtk-rs.org/#using).

If you want to track the bleeding edge, use the git dependency instead:

```
[dependencies]
glib = { git = "https://github.com/gtk-rs/gtk-rs-core.git", package = "glib" }
```
Avoid mixing versioned and git crates like this:

```
# This will not compile
[dependencies]
glib = "0.13"
glib = { git = "https://github.com/gtk-rs/gtk-rs-core.git", package = "glib" }
```
[§](https://gtk-rs.org#license)License

**glib** is available under the MIT License, please refer to it.

- [LogLevel](https://gtk-rs.org/enum.LogLevel.html)
- [LogWriter](https://gtk-rs.org/enum.LogWriterOutput.html)- Output
- Return values from #GLogWriterFuncs to indicate whether the given log entry was successfully handled by the writer, or whether there was an error in handling it (and hence a fallback writer should be used).
- [Markup](https://gtk-rs.org/enum.MarkupError.html)- Error
- Error codes returned by markup parsing.
- [Normalize](https://gtk-rs.org/enum.NormalizeMode.html)- Mode
- Defines how a Unicode string is transformed in a canonical form, standardizing such issues as whether a character with an accent is represented as a base character and combining accent or as a single precomposed character. Unicode strings should generally be normalized before comparing them.
- [Option](https://gtk-rs.org/enum.OptionArg.html)- Arg
- The #GOptionArg enum values determine which type of extra argument the
options expect to find. If an option expects an extra argument, it can
be specified in several ways; with a short option: `-x arg`, with a long option:`--name arg`or combined in a single argument:`--name=arg`.
- [Seek](https://gtk-rs.org/enum.SeekType.html)- Type
- An enumeration specifying the base position for a g_io_channel_seek_position() operation.
- [Time](https://gtk-rs.org/enum.TimeType.html)- Type
- Disambiguates a given time in two ways.
- [Unicode](https://gtk-rs.org/enum.UnicodeBreakType.html)- Break - Type
- These are the possible line break classifications.
- [Unicode](https://gtk-rs.org/enum.UnicodeScript.html)- Script
- The #GUnicodeScript enumeration identifies different writing systems. The values correspond to the names as defined in the Unicode standard. The enumeration has been added in GLib 2.14, and is interchangeable with #PangoScript.
- [Unicode](https://gtk-rs.org/enum.UnicodeType.html)- Type
- These are the possible character classifications from the
Unicode specification.
See [Unicode Character Database](http://www.unicode.org/reports/tr44/#General_Category_Values).
- [UriError](https://gtk-rs.org/enum.UriError.html)- `v2_66`
- Error codes returned by #GUri methods.
- [Variant](https://gtk-rs.org/enum.VariantClass.html)- Class
- The range of possible top-level types of #GVariant instances.

- This is the log domain used by the `clone!``log`functions.

## Statics[§](https://gtk-rs.org#statics)

- [CSET_](https://gtk-rs.org/static.CSET_A_2_Z.html)- A_ - 2_ - Z
- The set of uppercase ASCII alphabet characters. Used for specifying valid identifier characters in #GScannerConfig.
- [CSET_](https://gtk-rs.org/static.CSET_DIGITS.html)- DIGITS
- The set of ASCII digits. Used for specifying valid identifier characters in #GScannerConfig.
- [CSET_](https://gtk-rs.org/static.CSET_a_2_z.html)- a_ - 2_ - z
- The set of lowercase ASCII alphabet characters. Used for specifying valid identifier characters in #GScannerConfig.
- [KEY_](https://gtk-rs.org/static.KEY_FILE_DESKTOP_GROUP.html)- FILE_ - DESKTOP_ - GROUP

[Desktop Entry Specification](https://specifications.freedesktop.org/desktop-entry-spec/latest/).
- [KEY_](https://gtk-rs.org/static.KEY_FILE_DESKTOP_KEY_ACTIONS.html)- FILE_ - DESKTOP_ - KEY_ - ACTIONS
- A key under `GLib::KEY_FILE_DESKTOP_GROUP`, whose value is a string list giving the available application actions.
- [KEY_](https://gtk-rs.org/static.KEY_FILE_DESKTOP_KEY_CATEGORIES.html)- FILE_ - DESKTOP_ - KEY_ - CATEGORIES
- A key under `GLib::KEY_FILE_DESKTOP_GROUP`, whose value is a list of strings giving the categories in which the desktop entry should be shown in a menu.
- [KEY_](https://gtk-rs.org/static.KEY_FILE_DESKTOP_KEY_COMMENT.html)- FILE_ - DESKTOP_ - KEY_ - COMMENT
- A key under `GLib::KEY_FILE_DESKTOP_GROUP`, whose value is a localized string giving the tooltip for the desktop entry.
- [KEY_](https://gtk-rs.org/static.KEY_FILE_DESKTOP_KEY_DBUS_ACTIVATABLE.html)- FILE_ - DESKTOP_ - KEY_ - DBUS_ - ACTIVATABLE
- A key under `GLib::KEY_FILE_DESKTOP_GROUP`, whose value is a boolean set to true if the application is D-Bus activatable.
- [KEY_](https://gtk-rs.org/static.KEY_FILE_DESKTOP_KEY_EXEC.html)- FILE_ - DESKTOP_ - KEY_ - EXEC
- A key under `GLib::KEY_FILE_DESKTOP_GROUP`, whose value is a string giving the command line to execute.
- [KEY_](https://gtk-rs.org/static.KEY_FILE_DESKTOP_KEY_GENERIC_NAME.html)- FILE_ - DESKTOP_ - KEY_ - GENERIC_ - NAME
- A key under `GLib::KEY_FILE_DESKTOP_GROUP`, whose value is a localized string giving the generic name of the desktop entry.
- [KEY_](https://gtk-rs.org/static.KEY_FILE_DESKTOP_KEY_HIDDEN.html)- FILE_ - DESKTOP_ - KEY_ - HIDDEN
- A key under `GLib::KEY_FILE_DESKTOP_GROUP`, whose value is a boolean stating whether the desktop entry has been deleted by the user.
- [KEY_](https://gtk-rs.org/static.KEY_FILE_DESKTOP_KEY_ICON.html)- FILE_ - DESKTOP_ - KEY_ - ICON
- A key under `GLib::KEY_FILE_DESKTOP_GROUP`, whose value is a localized string giving the name of the icon to be displayed for the desktop entry.
- [KEY_](https://gtk-rs.org/static.KEY_FILE_DESKTOP_KEY_MIME_TYPE.html)- FILE_ - DESKTOP_ - KEY_ - MIME_ - TYPE
- A key under `GLib::KEY_FILE_DESKTOP_GROUP`, whose value is a list of strings giving the MIME types supported by this desktop entry.
- [KEY_](https://gtk-rs.org/static.KEY_FILE_DESKTOP_KEY_NAME.html)- FILE_ - DESKTOP_ - KEY_ - NAME
- A key under `GLib::KEY_FILE_DESKTOP_GROUP`, whose value is a localized string giving the specific name of the desktop entry.
- [KEY_](https://gtk-rs.org/static.KEY_FILE_DESKTOP_KEY_NOT_SHOW_IN.html)- FILE_ - DESKTOP_ - KEY_ - NOT_ - SHOW_ - IN
- A key under `GLib::KEY_FILE_DESKTOP_GROUP`, whose value is a list of strings identifying the environments that should not display the desktop entry.
- [KEY_](https://gtk-rs.org/static.KEY_FILE_DESKTOP_KEY_NO_DISPLAY.html)- FILE_ - DESKTOP_ - KEY_ - NO_ - DISPLAY
- A key under `GLib::KEY_FILE_DESKTOP_GROUP`, whose value is a boolean stating whether the desktop entry should be shown in menus.
- [KEY_](https://gtk-rs.org/static.KEY_FILE_DESKTOP_KEY_ONLY_SHOW_IN.html)- FILE_ - DESKTOP_ - KEY_ - ONLY_ - SHOW_ - IN
- A key under `GLib::KEY_FILE_DESKTOP_GROUP`, whose value is a list of strings identifying the environments that should display the desktop entry.
- [KEY_](https://gtk-rs.org/static.KEY_FILE_DESKTOP_KEY_PATH.html)- FILE_ - DESKTOP_ - KEY_ - PATH
- A key under `GLib::KEY_FILE_DESKTOP_GROUP`, whose value is a string containing the working directory to run the program in.
- [KEY_](https://gtk-rs.org/static.KEY_FILE_DESKTOP_KEY_STARTUP_NOTIFY.html)- FILE_ - DESKTOP_ - KEY_ - STARTUP_ - NOTIFY
- A key under `GLib::KEY_FILE_DESKTOP_GROUP`, whose value is a boolean stating whether the application supports the[Startup Notification Protocol Specification](https://specifications.freedesktop.org/startup-notification-spec/latest/).
- [KEY_](https://gtk-rs.org/static.KEY_FILE_DESKTOP_KEY_STARTUP_WM_CLASS.html)- FILE_ - DESKTOP_ - KEY_ - STARTUP_ - WM_ - CLASS
- A key under `GLib::KEY_FILE_DESKTOP_GROUP`, whose value is string identifying the WM class or name hint of a window that the application will create, which can be used to emulate[Startup Notification](https://specifications.freedesktop.org/startup-notification-spec/latest/)with older applications.
- [KEY_](https://gtk-rs.org/static.KEY_FILE_DESKTOP_KEY_TERMINAL.html)- FILE_ - DESKTOP_ - KEY_ - TERMINAL
- A key under `GLib::KEY_FILE_DESKTOP_GROUP`, whose value is a boolean stating whether the program should be run in a terminal window.
- [KEY_](https://gtk-rs.org/static.KEY_FILE_DESKTOP_KEY_TRY_EXEC.html)- FILE_ - DESKTOP_ - KEY_ - TRY_ - EXEC
- A key under `GLib::KEY_FILE_DESKTOP_GROUP`, whose value is a string giving the file name of a binary on disk used to determine if the program is actually installed.
- [KEY_](https://gtk-rs.org/static.KEY_FILE_DESKTOP_KEY_TYPE.html)- FILE_ - DESKTOP_ - KEY_ - TYPE
- A key under `GLib::KEY_FILE_DESKTOP_GROUP`, whose value is a string giving the type of the desktop entry.
- [KEY_](https://gtk-rs.org/static.KEY_FILE_DESKTOP_KEY_URL.html)- FILE_ - DESKTOP_ - KEY_ - URL
- A key under `GLib::KEY_FILE_DESKTOP_GROUP`, whose value is a string giving the URL to access.
- [KEY_](https://gtk-rs.org/static.KEY_FILE_DESKTOP_KEY_VERSION.html)- FILE_ - DESKTOP_ - KEY_ - VERSION
- A key under `GLib::KEY_FILE_DESKTOP_GROUP`, whose value is a string giving the version of the Desktop Entry Specification used for the desktop entry file.
- [KEY_](https://gtk-rs.org/static.KEY_FILE_DESKTOP_TYPE_APPLICATION.html)- FILE_ - DESKTOP_ - TYPE_ - APPLICATION
- The value of the `GLib::KEY_FILE_DESKTOP_KEY_TYPE`, key for desktop entries representing applications.
- [KEY_](https://gtk-rs.org/static.KEY_FILE_DESKTOP_TYPE_DIRECTORY.html)- FILE_ - DESKTOP_ - TYPE_ - DIRECTORY
- The value of the `GLib::KEY_FILE_DESKTOP_KEY_TYPE`, key for desktop entries representing directories.
- [KEY_](https://gtk-rs.org/static.KEY_FILE_DESKTOP_TYPE_LINK.html)- FILE_ - DESKTOP_ - TYPE_ - LINK
- The value of the `GLib::KEY_FILE_DESKTOP_KEY_TYPE`, key for desktop entries representing links to documents.
- [OPTION_](https://gtk-rs.org/static.OPTION_REMAINING.html)- REMAINING
- If a long option in the main group has this name, it is not treated as a
regular option. Instead it collects all non-option arguments which would
otherwise be left in `argv`. The option must be of type`OptionArg::Callback``OptionArg::StringArray``OptionArg::FilenameArray`
- [STR_](https://gtk-rs.org/static.STR_DELIMITERS.html)- DELIMITERS
- The standard delimiters, used in `strdelimit()`.
- [TEST_](https://gtk-rs.org/static.TEST_OPTION_ISOLATE_DIRS.html)- OPTION_ - ISOLATE_ - DIRS - `v2_60`
- A value that can be passed as an option to `test_init()`.
- [TEST_](https://gtk-rs.org/static.TEST_OPTION_NONFATAL_ASSERTIONS.html)- OPTION_ - NONFATAL_ - ASSERTIONS - `v2_84`
- A value that can be passed as an option to `test_init()`.
- [TEST_](https://gtk-rs.org/static.TEST_OPTION_NO_PRGNAME.html)- OPTION_ - NO_ - PRGNAME - `v2_84`
- A value that can be passed as an option to `test_init()`.
- [URI_](https://gtk-rs.org/static.URI_RESERVED_CHARS_GENERIC_DELIMITERS.html)- RESERVED_ - CHARS_ - GENERIC_ - DELIMITERS
- Generic delimiters characters as defined in
[RFC 3986](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc3986). Includes`:/?#[]@`.
- [URI_](https://gtk-rs.org/static.URI_RESERVED_CHARS_SUBCOMPONENT_DELIMITERS.html)- RESERVED_ - CHARS_ - SUBCOMPONENT_ - DELIMITERS
- Subcomponent delimiter characters as defined in
[RFC 3986](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc3986). Includes`!$&'()*+,;=`.

## Functions[§](https://gtk-rs.org#functions)

- [access](https://gtk-rs.org/fn.access.html)
- A wrapper for the POSIX access() function. This function is used to test a pathname for one or several of read, write or execute permissions, or just existence.
- [application_](https://gtk-rs.org/fn.application_name.html)- name
- Gets a human-readable name for the application, as set by
g_set_application_name(). This name should be localized if
possible, and is intended for display to the user.  Contrast with
g_get_prgname(), which gets a non-localized name. If
g_set_application_name() has not been called, returns the result of
g_get_prgname() (which may be `None`
- [base64_](https://gtk-rs.org/fn.base64_decode.html)- decode
- Decode a sequence of Base-64 encoded text into binary data. Note that the returned binary data is not necessarily zero-terminated, so it should not be used as a character string.
- [base64_](https://gtk-rs.org/fn.base64_encode.html)- encode
- Encode a sequence of binary data into its Base-64 stringified representation.
- [casefold](https://gtk-rs.org/fn.casefold.html)
- [charset](https://gtk-rs.org/fn.charset.html)
- Obtain the character set for the current locale.
- [check_](https://gtk-rs.org/fn.check_version.html)- version
- Checks that the GLib library in use is compatible with the given version.
- [child_](https://gtk-rs.org/fn.child_watch_future.html)- watch_ - future - `futures`
- Create a `Future`that will resolve once the child process with the given pid exits
- [child_](https://gtk-rs.org/fn.child_watch_future_with_priority.html)- watch_ - future_ - with_ - priority - `futures`
- Create a `Future`that will resolve once the child process with the given pid exits
- [codeset](https://gtk-rs.org/fn.codeset.html)
- Gets the character set for the current locale.
- [compute_](https://gtk-rs.org/fn.compute_checksum_for_bytes.html)- checksum_ - for_ - bytes
- Computes the checksum for a binary @data. This is a convenience wrapper for g_checksum_new(), g_checksum_get_string() and g_checksum_free().
- [compute_](https://gtk-rs.org/fn.compute_checksum_for_data.html)- checksum_ - for_ - data
- Computes the checksum for a binary @data of @length. This is a convenience wrapper for g_checksum_new(), g_checksum_get_string() and g_checksum_free().
- [compute_](https://gtk-rs.org/fn.compute_checksum_for_string.html)- checksum_ - for_ - string
- [compute_](https://gtk-rs.org/fn.compute_hmac_for_bytes.html)- hmac_ - for_ - bytes
- Computes the HMAC for a binary @data. This is a convenience wrapper for g_hmac_new(), g_hmac_get_string() and g_hmac_unref().
- [compute_](https://gtk-rs.org/fn.compute_hmac_for_data.html)- hmac_ - for_ - data
- Computes the HMAC for a binary @data of @length. This is a convenience wrapper for g_hmac_new(), g_hmac_get_string() and g_hmac_unref().
- [console_](https://gtk-rs.org/fn.console_charset.html)- charset - `v2_62`

- [convert](https://gtk-rs.org/fn.convert.html)
- Converts a string from one character set to another.
- [convert_](https://gtk-rs.org/fn.convert_with_fallback.html)- with_ - fallback
- Converts a string from one character set to another, possibly including fallback sequences for characters not representable in the output. Note that it is not guaranteed that the specification for the fallback sequences in @fallback will be honored. Some systems may do an approximate conversion from @from_codeset to @to_codeset in their iconv() functions, in which case GLib will simply return that approximate conversion.
- [current_](https://gtk-rs.org/fn.current_dir.html)- dir
- Gets the current directory.
- [dcgettext](https://gtk-rs.org/fn.dcgettext.html)
- This is a variant of g_dgettext() that allows specifying a locale
category instead of always using `LC_MESSAGES`. See g_dgettext() for more information about how this functions differs from calling dcgettext() directly.
- [dgettext](https://gtk-rs.org/fn.dgettext.html)
- This function is a wrapper of dgettext() which does not translate the message if the default domain as set with textdomain() has no translations for the current locale.
- [dngettext](https://gtk-rs.org/fn.dngettext.html)
- This function is a wrapper of dngettext() which does not translate the message if the default domain as set with textdomain() has no translations for the current locale.
- [dpgettext](https://gtk-rs.org/fn.dpgettext.html)
- This function is a variant of g_dgettext() which supports a disambiguating message context. GNU gettext uses the ‘\004’ character to separate the message context and message id in @msgctxtid. If 0 is passed as @msgidoffset, this function will fall back to trying to use the deprecated convention of using “|” as a separation character.
- [dpgettext2](https://gtk-rs.org/fn.dpgettext2.html)
- This function is a variant of g_dgettext() which supports a disambiguating message context. GNU gettext uses the ‘\004’ character to separate the message context and message id in @msgctxtid.
- [environ](https://gtk-rs.org/fn.environ.html)
- Gets the list of environment variables for the current process.
- [environ_](https://gtk-rs.org/fn.environ_getenv.html)- getenv
- [file_](https://gtk-rs.org/fn.file_get_contents.html)- get_ - contents
- Reads an entire file into allocated memory, with good error checking.
- [file_](https://gtk-rs.org/fn.file_open_tmp.html)- open_ - tmp - Unix
- Opens a file for writing in the preferred directory for temporary files (as returned by g_get_tmp_dir()).

- Writes all of @contents to a file named @filename. This is a convenience
wrapper around calling g_file_set_contents_full() with `flags`set to`G_FILE_SET_CONTENTS_CONSISTENT | G_FILE_SET_CONTENTS_ONLY_EXISTING`and`mode`set to`0666`.
- [file_](https://gtk-rs.org/fn.file_set_contents_full.html)- set_ - contents_ - full - `v2_66`
- Writes all of @contents to a file named @filename, with good error checking. If a file called @filename already exists it will be overwritten.
- [filename_](https://gtk-rs.org/fn.filename_charsets.html)- charsets
- Determines the preferred character sets used for filenames. The first character set from the @charsets is the filename encoding, the subsequent character sets are used when trying to generate a displayable representation of a filename, see g_filename_display_name().
- [filename_](https://gtk-rs.org/fn.filename_display_basename.html)- display_ - basename
- Returns the display basename for the particular filename, guaranteed to be valid UTF-8. The display name might not be identical to the filename, for instance there might be problems converting it to UTF-8, and some files can be translated in the display.
- [filename_](https://gtk-rs.org/fn.filename_display_name.html)- display_ - name
- Converts a filename into a valid UTF-8 string. The conversion is
not necessarily reversible, so you should keep the original around
and use the return value of this function only for display purposes.
Unlike g_filename_to_utf8(), the result is guaranteed to be non-`None`
- [filename_](https://gtk-rs.org/fn.filename_from_uri.html)- from_ - uri
- Converts an escaped ASCII-encoded URI to a local filename in the encoding used for filenames.
- [filename_](https://gtk-rs.org/fn.filename_from_utf8.html)- from_ - utf8
- Converts a string from UTF-8 to the encoding GLib uses for
filenames. Note that on Windows GLib uses UTF-8 for filenames;
on other platforms, this function indirectly depends on the
[current locale](https://gtk-rs.org/running.html#locale).
- [filename_](https://gtk-rs.org/fn.filename_to_uri.html)- to_ - uri
- Converts an absolute filename to an escaped ASCII-encoded URI, with the path component following Section 3.3. of RFC 2396.
- [filename_](https://gtk-rs.org/fn.filename_to_utf8.html)- to_ - utf8
- Converts a string which is in the encoding used by GLib for
filenames into a UTF-8 string. Note that on Windows GLib uses UTF-8
for filenames; on other platforms, this function indirectly depends on
the [current locale](https://gtk-rs.org/running.html#locale).
- [find_](https://gtk-rs.org/fn.find_program_in_path.html)- program_ - in_ - path
- Locates the first executable named @program in the user’s path, in the
same way that execvp() would locate it. Returns an allocated string
with the absolute path name, or `None``None`
- [format_](https://gtk-rs.org/fn.format_size.html)- size
- Formats a size (for example the size of a file) into a human readable string. Sizes are rounded to the nearest size prefix (kB, MB, GB) and are displayed rounded to the nearest tenth. E.g. the file size 3292528 bytes will be converted into the string “3.2 MB”. The returned string is UTF-8, and may use a non-breaking space to separate the number and units, to ensure they aren’t separated when line wrapped.
- [format_](https://gtk-rs.org/fn.format_size_full.html)- size_ - full
- Formats a size.

- [hostname_](https://gtk-rs.org/fn.hostname_to_unicode.html)- to_ - unicode

- [locale_](https://gtk-rs.org/fn.locale_to_utf8.html)- to_ - utf8
- Converts a string which is in the encoding used for strings by

- [locale_](https://gtk-rs.org/fn.locale_variants.html)- variants
- Returns a list of derived variants of @locale, which can be used to

`setlocale(3)`

[148](https://gtk-rs.org#148)    /// Creates a new closure around a Rust closure.
[149](https://gtk-rs.org#149)    ///
[150](https://gtk-rs.org#150)    /// Note that [`RustClosure`] provides more convenient and non-unsafe API for invoking
[151](https://gtk-rs.org#151)    /// closures. This type mostly exists for FFI interop.
[152](https://gtk-rs.org#152)    ///
[153](https://gtk-rs.org#153)    /// # Panics
[154](https://gtk-rs.org#154)    ///
[155](https://gtk-rs.org#155)    /// Invoking the closure with wrong argument types or returning the wrong return value type
[156](https://gtk-rs.org#156)    /// will panic.
[157](https://gtk-rs.org#157)    ///
[158](https://gtk-rs.org#158)    ///
[159](https://gtk-rs.org#159)    /// # Example
[160](https://gtk-rs.org#160)    ///
[161](https://gtk-rs.org#161)    /// ```
[162](https://gtk-rs.org#162)    /// use glib::prelude::*;
[163](https://gtk-rs.org#163)    ///
[164](https://gtk-rs.org#164)    /// let closure = glib::Closure::new(|values| {
[165](https://gtk-rs.org#165)    ///     let x = values[0].get::<i32>().unwrap();
[166](https://gtk-rs.org#166)    ///     Some((x + 1).to_value())
[167](https://gtk-rs.org#167)    /// });
[168](https://gtk-rs.org#168)    ///
[169](https://gtk-rs.org#169)    /// // Invoking non-Rust closures is unsafe because of possibly missing
[170](https://gtk-rs.org#170)    /// // argument and return value type checks.
[171](https://gtk-rs.org#171)    /// let res = unsafe {
[172](https://gtk-rs.org#172)    ///     closure
[173](https://gtk-rs.org#173)    ///         .invoke_with_values(glib::Type::I32, &[1i32.to_value()])
[174](https://gtk-rs.org#174)    ///         .and_then(|v| v.get::<i32>().ok())
[175](https://gtk-rs.org#175)    ///         .expect("Invalid return value")
[176](https://gtk-rs.org#176)    /// };
[177](https://gtk-rs.org#177)    ///
[178](https://gtk-rs.org#178)    /// assert_eq!(res, 2);
[179](https://gtk-rs.org#179)    /// ```
[180](https://gtk-rs.org#180)    #[doc(alias = "g_closure_new")]

[182](https://gtk-rs.org#182)        unsafe { Self::[new_unsafe](https://gtk-rs.org#213-290)([callback](https://gtk-rs.org#181)) }

[295](https://gtk-rs.org#295)    /// For invalidated closures this returns the "default" value of the return type.
[296](https://gtk-rs.org#296)    ///
[297](https://gtk-rs.org#297)    /// # Safety
[298](https://gtk-rs.org#298)    ///
[299](https://gtk-rs.org#299)    /// The argument types and return value type must match the ones expected by the closure or
[300](https://gtk-rs.org#300)    /// otherwise the behaviour is undefined.
[301](https://gtk-rs.org#301)    ///
[302](https://gtk-rs.org#302)    /// Closures created from Rust via e.g. [`Closure::new`] will panic on type mismatches but

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#impl-RustClosure)

### impl [RustClosure](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.RustClosure.html)

Creates a new closure around a Rust closure.

See [ glib::closure!](https://gtk-rs.org/macro.closure.html) for a way to create a closure with concrete
types.

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#panics)Panics

Invoking the closure with wrong argument types or returning the wrong return value type will panic.

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#example)Example

```
use glib::prelude::*;
let closure = glib::RustClosure::new(|values| {
    let x = values[0].get::<i32>().unwrap();
    Some((x + 1).to_value())
});
assert_eq!(
    closure.invoke::<i32>(&[&1i32]),
    2,
);
```
Creates a new closure around a Rust closure.

See [ glib::closure_local!](https://gtk-rs.org/macro.closure_local.html) for a way to create a closure with
concrete types.

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#panics-1)Panics

Invoking the closure with wrong argument types or returning the wrong return value type will panic.

Invoking the closure from a different thread than this one will panic.

[Source](https://gtk-rs.org/src/glib/closure.rs.html#90-99)#### pub fn [invoke](https://gtk-rs.org#method.invoke)<R: [TryFromClosureReturnValue](https://gtk-rs.org/trait.TryFromClosureReturnValue.html)>(&self, values: &[&dyn [ToValue](https://gtk-rs.org/value/trait.ToValue.html)]) -> R

[Source](https://gtk-rs.org/src/glib/closure.rs.html#90-99)

#### pub fn [invoke](https://gtk-rs.org#method.invoke)<R: [TryFromClosureReturnValue](https://gtk-rs.org/trait.TryFromClosureReturnValue.html)>(&self, values: &[&dyn [ToValue](https://gtk-rs.org/value/trait.ToValue.html)]) -> R

Invokes the closure with the given arguments.

For invalidated closures this returns the “default” value of the return type. For nullable
types this is `None`, which means that e.g. requesting `R = String` will panic will `R = Option<String>` will return `None`.

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#panics-2)Panics

The argument types and return value type must match the ones expected by the closure or otherwise this function panics.

Invokes the closure with the given arguments.

For invalidated closures this returns the “default” value of the return type.

# ParamSpecBoxed in glib - Rust

`pub struct ParamSpecBoxed { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

A #GParamSpec derived structure that contains the meta data for boxed properties.

GLib type: Shared boxed type with reference counted clone semantics.

If this `ParamSpec` does not have a nickname, the nickname of its redirect target is returned if it has one.
Otherwise, `self.name()` is returned.

#### pub fn [redirect_target](https://gtk-rs.org#method.redirect_target)(&self) -> [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<[ParamSpec](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.ParamSpec.html)>

If the paramspec redirects operations to another paramspec, returns that paramspec. Redirect is used typically for providing a new implementation of a property in a derived type while preserving all the properties from the parent type. Redirection is established by creating a property of type #GParamSpecOverride. See g_object_class_override_property() for an example of the use of this capability.

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#returns-5)Returns

paramspec to which requests on this
paramspec should be redirected, or [ None](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html#variant.None) if none.

[2961](#2961)    fn none_value() {
[2962](#2962)        const CLONG_NONE: libc::c_long = -1;
[2963](#2963)
[2964](#2964)        #[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
[2965](#2965)        struct SpecialU32(u32);
[2966](#2966)        impl IntoGlib for SpecialU32 {
[2967](#2967)            type GlibType = libc::c_uint;
[2968](#2968)            fn into_glib(self) -> libc::c_uint {
[2969](#2969)                self.0 as libc::c_uint
[2970](#2970)            }
[2971](#2971)        }
[2972](#2972)        impl OptionIntoGlib for SpecialU32 {
[2973](#2973)            const GLIB_NONE: Self::GlibType = CLONG_NONE as libc::c_uint;
[2974](#2974)        }
[2975](#2975)
[2976](#2976)        assert_eq!(SpecialU32(0).into_glib(), 0);
[2977](#2977)        assert_eq!(SpecialU32(42).into_glib(), 42);
[2978](#2978)        assert_eq!(Some(SpecialU32(0)).into_glib(), 0);
[2979](#2979)        assert_eq!(Some(SpecialU32(42)).into_glib(), 42);
[2980](#2980)        assert_eq!(
[2981](#2981)            Option::None::<SpecialU32>.into_glib(),
[2982](#2982)            SpecialU32::GLIB_NONE
[2983](#2983)        );
[2984](#2984)
[2985](#2985)        impl TryFromGlib<libc::c_uint> for SpecialU32 {
[2986](#2986)            type Error = GlibNoneError;
[2987](#2987)            #[allow(clippy::unnecessary_cast)]
[2988](#2988)            unsafe fn try_from_glib(val: libc::c_uint) -> Result<Self, GlibNoneError> {
[2989](#2989)                if val == SpecialU32::GLIB_NONE {
[2990](#2990)                    return Err(GlibNoneError);
[2991](#2991)                }
[2992](#2992)
[2993](#2993)                Ok(SpecialU32(val as u32))
[2994](#2994)            }
[2995](#2995)        }
[2996](#2996)

[2998](#2998)        assert_eq!(unsafe { SpecialU32::try_from_glib(42) }, Ok(SpecialU32(42)));
[2999](#2999)        assert_eq!(

[3001](#3001)            Err(GlibNoneError)
[3002](#3002)        );

[3038](#3038)
[3039](#3039)        #[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
[3040](#3040)        struct SpecialU32(u32);
[3041](#3041)        impl IntoGlib for SpecialU32 {
[3042](#3042)            type GlibType = libc::c_long;
[3043](#3043)            fn into_glib(self) -> libc::c_long {
[3044](#3044)                self.0 as libc::c_long
[3045](#3045)            }
[3046](#3046)        }
[3047](#3047)        impl OptionIntoGlib for SpecialU32 {
[3048](#3048)            const GLIB_NONE: Self::GlibType = -1;
[3049](#3049)        }
[3050](#3050)
[3051](#3051)        assert_eq!(SpecialU32(0).into_glib(), 0);
[3052](#3052)        assert_eq!(SpecialU32(42).into_glib(), 42);
[3053](#3053)        assert_eq!(Some(SpecialU32(42)).into_glib(), 42);
[3054](#3054)        assert_eq!(
[3055](#3055)            Option::None::<SpecialU32>.into_glib(),
[3056](#3056)            SpecialU32::GLIB_NONE
[3057](#3057)        );
[3058](#3058)
[3059](#3059)        impl TryFromGlib<libc::c_long> for SpecialU32 {
[3060](#3060)            type Error = GlibNoneOrInvalidError<TryFromIntError>;
[3061](#3061)            unsafe fn try_from_glib(
[3062](#3062)                val: libc::c_long,
[3063](#3063)            ) -> Result<Self, GlibNoneOrInvalidError<TryFromIntError>> {
[3064](#3064)                if val == SpecialU32::GLIB_NONE {
[3065](#3065)                    return Err(GlibNoneOrInvalidError::None);
[3066](#3066)                }
[3067](#3067)
[3068](#3068)                Ok(SpecialU32(u32::try_from(val)?))
[3069](#3069)            }
[3070](#3070)        }
[3071](#3071)
[3072](#3072)        assert_eq!(unsafe { SpecialU32::try_from_glib(0) }, Ok(SpecialU32(0)));
[3073](#3073)        assert_eq!(unsafe { SpecialU32::try_from_glib(42) }, Ok(SpecialU32(42)));
[3074](#3074)        assert!(
[3075](#3075)            unsafe { SpecialU32::try_from_glib(SpecialU32::GLIB_NONE) }
[3076](#3076)                .unwrap_err()
[3077](#3077)                .is_none()
[3078](#3078)        );
[3079](#3079)        assert!(
[3080](#3080)            unsafe { SpecialU32::try_from_glib(-42) }
[3081](#3081)                .unwrap_err()
[3082](#3082)                .is_invalid()
[3083](#3083)        );
[3084](#3084)
[3085](#3085)        assert_eq!(
[3086](#3086)            unsafe { Result::<Option<SpecialU32>, _>::from_glib(0) },
[3087](#3087)            Ok(Some(SpecialU32(0)))
[3088](#3088)        );
[3089](#3089)        assert_eq!(

[3092](#3092)        );
[3093](#3093)        assert_eq!(
[3094](#3094)            unsafe { Result::<Option<SpecialU32>, _>::from_glib(SpecialU32::GLIB_NONE) },

# FromGlibPtrNone in glib::translate - Rust

Source: https://gtk-rs.org/gtk-rs-core/stable/latest/docs/glib/translate/trait.FromGlibPtrNone.html

`pub trait FromGlibPtrNone<P: `[Ptr](https://gtk-rs.org/trait.Ptr.html)>: [Sized](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/marker/trait.Sized.html) {
    // Required method
    unsafe fn [from_glib_none](https://gtk-rs.org#tymethod.from_glib_none)(ptr: P) -> Self;
}## Expand description

Translate from a pointer type which is annotated with `transfer none`.
The resulting value is referenced at least once, by the bindings.

This is suitable for floating references, which become strong references.
It is also suitable for acquiring non-gobject values, like `gchar*`.

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#safety)Safety

The implementation of this trait should acquire a reference to the value
in a way appropriate to the type,
e.g. by increasing the reference count or copying.
Values obtained using this trait must be properly released on `drop()`
by the implementing type.

For more information, refer to module level documentation.

## Required Methods[§](https://gtk-rs.org#required-methods)

## Dyn Compatibility[§](https://gtk-rs.org#dyn-compatibility)

This trait is **not** [dyn compatible](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/reference/items/traits.html#dyn-compatibility).

*In older versions of Rust, dyn compatibility was called "object safety".*

## Implementations on Foreign Types[§](https://gtk-rs.org#foreign-impls)

## Implementors[§](https://gtk-rs.org#implementors)

# FromGlibPtrFull in glib::translate - Rust

Source: https://gtk-rs.org/gtk-rs-core/stable/latest/docs/glib/translate/trait.FromGlibPtrFull.html

`pub trait FromGlibPtrFull<P: `[Ptr](https://gtk-rs.org/trait.Ptr.html)>: [Sized](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/marker/trait.Sized.html) {
    // Required method
    unsafe fn [from_glib_full](https://gtk-rs.org#tymethod.from_glib_full)(ptr: P) -> Self;
}## Expand description

Translate from a pointer type which is annotated with `transfer full`.
This transfers the ownership of the value to the Rust side.

Because ownership can only be transferred if something is already referenced, this is unsuitable for floating references.

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#safety)Safety

The implementation of this trait should not alter the reference count
or make copies of the underlying value.
Values obtained using this trait must be properly released on `drop()`
by the implementing type.

For more information, refer to module level documentation.

## Required Methods[§](https://gtk-rs.org#required-methods)

## Dyn Compatibility[§](https://gtk-rs.org#dyn-compatibility)

This trait is **not** [dyn compatible](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/reference/items/traits.html#dyn-compatibility).

# Property in glib::property - Rust

Source: https://gtk-rs.org/gtk-rs-core/stable/latest/docs/glib/property/trait.Property.html

```
pub trait Property {
    type
```
[Value](https://gtk-rs.org#associatedtype.Value): [HasParamSpec](https://gtk-rs.org/trait.HasParamSpec.html);
}## Expand description

A type that can be used as a property. It covers every type which have an associated `ParamSpec`
(`HasParamSpec`) and some useful types wrapping `HasParamSpec`.
The definition is recursive, so you can nest many `Property`s together. The final `ParamSpec` will
be the one of the innermost type

## Required Associated Types[§](https://gtk-rs.org#required-associated-types)

## Dyn Compatibility[§](https://gtk-rs.org#dyn-compatibility)

This trait **is** [dyn compatible](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/reference/items/traits.html#dyn-compatibility).

*In older versions of Rust, dyn compatibility was called "object safety".*

---

#### pub fn [is](https://gtk-rs.org#method.is)<T: [StaticType](https://gtk-rs.org/types/trait.StaticType.html)>(&self) -> [bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html)

Returns `true` if the type of the value corresponds to `T`
or is a sub-type of `T`.

Returns `true` if the type of the value corresponds to `type_`
or is a sub-type of `type_`.

Tries to transform the value into a value of the target type Tries to cast the contents of @self into a type appropriate to store in @dest_value.

If a transformation is not possible, @dest_value is not modified.

For example, this could transform a `G_TYPE_INT` value into a `G_TYPE_FLOAT`
value.

Performing transformations between value types might incur precision loss. Especially transformations into strings might reveal seemingly arbitrary results and the format of particular transformations to strings is not guaranteed over time.

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#dest_value)`dest_value`

target value

true on success; false otherwise

# TransparentType in glib::translate - Rust

Source: https://gtk-rs.org/gtk-rs-core/stable/latest/docs/glib/translate/trait.TransparentType.html

## Expand description

Trait for types that have the same memory representation as their FFI type.

Values of types implementing this trait can be transmuted directly to the FFI type, references to pointers to the FFI type.

## Required Associated Types[§](https://gtk-rs.org#required-associated-types)

## Dyn Compatibility[§](https://gtk-rs.org#dyn-compatibility)

This trait is **not** [dyn compatible](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/reference/items/traits.html#dyn-compatibility).

*In older versions of Rust, dyn compatibility was called "object safety".*

# glib::value - Rust

Source: https://gtk-rs.org/gtk-rs-core/stable/latest/docs/glib/value/index.html

## Expand description

`Value` binding and helper traits.

The type of a [ Value](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.Value.html) is dynamic in that it generally
isn’t known at compile time but once created a

`Value` can’t change its
type.[ SendValue](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.SendValue.html) is a version of

[that can only store types that implement](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.Value.html)

`Value``Send` and as such implements `Send` itself. It
dereferences to `Value` so it can be used everywhere `Value` references are accepted.Supported types are `bool`, `i8`, `u8`, `i32`, `u32`, `i64`, `u64`, `f32`,
`f64`, `String` and objects (`T: IsA<Object>`).

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#examples)Examples

```
use glib::prelude::*; // or `use gtk::prelude::*;`
use glib::Value;
// Value implement From<&i32>, From<&str> and From<Option<&str>>.
// Another option is the `ToValue` trait.
let mut num = 10.to_value();
let mut hello = Value::from("Hello!");
let none: Option<&str> = None;
let str_none = none.to_value();
// `is` tests the type of the value.
assert!(num.is::<i32>());
assert!(hello.is::<String>());
// `get` tries to get an optional value of the specified type
// and returns an `Err` if the type doesn't match.
assert_eq!(num.get(), Ok(10));
assert!(num.get::<String>().is_err());
assert_eq!(hello.get(), Ok(String::from("Hello!")));
assert_eq!(hello.get::<String>(), Ok(String::from("Hello!")));
assert_eq!(str_none.get::<Option<String>>(), Ok(None));
```

# TypeValueTable in glib - Rust

Source: https://gtk-rs.org/gtk-rs-core/stable/latest/docs/glib/struct.TypeValueTable.html

`pub struct TypeValueTable(/* private fields */);`## Expand description

-
`'i'`: Integers, passed as`collect_values[].v_int`- `'l'`: Longs, passed as- `collect_values[].v_long`
- `'d'`: Doubles, passed as- `collect_values[].v_double`
- `'p'`: Pointers, passed as- `collect_values[].v_pointer`
 It should be noted that for variable argument list construction, ANSI C promotes every type smaller than an integer to an int, and floats to doubles. So for collection of short int or char, `'i'`needs to be used, and for collection of floats`'d'`. The #GTypeValueTable provides the functions required by the #GValue implementation, to serve as a container for values of a type.

[Source](https://gtk-rs.org/src/glib/gstring.rs.html#193-195)#### pub const fn [as_bytes_with_nul](https://gtk-rs.org#method.as_bytes_with_nul)(&self) -> &[[u8](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u8.html)] [ⓘ](https://gtk-rs.org)

Converts this GLib string to a byte slice containing the trailing 0 byte.

This function is the equivalent of [ GStr::as_bytes](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.GStr.html#method.as_bytes) except that it will retain the
trailing nul terminator instead of chopping it off.

Converts this GLib string to a byte slice.

The returned slice will **not** contain the trailing nul terminator that this GLib
string has.

Returns the inner pointer to this GLib string.

The returned pointer will be valid for as long as `self` is, and points to a contiguous
region of memory terminated with a 0 byte to represent the end of the string.

**WARNING**

The returned pointer is read-only; writing to it (including passing it to C code that writes to it) causes undefined behavior. It is your responsibility to make sure that the underlying memory is not freed too early.
