The [pattern](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/str/pattern/index.html) can be a `&str`, [ char](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.char.html), a slice of

[s, or a function or closure that determines if a character matches.](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.char.html)

`char`[§](https://gtk-rs.org#iterator-behavior-5)Iterator behavior

The returned iterator will not be double ended, because it is not efficient to support.

For splitting from the front, the [ splitn](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html#method.splitn) method can be used.

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#examples-30)Examples

Simple patterns:

```
let v: Vec<&str> = "Mary had a little lamb".rsplitn(3, ' ').collect();
assert_eq!(v, ["lamb", "little", "Mary had a"]);
let v: Vec<&str> = "lionXXtigerXleopard".rsplitn(3, 'X').collect();
assert_eq!(v, ["leopard", "tiger", "lionX"]);
let v: Vec<&str> = "lion::tiger::leopard".rsplitn(2, "::").collect();
assert_eq!(v, ["leopard", "lion::tiger"]);
```
A more complex pattern, using a closure:

```
let v: Vec<&str> = "abc1defXghi".rsplitn(2, |c| c == '1' || c == 'X').collect();
assert_eq!(v, ["ghi", "abc1def"]);
```

Because `parse` is so general, it can cause problems with type
inference. As such, `parse` is one of the few times you’ll see
the syntax affectionately known as the ‘turbofish’: `::<>`. This
helps the inference algorithm understand specifically which type
you’re trying to parse into.

`parse` can parse into any type that implements the [ FromStr](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/str/traits/trait.FromStr.html) trait.

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#errors)Errors

Will return [ Err](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/str/traits/trait.FromStr.html#associatedtype.Err) if it’s not possible to parse this string slice into
the desired type.

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#examples-52)Examples

Basic usage:

```
let four: u32 = "4".parse().unwrap();
assert_eq!(4, four);
```
Using the ‘turbofish’ instead of annotating `four`:

```
let four = "4".parse::<u32>();
assert_eq!(Ok(4), four);
```
Failing to parse:

```
let nope = "j".parse::<u32>();
assert!(nope.is_err());
```

[Source](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/src/core/str/mod.rs.html#2907)#### pub fn [eq_ignore_case_unnormalized](https://gtk-rs.org#method.eq_ignore_case_unnormalized)(&self, other: &[str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html)) -> [bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html)

`casefold`)

[Source](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/src/core/str/mod.rs.html#2907)

#### pub fn [eq_ignore_case_unnormalized](https://gtk-rs.org#method.eq_ignore_case_unnormalized)(&self, other: &[str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html)) -> [bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html)

`casefold`)Checks that two strings are a caseless match, according to
[Definition 144](https://www.unicode.org/versions/latest/core-spec/chapter-3/#G53513) in Chapter 3 of the Unicode Standard.

Same as `a.to_casefold_unnormalized() == b.to_casefold_unnormalized()`,
but without allocating. See that method’s documentation,
as well as [ char::to_casefold_unnormalized()](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.char.html#method.to_casefold_unnormalized),
for more information about case folding.

No [normalization](https://www.unicode.org/faq/normalization.html) (e.g. NFC) is performed, so visually and semantically identical strings
might still compare unequal. For example, `"Å"` (U+00C5 LATIN CAPITAL LETTER A WITH RING ABOVE)
is considered distinct from `"Å"` (A followed by U+030A COMBINING RING ABOVE),
even though Unicode considers them canonically equivalent.

In addition, this method is independent of language/locale, so the special behavior of I/ı/İ/i in Turkish and Azeri is not handled.

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#examples-55)Examples

```
#![feature(casefold)]
assert!("Ferris".eq_ignore_case_unnormalized("FERRIS"));
assert!("Ferrös".eq_ignore_case_unnormalized("FERRÖS"));
assert!("ẞ".eq_ignore_case_unnormalized("ss"));
```
No NFC [normalization](https://www.unicode.org/faq/normalization.html) is performed:

```
#![feature(casefold)]
// These two strings are visually and semantically identical...
let comp = "Å";
let decomp = "Å";
// ... but not codepoint-for-codepoint equal.
assert_eq!(comp, "\u{C5}");
assert_eq!(decomp, "A\u{030A}");
// Their case-foldings are likewise unequal:
assert!(!comp.eq_ignore_case_unnormalized(decomp));
```

Returns `None` if `substr` does not point within `self`.

Unlike [ str::find](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html#method.find),

**this does not search through the string**. Instead, it uses pointer arithmetic to find where in the string

`substr` is derived from.This is useful for extending [ str::split](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html#method.split) and similar methods.

Note that this method may return false positives (typically either
`Some(0..0)` or `Some(self.len()..self.len())`) if `substr` is a
zero-length `str` that points at the beginning or end of another,
independent, `str`.

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#examples-62)Examples

```
use core::range::Range;
let data = "a, b, b, a";
let mut iter = data.split(", ").map(|s| data.substr_range(s).unwrap());
assert_eq!(iter.next(), Some(Range { start: 0, end: 1 }));
assert_eq!(iter.next(), Some(Range { start: 3, end: 4 }));
assert_eq!(iter.next(), Some(Range { start: 6, end: 7 }));
assert_eq!(iter.next(), Some(Range { start: 9, end: 10 }));
```
Returns the same string as a string slice `&str`.

This method is redundant when used directly on `&str`, but
it helps dereferencing other string-like types to string slices,
for example references to `Box<str>` or `Arc<str>`.

1.0.0 · [Source](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/src/alloc/str.rs.html#308) Available on **non-**`no_global_oom_handling` only.

[Source](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/src/alloc/str.rs.html#308)

**non-**only.

`no_global_oom_handling`Replaces all matches of a pattern with another string.

`replace` creates a new [ String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html), and copies the data from this string slice into it.
While doing so, it attempts to find matches of a pattern. If it finds any, it
replaces them with the replacement string slice.

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#examples-63)Examples

```
let s = "this is old";
assert_eq!("this is new", s.replace("old", "new"));
assert_eq!("than an old", s.replace("is", "an"));
```
When the pattern doesn’t match, it returns this string slice as [ String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html):

```
let s = "this is old";
assert_eq!(s, s.replace("cookie monster", "little lamb"));
```

While doing so, it attempts to find matches of a pattern. If it finds any, it
replaces them with the replacement string slice at most

`count` times.[§](https://gtk-rs.org#examples-64)Examples

```
let s = "foo foo 123 foo";
assert_eq!("new new 123 foo", s.replacen("foo", "new", 2));
assert_eq!("faa fao 123 foo", s.replacen('o', "a", 3));
assert_eq!("foo foo new23 foo", s.replacen(char::is_numeric, "new", 1));
```
When the pattern doesn’t match, it returns this string slice as [ String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html):

```
let s = "this is old";
assert_eq!(s, s.replacen("cookie monster", "little lamb", 10));
```
1.2.0 · [Source](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/src/alloc/str.rs.html#433)#### pub fn [to_lowercase](https://gtk-rs.org#method.to_lowercase)(&self) -> [String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html)

 Available on **non-**`no_global_oom_handling` only.

[Source](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/src/alloc/str.rs.html#433)

#### pub fn [to_lowercase](https://gtk-rs.org#method.to_lowercase)(&self) -> [String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html)

**non-**only.

`no_global_oom_handling`Returns the lowercase equivalent of this string slice, as a new [ String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html).

‘Lowercase’ is defined according to the terms of
[Chapter 3 (Conformance)](https://www.unicode.org/versions/latest/core-spec/chapter-3/#G34432)
of the Unicode standard.

Since some characters can expand into multiple characters when changing
the case, this function returns a [ String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html) instead of modifying the
parameter in-place.

Unlike [ char::to_lowercase()](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.char.html#method.to_lowercase), this method fully handles the context-dependent
casing of Greek sigma. However, like that method, it does not handle locale-specific
casing, like Turkish and Azeri I/ı/İ/i. See its documentation
for more information.

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#examples-65)Examples

Basic usage:

```
let s = "HELLO WORLD";
assert_eq!("hello world", s.to_lowercase());
```
Tricky examples, with sigma:

```
let sigma = "Σ";
assert_eq!("σ", sigma.to_lowercase());
// but at the end of a word, it's ς, not σ:
let odysseus = "ὈΔΥΣΣΕΎΣ";
assert_eq!("ὀδυσσεύς", odysseus.to_lowercase());
let odysseus_king_of_ithaca = "Ο ΟΔΥΣΣΈΑΣ ΒΑΣΙΛΙΆΣ ΤΗΣ ΙΘΆΚΗΣ";
assert_eq!("ο οδυσσέας βασιλιάς της ιθάκης", odysseus_king_of_ithaca.to_lowercase());
```
Languages without case are not changed:

```
let new_year = "农历新年";
assert_eq!(new_year, new_year.to_lowercase());
```
[Source](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/src/alloc/str.rs.html#554)#### pub fn [word_to_titlecase](https://gtk-rs.org#method.word_to_titlecase)(&self) -> [String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html)

`titlecase`)Available on **non-**`no_global_oom_handling` only.

[Source](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/src/alloc/str.rs.html#554)

#### pub fn [word_to_titlecase](https://gtk-rs.org#method.word_to_titlecase)(&self) -> [String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html)

`titlecase`)**non-**only.

`no_global_oom_handling`Returns the titlecase equivalent of this string slice,
which is assumed to represent a single word,
as a new [ String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html).

Essentially, this consists of uppercasing the first cased letter
(with [ char::to_titlecase()](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.char.html#method.to_titlecase)), and lowercasing everything that follows.

‘Titlecase’ is defined according to the terms of
[Chapter 3 (Conformance)](https://www.unicode.org/versions/latest/core-spec/chapter-3/#G34082)
of the Unicode standard.

Since some characters can expand into multiple characters when changing
the case, this function returns a [ String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html) instead of modifying the
parameter in-place.

Unlike [ char::to_lowercase()](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.char.html#method.to_lowercase), this method fully handles the context-dependent
casing of Greek sigma. However, like that method, it does not handle locale-specific
casing, like Turkish and Azeri I/ı/İ/i. See its documentation
for more information.

This method does not perform any kind of word segmentation.

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#examples-66)Examples

Basic usage:

```
#![feature(titlecase)]
let s = "HELLO WORLD";
assert_eq!("Hello world", s.word_to_titlecase());
```
The first *cased* letter is uppercased:

```
#![feature(titlecase)]
let the_night_before_christmas = "'twas";
assert_eq!("'Twas", the_night_before_christmas.word_to_titlecase());
```
Languages without case are not changed:

```
#![feature(titlecase)]
let new_year = "农历新年";
assert_eq!(new_year, new_year.word_to_titlecase());
```
Georgian uppercase (“Mtavruli”) letters are not used in titlecase:

```
#![feature(titlecase)]
let georgian = "ერთობაშია";
assert_eq!(georgian, georgian.word_to_titlecase());
```
No word segmentation is performed, so only the first cased letter in the whole string gets uppercased:

```
#![feature(titlecase)]
let blazingly_fast = "ferris and I";
assert_eq!("Ferris and i", blazingly_fast.word_to_titlecase());
```
Tricky examples, with sigma:

```
#![feature(titlecase)]
let odysseus = "ὈΔΥΣΣΕΎΣ";
assert_eq!("Ὀδυσσεύς", odysseus.word_to_titlecase());
let odysseus_king_of_ithaca = "Ο ΟΔΥΣΣΈΑΣ ΒΑΣΙΛΙΆΣ ΤΗΣ ΙΘΆΚΗΣ";
assert_eq!("Ο οδυσσέας βασιλιάς της ιθάκης", odysseus_king_of_ithaca.word_to_titlecase());
```

[Source](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/src/alloc/str.rs.html#742)#### pub fn [to_casefold_unnormalized](https://gtk-rs.org#method.to_casefold_unnormalized)(&self) -> [String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html)

`casefold`)Available on **non-**`no_global_oom_handling` only.

[Source](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/src/alloc/str.rs.html#742)

#### pub fn [to_casefold_unnormalized](https://gtk-rs.org#method.to_casefold_unnormalized)(&self) -> [String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html)

`casefold`)**non-**only.

`no_global_oom_handling`Returns the case-folded equivalent of this string slice, as a new [ String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html).

Case folding is a transformation, mostly matching lowercase, that is meant to be used for case-insensitive string comparisons. Case-folded strings should not usually be exposed directly to users.

For the precise specification of case folding, see
[Chapter 3 (Conformance)](https://www.unicode.org/versions/latest/core-spec/chapter-3/#G63737)
of the Unicode standard.

Since some characters can expand into multiple characters when case folding,
this function returns a [ String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html) instead of modifying the parameter in-place.

No [normalization](https://www.unicode.org/faq/normalization.html) (e.g. NFC) is performed, so visually and semantically identical strings
might still casefold differently. For example, `"Å"` (U+00C5 LATIN CAPITAL LETTER A WITH RING ABOVE)
is considered distinct from `"Å"` (A followed by U+030A COMBINING RING ABOVE),
even though Unicode considers them canonically equivalent.

Like [ char::to_casefold_unnormalized()](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.char.html#method.to_casefold_unnormalized) this method does not handle language-specific
casing, like Turkish and Azeri I/ı/İ/i. See that method’s documentation
for more information.

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#examples-68)Examples

Basic usage:

```
#![feature(casefold)]
let s0 = "HELLO";
let s1 = "Hello";
assert_eq!(s0.to_casefold_unnormalized(), s1.to_casefold_unnormalized());
assert_eq!(s0.to_casefold_unnormalized(), "hello")
```
Scripts without case are not changed:

```
#![feature(casefold)]
let new_year = "农历新年";
assert_eq!(new_year, new_year.to_casefold_unnormalized());
```
One character can become multiple:

```
#![feature(casefold)]
let s0 = "TSCHÜẞ";
let s1 = "TSCHÜSS";
let s2 = "tschüß";
assert_eq!(s0.to_casefold_unnormalized(), s1.to_casefold_unnormalized());
assert_eq!(s0.to_casefold_unnormalized(), s2.to_casefold_unnormalized());
assert_eq!(s0.to_casefold_unnormalized(), "tschüss");
```
No NFC [normalization](https://www.unicode.org/faq/normalization.html) is performed:

```
#![feature(casefold)]
// These two strings are visually and semantically identical...
let comp = "Å";
let decomp = "Å";
// ... but not codepoint-for-codepoint equal.
assert_eq!(comp, "\u{C5}");
assert_eq!(decomp, "A\u{030A}");
// Their case-foldings are likewise unequal:
assert_eq!(comp.to_casefold_unnormalized(), "\u{E5}");
assert_eq!(decomp.to_casefold_unnormalized(), "a\u{030A}");
```

[19](https://gtk-rs.org#19)        /// Guarantee file consistency: after a crash,
[20](https://gtk-rs.org#20)        ///   either the old version of the file or the new version of the file will be
[21](https://gtk-rs.org#21)        ///   available, but not a mixture. On Unix systems this equates to an `fsync()`

[28](https://gtk-rs.org#28)        ///   an `fsync()` on the file (if [`CONSISTENT`][Self::CONSISTENT] is unset), or
[29](https://gtk-rs.org#29)        ///   the effects of [`CONSISTENT`][Self::CONSISTENT] plus an `fsync()` on the
[30](https://gtk-rs.org#30)        ///   directory containing the file after calling `rename()`.
[31](https://gtk-rs.org#31)        #[doc(alias = "G_FILE_SET_CONTENTS_DURABLE")]
[32](https://gtk-rs.org#32)        const DURABLE = ffi::G_FILE_SET_CONTENTS_DURABLE as _;
[33](https://gtk-rs.org#33)        /// Only apply consistency and durability
[34](https://gtk-rs.org#34)        ///   guarantees if the file already exists. This may speed up file operations
[35](https://gtk-rs.org#35)        ///   if the file doesn’t currently exist, but may result in a corrupted version
[36](https://gtk-rs.org#36)        ///   of the new file if the system crashes while writing it.
[37](https://gtk-rs.org#37)        #[doc(alias = "G_FILE_SET_CONTENTS_ONLY_EXISTING")]

[415](https://gtk-rs.org#415)    pub struct [OptionFlags](https://gtk-rs.org/glib/struct.OptionFlags.html): u32 {
[416](https://gtk-rs.org#416)        /// No flags.
[417](https://gtk-rs.org#417)        #[doc(alias = "G_OPTION_FLAG_NONE")]
[418](https://gtk-rs.org#418)        const NONE = ffi::G_OPTION_FLAG_NONE as _;
[419](https://gtk-rs.org#419)        /// The option doesn't appear in `--help` output.
[420](https://gtk-rs.org#420)        #[doc(alias = "G_OPTION_FLAG_HIDDEN")]
[421](https://gtk-rs.org#421)        const HIDDEN = ffi::G_OPTION_FLAG_HIDDEN as _;
[422](https://gtk-rs.org#422)        /// The option appears in the main section of the
[423](https://gtk-rs.org#423)        ///   `--help` output, even if it is defined in a group.
[424](https://gtk-rs.org#424)        #[doc(alias = "G_OPTION_FLAG_IN_MAIN")]
[425](https://gtk-rs.org#425)        const IN_MAIN = ffi::G_OPTION_FLAG_IN_MAIN as _;
[426](https://gtk-rs.org#426)        /// For options of the [`OptionArg::None`][crate::OptionArg::None] kind, this
[427](https://gtk-rs.org#427)        ///   flag indicates that the sense of the option is reversed. i.e. [`false`] will
[428](https://gtk-rs.org#428)        ///   be stored into the argument rather than [`true`].
[429](https://gtk-rs.org#429)        #[doc(alias = "G_OPTION_FLAG_REVERSE")]
[430](https://gtk-rs.org#430)        const REVERSE = ffi::G_OPTION_FLAG_REVERSE as _;
[431](https://gtk-rs.org#431)        /// For options of the [`OptionArg::Callback`][crate::OptionArg::Callback] kind,
[432](https://gtk-rs.org#432)        ///   this flag indicates that the callback does not take any argument
[433](https://gtk-rs.org#433)        ///   (like a [`OptionArg::None`][crate::OptionArg::None] option). Since 2.8
[434](https://gtk-rs.org#434)        #[doc(alias = "G_OPTION_FLAG_NO_ARG")]
[435](https://gtk-rs.org#435)        const NO_ARG = ffi::G_OPTION_FLAG_NO_ARG as _;
[436](https://gtk-rs.org#436)        /// For options of the [`OptionArg::Callback`][crate::OptionArg::Callback]
[437](https://gtk-rs.org#437)        ///   kind, this flag indicates that the argument should be passed to the
[438](https://gtk-rs.org#438)        ///   callback in the GLib filename encoding rather than UTF-8. Since 2.8
[439](https://gtk-rs.org#439)        #[doc(alias = "G_OPTION_FLAG_FILENAME")]
[440](https://gtk-rs.org#440)        const FILENAME = ffi::G_OPTION_FLAG_FILENAME as _;
[441](https://gtk-rs.org#441)        /// For options of the [`OptionArg::Callback`][crate::OptionArg::Callback]
[442](https://gtk-rs.org#442)        ///   kind, this flag indicates that the argument supply is optional.
[443](https://gtk-rs.org#443)        ///   If no argument is given then data of `GOptionParseFunc` will be
[444](https://gtk-rs.org#444)        ///   set to NULL. Since 2.8
[445](https://gtk-rs.org#445)        #[doc(alias = "G_OPTION_FLAG_OPTIONAL_ARG")]
[446](https://gtk-rs.org#446)        const OPTIONAL_ARG = ffi::G_OPTION_FLAG_OPTIONAL_ARG as _;
[447](https://gtk-rs.org#447)        /// This flag turns off the automatic conflict
[448](https://gtk-rs.org#448)        ///   resolution which prefixes long option names with `groupname-` if
[449](https://gtk-rs.org#449)        ///   there is a conflict. This option should only be used in situations
[450](https://gtk-rs.org#450)        ///   where aliasing is necessary to model some legacy commandline interface.
[451](https://gtk-rs.org#451)        ///   It is not safe to use this option, unless all option groups are under
[452](https://gtk-rs.org#452)        ///   your direct control. Since 2.8.

[486](https://gtk-rs.org#486)    /// Flags specifying compile-time options.
[487](https://gtk-rs.org#487)    #[derive([Clone](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/clone/derive.Clone.html), [Copy](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/marker/derive.Copy.html), [Debug](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/fmt/macros/derive.Debug.html), [PartialEq](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/cmp/derive.PartialEq.html), [Eq](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/cmp/derive.Eq.html), [Hash](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/hash/macros/derive.Hash.html))]
[488](https://gtk-rs.org#488)    #[doc(alias = "GRegexCompileFlags")]
[489](https://gtk-rs.org#489)    pub struct [RegexCompileFlags](https://gtk-rs.org/glib/struct.RegexCompileFlags.html): u32 {
[490](https://gtk-rs.org#490)        /// No special options set. Since: 2.74
[491](https://gtk-rs.org#491)        #[doc(alias = "G_REGEX_DEFAULT")]
[492](https://gtk-rs.org#492)        const DEFAULT = ffi::G_REGEX_DEFAULT as _;
[493](https://gtk-rs.org#493)        /// Letters in the pattern match both upper- and
[494](https://gtk-rs.org#494)        ///   lowercase letters. This option can be changed within a pattern
[495](https://gtk-rs.org#495)        ///   by a `(?i)` option setting.
[496](https://gtk-rs.org#496)        #[doc(alias = "G_REGEX_CASELESS")]
[497](https://gtk-rs.org#497)        const CASELESS = ffi::G_REGEX_CASELESS as _;
[498](https://gtk-rs.org#498)        /// By default, [type@GLib.Regex] treats the strings as consisting
[499](https://gtk-rs.org#499)        ///   of a single line of characters (even if it actually contains
[500](https://gtk-rs.org#500)        ///   newlines). The ‘start of line’ metacharacter (`^`) matches only
[501](https://gtk-rs.org#501)        ///   at the start of the string, while the ‘end of line’ metacharacter
[502](https://gtk-rs.org#502)        ///   (`$`) matches only at the end of the string, or before a terminating
[503](https://gtk-rs.org#503)        ///   newline (unless [flags@GLib.RegexCompileFlags.DOLLAR_ENDONLY] is set). When
[504](https://gtk-rs.org#504)        ///   [flags@GLib.RegexCompileFlags.MULTILINE] is set, the ‘start of line’ and
[505](https://gtk-rs.org#505)        ///   ‘end of line’ constructs match immediately following or immediately before
[506](https://gtk-rs.org#506)        ///   any newline in the string, respectively, as well as at the very start
[507](https://gtk-rs.org#507)        ///   and end. This can be changed within a pattern by a `(?m)` option
[508](https://gtk-rs.org#508)        ///   setting.
[509](https://gtk-rs.org#509)        #[doc(alias = "G_REGEX_MULTILINE")]
[510](https://gtk-rs.org#510)        const MULTILINE = ffi::G_REGEX_MULTILINE as _;
[511](https://gtk-rs.org#511)        /// A dot metacharacter (`.`) in the pattern matches all
[512](https://gtk-rs.org#512)        ///   characters, including newlines. Without it, newlines are excluded.
[513](https://gtk-rs.org#513)        ///   This option can be changed within a pattern by a `(?s)` option setting.
[514](https://gtk-rs.org#514)        #[doc(alias = "G_REGEX_DOTALL")]
[515](https://gtk-rs.org#515)        const DOTALL = ffi::G_REGEX_DOTALL as _;
[516](https://gtk-rs.org#516)        /// Whitespace data characters in the pattern are
[517](https://gtk-rs.org#517)        ///   totally ignored except when escaped or inside a character class.
[518](https://gtk-rs.org#518)        ///   Whitespace does not include the VT character (code 11). In addition,
[519](https://gtk-rs.org#519)        ///   characters between an unescaped `#` outside a character class and
[520](https://gtk-rs.org#520)        ///   the next newline character, inclusive, are also ignored. This can
[521](https://gtk-rs.org#521)        ///   be changed within a pattern by a `(?x)` option setting.
[522](https://gtk-rs.org#522)        #[doc(alias = "G_REGEX_EXTENDED")]
[523](https://gtk-rs.org#523)        const EXTENDED = ffi::G_REGEX_EXTENDED as _;
[524](https://gtk-rs.org#524)        /// The pattern is forced to be ‘anchored’, that is,
[525](https://gtk-rs.org#525)        ///   it is constrained to match only at the first matching point in the
[526](https://gtk-rs.org#526)        ///   string that is being searched. This effect can also be achieved by
[527](https://gtk-rs.org#527)        ///   appropriate constructs in the pattern itself such as the `^`
[528](https://gtk-rs.org#528)        ///   metacharacter.
[529](https://gtk-rs.org#529)        #[doc(alias = "G_REGEX_ANCHORED")]
[530](https://gtk-rs.org#530)        const ANCHORED = ffi::G_REGEX_ANCHORED as _;
[531](https://gtk-rs.org#531)        /// A dollar metacharacter (`$`) in the pattern
[532](https://gtk-rs.org#532)        ///   matches only at the end of the string. Without this option, a
[533](https://gtk-rs.org#533)        ///   dollar also matches immediately before the final character if
[534](https://gtk-rs.org#534)        ///   it is a newline (but not before any other newlines). This option
[535](https://gtk-rs.org#535)        ///   is ignored if [flags@GLib.RegexCompileFlags.MULTILINE] is set.
[536](https://gtk-rs.org#536)        #[doc(alias = "G_REGEX_DOLLAR_ENDONLY")]
[537](https://gtk-rs.org#537)        const DOLLAR_ENDONLY = ffi::G_REGEX_DOLLAR_ENDONLY as _;
[538](https://gtk-rs.org#538)        /// Inverts the ‘greediness’ of the quantifiers so that
[539](https://gtk-rs.org#539)        ///   they are not greedy by default, but become greedy if followed by `?`.
[540](https://gtk-rs.org#540)        ///   It can also be set by a `(?U)` option setting within the pattern.
[541](https://gtk-rs.org#541)        #[doc(alias = "G_REGEX_UNGREEDY")]
[542](https://gtk-rs.org#542)        const UNGREEDY = ffi::G_REGEX_UNGREEDY as _;
[543](https://gtk-rs.org#543)        /// Usually strings must be valid UTF-8 strings, using this
[544](https://gtk-rs.org#544)        ///   flag they are considered as a raw sequence of bytes.
[545](https://gtk-rs.org#545)        #[doc(alias = "G_REGEX_RAW")]
[546](https://gtk-rs.org#546)        const RAW = ffi::G_REGEX_RAW as _;
[547](https://gtk-rs.org#547)        /// Disables the use of numbered capturing
[548](https://gtk-rs.org#548)        ///   parentheses in the pattern. Any opening parenthesis that is not
[549](https://gtk-rs.org#549)        ///   followed by `?` behaves as if it were followed by `?:` but named
[550](https://gtk-rs.org#550)        ///   parentheses can still be used for capturing (and they acquire numbers
[551](https://gtk-rs.org#551)        ///   in the usual way).
[552](https://gtk-rs.org#552)        #[doc(alias = "G_REGEX_NO_AUTO_CAPTURE")]
[553](https://gtk-rs.org#553)        const NO_AUTO_CAPTURE = ffi::G_REGEX_NO_AUTO_CAPTURE as _;
[554](https://gtk-rs.org#554)        /// Since 2.74 and the port to pcre2, requests JIT
[555](https://gtk-rs.org#555)        ///   compilation, which, if the just-in-time compiler is available, further
[556](https://gtk-rs.org#556)        ///   processes a compiled pattern into machine code that executes much
[557](https://gtk-rs.org#557)        ///   faster. However, it comes at the cost of extra processing before the
[558](https://gtk-rs.org#558)        ///   match is performed, so it is most beneficial to use this when the same
[559](https://gtk-rs.org#559)        ///   compiled pattern is used for matching many times. Before 2.74 this
[560](https://gtk-rs.org#560)        ///   option used the built-in non-JIT optimizations in pcre1.
[561](https://gtk-rs.org#561)        #[doc(alias = "G_REGEX_OPTIMIZE")]
[562](https://gtk-rs.org#562)        const OPTIMIZE = ffi::G_REGEX_OPTIMIZE as _;
[563](https://gtk-rs.org#563)        /// Limits an unanchored pattern to match before (or at) the
[564](https://gtk-rs.org#564)        ///   first newline. Since: 2.34
[565](https://gtk-rs.org#565)        #[doc(alias = "G_REGEX_FIRSTLINE")]
[566](https://gtk-rs.org#566)        const FIRSTLINE = ffi::G_REGEX_FIRSTLINE as _;
[567](https://gtk-rs.org#567)        /// Names used to identify capturing subpatterns need not
[568](https://gtk-rs.org#568)        ///   be unique. This can be helpful for certain types of pattern when it
[569](https://gtk-rs.org#569)        ///   is known that only one instance of the named subpattern can ever be
[570](https://gtk-rs.org#570)        ///   matched.
[571](https://gtk-rs.org#571)        #[doc(alias = "G_REGEX_DUPNAMES")]
[572](https://gtk-rs.org#572)        const DUPNAMES = ffi::G_REGEX_DUPNAMES as _;
[573](https://gtk-rs.org#573)        /// Usually any newline character or character sequence is
[574](https://gtk-rs.org#574)        ///   recognized. If this option is set, the only recognized newline character
[575](https://gtk-rs.org#575)        ///   is `\r`.
[576](https://gtk-rs.org#576)        #[doc(alias = "G_REGEX_NEWLINE_CR")]
[577](https://gtk-rs.org#577)        const NEWLINE_CR = ffi::G_REGEX_NEWLINE_CR as _;
[578](https://gtk-rs.org#578)        /// Usually any newline character or character sequence is
[579](https://gtk-rs.org#579)        ///   recognized. If this option is set, the only recognized newline character
[580](https://gtk-rs.org#580)        ///   is `\n`.
[581](https://gtk-rs.org#581)        #[doc(alias = "G_REGEX_NEWLINE_LF")]
[582](https://gtk-rs.org#582)        const NEWLINE_LF = ffi::G_REGEX_NEWLINE_LF as _;
[583](https://gtk-rs.org#583)        #[doc(alias = "G_REGEX_NEWLINE_RESERVED1")]
[584](https://gtk-rs.org#584)        const NEWLINE_RESERVED1 = ffi::G_REGEX_NEWLINE_RESERVED1 as _;
[585](https://gtk-rs.org#585)    }

[606](https://gtk-rs.org#606)bitflags! {
[607](https://gtk-rs.org#607)    /// Flags specifying match-time options.
[608](https://gtk-rs.org#608)    #[derive([Clone](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/clone/derive.Clone.html), [Copy](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/marker/derive.Copy.html), [Debug](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/fmt/macros/derive.Debug.html), [PartialEq](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/cmp/derive.PartialEq.html), [Eq](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/cmp/derive.Eq.html), [Hash](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/hash/macros/derive.Hash.html))]
[609](https://gtk-rs.org#609)    #[doc(alias = "GRegexMatchFlags")]
[610](https://gtk-rs.org#610)    pub struct [RegexMatchFlags](https://gtk-rs.org/glib/struct.RegexMatchFlags.html): u32 {
[611](https://gtk-rs.org#611)        /// No special options set. Since: 2.74
[612](https://gtk-rs.org#612)        #[doc(alias = "G_REGEX_MATCH_DEFAULT")]
[613](https://gtk-rs.org#613)        const DEFAULT = ffi::G_REGEX_MATCH_DEFAULT as _;
[614](https://gtk-rs.org#614)        /// The pattern is forced to be ‘anchored’, that is,
[615](https://gtk-rs.org#615)        ///   it is constrained to match only at the first matching point in the
[616](https://gtk-rs.org#616)        ///   string that is being searched. This effect can also be achieved by
[617](https://gtk-rs.org#617)        ///   appropriate constructs in the pattern itself such as the `^`
[618](https://gtk-rs.org#618)        ///   metacharacter.
[619](https://gtk-rs.org#619)        #[doc(alias = "G_REGEX_MATCH_ANCHORED")]
[620](https://gtk-rs.org#620)        const ANCHORED = ffi::G_REGEX_MATCH_ANCHORED as _;
[621](https://gtk-rs.org#621)        /// Specifies that first character of the string is
[622](https://gtk-rs.org#622)        ///   not the beginning of a line, so the circumflex metacharacter should
[623](https://gtk-rs.org#623)        ///   not match before it. Setting this without
[624](https://gtk-rs.org#624)        ///   [flags@GLib.RegexCompileFlags.MULTILINE] (at
[625](https://gtk-rs.org#625)        ///   compile time) causes circumflex never to match. This option affects
[626](https://gtk-rs.org#626)        ///   only the behaviour of the circumflex metacharacter, it does not
[627](https://gtk-rs.org#627)        ///   affect `\A`.
[628](https://gtk-rs.org#628)        #[doc(alias = "G_REGEX_MATCH_NOTBOL")]
[629](https://gtk-rs.org#629)        const NOTBOL = ffi::G_REGEX_MATCH_NOTBOL as _;
[630](https://gtk-rs.org#630)        /// Specifies that the end of the subject string is
[631](https://gtk-rs.org#631)        ///   not the end of a line, so the dollar metacharacter should not match
[632](https://gtk-rs.org#632)        ///   it nor (except in multiline mode) a newline immediately before it.
[633](https://gtk-rs.org#633)        ///   Setting this without [flags@GLib.RegexCompileFlags.MULTILINE]
[634](https://gtk-rs.org#634)        ///   (at compile time) causes dollar never to match. This option affects only
[635](https://gtk-rs.org#635)        ///   the behaviour of the dollar metacharacter, it does not affect `\Z` or `\z`.
[636](https://gtk-rs.org#636)        #[doc(alias = "G_REGEX_MATCH_NOTEOL")]
[637](https://gtk-rs.org#637)        const NOTEOL = ffi::G_REGEX_MATCH_NOTEOL as _;
[638](https://gtk-rs.org#638)        /// An empty string is not considered to be a valid
[639](https://gtk-rs.org#639)        ///   match if this option is set. If there are alternatives in the pattern,
[640](https://gtk-rs.org#640)        ///   they are tried. If all the alternatives match the empty string, the
[641](https://gtk-rs.org#641)        ///   entire match fails. For example, if the pattern `a?b?` is applied to
[642](https://gtk-rs.org#642)        ///   a string not beginning with `a` or `b`, it matches the empty string
[643](https://gtk-rs.org#643)        ///   at the start of the string. With this flag set, this match is not
[644](https://gtk-rs.org#644)        ///   valid, so [type@GLib.Regex] searches further into the string for
[645](https://gtk-rs.org#645)        ///   occurrences of `a` or `b`.
[646](https://gtk-rs.org#646)        #[doc(alias = "G_REGEX_MATCH_NOTEMPTY")]
[647](https://gtk-rs.org#647)        const NOTEMPTY = ffi::G_REGEX_MATCH_NOTEMPTY as _;
[648](https://gtk-rs.org#648)        /// Turns on the partial matching feature, for more
[649](https://gtk-rs.org#649)        ///   documentation on partial matching see
[650](https://gtk-rs.org#650)        ///   [`MatchInfo::is_partial_match()`][crate::MatchInfo::is_partial_match()].
[651](https://gtk-rs.org#651)        #[doc(alias = "G_REGEX_MATCH_PARTIAL")]
[652](https://gtk-rs.org#652)        const PARTIAL = ffi::G_REGEX_MATCH_PARTIAL as _;
[653](https://gtk-rs.org#653)        /// Overrides the newline definition set when
[654](https://gtk-rs.org#654)        ///   creating a new [type@GLib.Regex], setting the `\r` character as line
[655](https://gtk-rs.org#655)        ///   terminator.
[656](https://gtk-rs.org#656)        #[doc(alias = "G_REGEX_MATCH_NEWLINE_CR")]
[657](https://gtk-rs.org#657)        const NEWLINE_CR = ffi::G_REGEX_MATCH_NEWLINE_CR as _;
[658](https://gtk-rs.org#658)        /// Overrides the newline definition set when
[659](https://gtk-rs.org#659)        ///   creating a new [type@GLib.Regex], setting the `\n` character as line
[660](https://gtk-rs.org#660)        ///   terminator.
[661](https://gtk-rs.org#661)        #[doc(alias = "G_REGEX_MATCH_NEWLINE_LF")]
[662](https://gtk-rs.org#662)        const NEWLINE_LF = ffi::G_REGEX_MATCH_NEWLINE_LF as _;
[663](https://gtk-rs.org#663)        /// Overrides the newline definition set when
[664](https://gtk-rs.org#664)        ///   creating a new [type@GLib.Regex], setting the `\r\n` character sequence as
[665](https://gtk-rs.org#665)        ///   line terminator.
[666](https://gtk-rs.org#666)        #[doc(alias = "G_REGEX_MATCH_NEWLINE_CRLF")]
[667](https://gtk-rs.org#667)        const NEWLINE_CRLF = ffi::G_REGEX_MATCH_NEWLINE_CRLF as _;
[668](https://gtk-rs.org#668)        /// Overrides the newline definition set when
[669](https://gtk-rs.org#669)        ///   creating a new [type@GLib.Regex], any Unicode newline sequence
[670](https://gtk-rs.org#670)        ///   is recognised as a newline. These are `\r`, `\n` and `\r\n`, and the
[671](https://gtk-rs.org#671)        ///   single characters U+000B LINE TABULATION, U+000C FORM FEED (FF),
[672](https://gtk-rs.org#672)        ///   U+0085 NEXT LINE (NEL), U+2028 LINE SEPARATOR and
[673](https://gtk-rs.org#673)        ///   U+2029 PARAGRAPH SEPARATOR.
[674](https://gtk-rs.org#674)        #[doc(alias = "G_REGEX_MATCH_NEWLINE_ANY")]
[675](https://gtk-rs.org#675)        const NEWLINE_ANY = ffi::G_REGEX_MATCH_NEWLINE_ANY as _;
[676](https://gtk-rs.org#676)        /// Overrides the newline definition set when
[677](https://gtk-rs.org#677)        ///   creating a new [type@GLib.Regex]; any `\r`, `\n`, or `\r\n` character
[678](https://gtk-rs.org#678)        ///   sequence is recognized as a newline. Since: 2.34
[679](https://gtk-rs.org#679)        #[doc(alias = "G_REGEX_MATCH_NEWLINE_ANYCRLF")]
[680](https://gtk-rs.org#680)        const NEWLINE_ANYCRLF = ffi::G_REGEX_MATCH_NEWLINE_ANYCRLF as _;
[681](https://gtk-rs.org#681)        /// Overrides the newline definition for `\R` set when
[682](https://gtk-rs.org#682)        ///   creating a new [type@GLib.Regex]; only `\r`, `\n`, or `\r\n` character
[683](https://gtk-rs.org#683)        ///   sequences are recognized as a newline by `\R`. Since: 2.34
[684](https://gtk-rs.org#684)        #[doc(alias = "G_REGEX_MATCH_BSR_ANYCRLF")]
[685](https://gtk-rs.org#685)        const BSR_ANYCRLF = ffi::G_REGEX_MATCH_BSR_ANYCRLF as _;
[686](https://gtk-rs.org#686)        /// Overrides the newline definition for `\R` set when
[687](https://gtk-rs.org#687)        ///   creating a new [type@GLib.Regex]; any Unicode newline characters or
[688](https://gtk-rs.org#688)        ///   character sequences are recognized as a newline by `\R`. These are `\r`,
[689](https://gtk-rs.org#689)        ///   `\n` and `\r\n`, and the single characters U+000B LINE TABULATION,
[690](https://gtk-rs.org#690)        ///   U+000C FORM FEED (FF), U+0085 NEXT LINE (NEL), U+2028 LINE SEPARATOR and
[691](https://gtk-rs.org#691)        ///   U+2029 PARAGRAPH SEPARATOR. Since: 2.34
[692](https://gtk-rs.org#692)        #[doc(alias = "G_REGEX_MATCH_BSR_ANY")]
[693](https://gtk-rs.org#693)        const BSR_ANY = ffi::G_REGEX_MATCH_BSR_ANY as _;
[694](https://gtk-rs.org#694)        /// An alias for [flags@GLib.RegexMatchFlags.PARTIAL].
[695](https://gtk-rs.org#695)        ///   Since: 2.34
[696](https://gtk-rs.org#696)        #[doc(alias = "G_REGEX_MATCH_PARTIAL_SOFT")]
[697](https://gtk-rs.org#697)        const PARTIAL_SOFT = ffi::G_REGEX_MATCH_PARTIAL_SOFT as _;
[698](https://gtk-rs.org#698)        /// Turns on the partial matching feature. In
[699](https://gtk-rs.org#699)        ///   contrast to [flags@GLib.RegexMatchFlags.PARTIAL_SOFT], this stops matching

[828](https://gtk-rs.org#828)        #[doc(alias = "G_URI_FLAGS_NONE")]

[830](https://gtk-rs.org#830)        /// Parse the URI more relaxedly than the
[831](https://gtk-rs.org#831)        ///     [RFC 3986](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc3986) grammar specifies,
[832](https://gtk-rs.org#832)        ///     fixing up or ignoring common mistakes in URIs coming from external
[833](https://gtk-rs.org#833)        ///     sources. This is also needed for some obscure URI schemes where `;`
[834](https://gtk-rs.org#834)        ///     separates the host from the path. Don’t use this flag unless you need to.
[835](https://gtk-rs.org#835)        #[doc(alias = "G_URI_FLAGS_PARSE_RELAXED")]

[838](https://gtk-rs.org#838)        ///     which will be separated from the username by `:`.
[839](https://gtk-rs.org#839)        #[doc(alias = "G_URI_FLAGS_HAS_PASSWORD")]
[840](https://gtk-rs.org#840)        const HAS_PASSWORD = ffi::G_URI_FLAGS_HAS_PASSWORD as _;
[841](https://gtk-rs.org#841)        /// The userinfo may contain additional
[842](https://gtk-rs.org#842)        ///     authentication-related parameters, which will be separated from

[844](https://gtk-rs.org#844)        #[doc(alias = "G_URI_FLAGS_HAS_AUTH_PARAMS")]
[845](https://gtk-rs.org#845)        const HAS_AUTH_PARAMS = ffi::G_URI_FLAGS_HAS_AUTH_PARAMS as _;
[846](https://gtk-rs.org#846)        /// When parsing a URI, this indicates that `%`-encoded
[847](https://gtk-rs.org#847)        ///     characters in the userinfo, path, query, and fragment fields
[848](https://gtk-rs.org#848)        ///     should not be decoded. (And likewise the host field if

[850](https://gtk-rs.org#850)        ///     that you have already `%`-encoded the components, and so #GUri
[851](https://gtk-rs.org#851)        ///     should not do any encoding itself.
[852](https://gtk-rs.org#852)        #[doc(alias = "G_URI_FLAGS_ENCODED")]
[853](https://gtk-rs.org#853)        const ENCODED = ffi::G_URI_FLAGS_ENCODED as _;
[854](https://gtk-rs.org#854)        /// The host component should not be assumed to be a
[855](https://gtk-rs.org#855)        ///     DNS hostname or IP address (for example, for `smb` URIs with NetBIOS
[856](https://gtk-rs.org#856)        ///     hostnames).
[857](https://gtk-rs.org#857)        #[doc(alias = "G_URI_FLAGS_NON_DNS")]
[858](https://gtk-rs.org#858)        const NON_DNS = ffi::G_URI_FLAGS_NON_DNS as _;

[860](https://gtk-rs.org#860)        ///     field only.
[861](https://gtk-rs.org#861)        #[doc(alias = "G_URI_FLAGS_ENCODED_QUERY")]
[862](https://gtk-rs.org#862)        const ENCODED_QUERY = ffi::G_URI_FLAGS_ENCODED_QUERY as _;
[863](https://gtk-rs.org#863)        /// Same as [`ENCODED`][Self::ENCODED], for the path only.
[864](https://gtk-rs.org#864)        #[doc(alias = "G_URI_FLAGS_ENCODED_PATH")]
[865](https://gtk-rs.org#865)        const ENCODED_PATH = ffi::G_URI_FLAGS_ENCODED_PATH as _;
[866](https://gtk-rs.org#866)        /// Same as [`ENCODED`][Self::ENCODED], for the
[867](https://gtk-rs.org#867)        ///     fragment only.
[868](https://gtk-rs.org#868)        #[doc(alias = "G_URI_FLAGS_ENCODED_FRAGMENT")]
[869](https://gtk-rs.org#869)        const ENCODED_FRAGMENT = ffi::G_URI_FLAGS_ENCODED_FRAGMENT as _;
[870](https://gtk-rs.org#870)        /// A scheme-based normalization will be applied.
[871](https://gtk-rs.org#871)        ///     For example, when parsing an HTTP URI changing omitted path to `/` and
[872](https://gtk-rs.org#872)        ///     omitted port to `80`; and when building a URI, changing empty path to `/`
[873](https://gtk-rs.org#873)        ///     and default port `80`). This only supports a subset of known schemes. (Since: 2.68)
[874](https://gtk-rs.org#874)        #[doc(alias = "G_URI_FLAGS_SCHEME_NORMALIZE")]

[19](https://gtk-rs.org#19)    /// with comments.
[20](https://gtk-rs.org#20)    ///
[21](https://gtk-rs.org#21)    /// **⚠️ The following code is in txt ⚠️**
[22](https://gtk-rs.org#22)    ///
[23](https://gtk-rs.org#23)    /// ```txt
[24](https://gtk-rs.org#24)    /// # this is just an example
[25](https://gtk-rs.org#25)    /// # there can be comments before the first group
[26](https://gtk-rs.org#26)    ///
[27](https://gtk-rs.org#27)    /// [First Group]
[28](https://gtk-rs.org#28)    ///
[29](https://gtk-rs.org#29)    /// Name=Key File Example\tthis value shows\nescaping
[30](https://gtk-rs.org#30)    ///
[31](https://gtk-rs.org#31)    /// # localized strings are stored in multiple key-value pairs
[32](https://gtk-rs.org#32)    /// Welcome=Hello
[33](https://gtk-rs.org#33)    /// Welcome[de]=Hallo
[34](https://gtk-rs.org#34)    /// Welcome[fr_FR]=Bonjour
[35](https://gtk-rs.org#35)    /// Welcome[it]=Ciao
[36](https://gtk-rs.org#36)    ///
[37](https://gtk-rs.org#37)    /// [Another Group]
[38](https://gtk-rs.org#38)    ///
[39](https://gtk-rs.org#39)    /// Numbers=2;20;-200;0
[40](https://gtk-rs.org#40)    ///
[41](https://gtk-rs.org#41)    /// Booleans=true;false;true;true
[42](https://gtk-rs.org#42)    /// ```
[43](https://gtk-rs.org#43)    ///
[44](https://gtk-rs.org#44)    /// Lines beginning with a `#` and blank lines are considered comments.
[45](https://gtk-rs.org#45)    ///
[46](https://gtk-rs.org#46)    /// Groups are started by a header line containing the group name enclosed
[47](https://gtk-rs.org#47)    /// in `[` and `]`, and ended implicitly by the start of the next group or
[48](https://gtk-rs.org#48)    /// the end of the file. Each key-value pair must be contained in a group.
[49](https://gtk-rs.org#49)    ///
[50](https://gtk-rs.org#50)    /// Key-value pairs generally have the form `key=value`, with the exception
[51](https://gtk-rs.org#51)    /// of localized strings, which have the form `key[locale]=value`, with a
[52](https://gtk-rs.org#52)    /// locale identifier of the form `lang_COUNTRY@MODIFIER` where `COUNTRY`
[53](https://gtk-rs.org#53)    /// and `MODIFIER` are optional. As a special case, the locale `C` is associated
[54](https://gtk-rs.org#54)    /// with the untranslated pair `key=value` (since GLib 2.84). Space before and
[55](https://gtk-rs.org#55)    /// after the `=` character is ignored. Newline, tab, carriage return and
[56](https://gtk-rs.org#56)    /// backslash characters in value are escaped as `\n`, `\t`, `\r`, and `\\\\`,
[57](https://gtk-rs.org#57)    /// respectively. To preserve leading spaces in values, these can also be escaped
[58](https://gtk-rs.org#58)    /// as `\s`.
[59](https://gtk-rs.org#59)    ///
[60](https://gtk-rs.org#60)    /// Key files can store strings (possibly with localized variants), integers,
[61](https://gtk-rs.org#61)    /// booleans and lists of these. Lists are separated by a separator character,
[62](https://gtk-rs.org#62)    /// typically `;` or `,`. To use the list separator character in a value in
[63](https://gtk-rs.org#63)    /// a list, it has to be escaped by prefixing it with a backslash.
[64](https://gtk-rs.org#64)    ///
[65](https://gtk-rs.org#65)    /// This syntax is obviously inspired by the .ini files commonly met
[66](https://gtk-rs.org#66)    /// on Windows, but there are some important differences:
[67](https://gtk-rs.org#67)    ///
[68](https://gtk-rs.org#68)    /// - .ini files use the `;` character to begin comments,
[69](https://gtk-rs.org#69)    ///   key files use the `#` character.
[70](https://gtk-rs.org#70)    ///
[71](https://gtk-rs.org#71)    /// - Key files do not allow for ungrouped keys meaning only
[72](https://gtk-rs.org#72)    ///   comments can precede the first group.
[73](https://gtk-rs.org#73)    ///
[74](https://gtk-rs.org#74)    /// - Key files are always encoded in UTF-8.
[75](https://gtk-rs.org#75)    ///
[76](https://gtk-rs.org#76)    /// - Key and Group names are case-sensitive. For example, a group called
[77](https://gtk-rs.org#77)    ///   `[GROUP]` is a different from `[group]`.
[78](https://gtk-rs.org#78)    ///
[79](https://gtk-rs.org#79)    /// - .ini files don’t have a strongly typed boolean entry type,
[80](https://gtk-rs.org#80)    ///    they only have `GetProfileInt()`. In key files, only
[81](https://gtk-rs.org#81)    ///    `true` and `false` (in lower case) are allowed.
[82](https://gtk-rs.org#82)    ///
[83](https://gtk-rs.org#83)    /// Note that in contrast to the
[84](https://gtk-rs.org#84)    /// [Desktop Entry Specification](https://specifications.freedesktop.org/desktop-entry-spec/latest/),
[85](https://gtk-rs.org#85)    /// groups in key files may contain the same key multiple times; the last entry wins.
[86](https://gtk-rs.org#86)    /// Key files may also contain multiple groups with the same name; they are merged
[87](https://gtk-rs.org#87)    /// together. Another difference is that keys and group names in key files are not
[88](https://gtk-rs.org#88)    /// restricted to ASCII characters.
[89](https://gtk-rs.org#89)    ///
[90](https://gtk-rs.org#90)    /// Here is an example of loading a key file and reading a value:
[91](https://gtk-rs.org#91)    ///
[92](https://gtk-rs.org#92)    /// **⚠️ The following code is in c ⚠️**
[93](https://gtk-rs.org#93)    ///
[94](https://gtk-rs.org#94)    /// ```c
[95](https://gtk-rs.org#95)    /// g_autoptr(GError) error = NULL;
[96](https://gtk-rs.org#96)    /// g_autoptr(GKeyFile) key_file = g_key_file_new ();
[97](https://gtk-rs.org#97)    ///
[98](https://gtk-rs.org#98)    /// if (!g_key_file_load_from_file (key_file, "key-file.ini", flags, &error))
[99](https://gtk-rs.org#99)    ///   {
[100](https://gtk-rs.org#100)    ///     if (!g_error_matches (error, G_FILE_ERROR, G_FILE_ERROR_NOENT))
[101](https://gtk-rs.org#101)    ///       g_warning ("Error loading key file: %s", error->message);
[102](https://gtk-rs.org#102)    ///     return;
[103](https://gtk-rs.org#103)    ///   }
[104](https://gtk-rs.org#104)    ///
[105](https://gtk-rs.org#105)    /// g_autofree gchar *val = g_key_file_get_string (key_file, "Group Name", "SomeKey", &error);
[106](https://gtk-rs.org#106)    /// if (val == NULL &&
[107](https://gtk-rs.org#107)    ///     !g_error_matches (error, G_KEY_FILE_ERROR, G_KEY_FILE_ERROR_KEY_NOT_FOUND))
[108](https://gtk-rs.org#108)    ///   {
[109](https://gtk-rs.org#109)    ///     g_warning ("Error finding key in key file: %s", error->message);
[110](https://gtk-rs.org#110)    ///     return;
[111](https://gtk-rs.org#111)    ///   }
[112](https://gtk-rs.org#112)    /// else if (val == NULL)
[113](https://gtk-rs.org#113)    ///   {
[114](https://gtk-rs.org#114)    ///     // Fall back to a default value.
[115](https://gtk-rs.org#115)    ///     val = g_strdup ("default-value");
[116](https://gtk-rs.org#116)    ///   }
[117](https://gtk-rs.org#117)    /// ```
[118](https://gtk-rs.org#118)    ///
[119](https://gtk-rs.org#119)    /// Here is an example of creating and saving a key file:
[120](https://gtk-rs.org#120)    ///
[121](https://gtk-rs.org#121)    /// **⚠️ The following code is in c ⚠️**
[122](https://gtk-rs.org#122)    ///
[123](https://gtk-rs.org#123)    /// ```c
[124](https://gtk-rs.org#124)    /// g_autoptr(GKeyFile) key_file = g_key_file_new ();
[125](https://gtk-rs.org#125)    /// const gchar *val = …;
[126](https://gtk-rs.org#126)    /// g_autoptr(GError) error = NULL;
[127](https://gtk-rs.org#127)    ///
[128](https://gtk-rs.org#128)    /// g_key_file_set_string (key_file, "Group Name", "SomeKey", val);
[129](https://gtk-rs.org#129)    ///
[130](https://gtk-rs.org#130)    /// // Save as a file.
[131](https://gtk-rs.org#131)    /// if (!g_key_file_save_to_file (key_file, "key-file.ini", &error))
[132](https://gtk-rs.org#132)    ///   {
[133](https://gtk-rs.org#133)    ///     g_warning ("Error saving key file: %s", error->message);
[134](https://gtk-rs.org#134)    ///     return;
[135](https://gtk-rs.org#135)    ///   }
[136](https://gtk-rs.org#136)    ///
[137](https://gtk-rs.org#137)    /// // Or store to a GBytes for use elsewhere.
[138](https://gtk-rs.org#138)    /// gsize data_len;
[139](https://gtk-rs.org#139)    /// g_autofree guint8 *data = (guint8 *) g_key_file_to_data (key_file, &data_len, &error);
[140](https://gtk-rs.org#140)    /// if (data == NULL)
[141](https://gtk-rs.org#141)    ///   {
[142](https://gtk-rs.org#142)    ///     g_warning ("Error saving key file: %s", error->message);
[143](https://gtk-rs.org#143)    ///     return;
[144](https://gtk-rs.org#144)    ///   }
[145](https://gtk-rs.org#145)    /// g_autoptr(GBytes) bytes = g_bytes_new_take (g_steal_pointer (&data), data_len);
[146](https://gtk-rs.org#146)    /// ```
[147](https://gtk-rs.org#147)    #[derive([Debug](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/fmt/macros/derive.Debug.html), [PartialEq](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/cmp/derive.PartialEq.html), [Eq](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/cmp/derive.Eq.html), [PartialOrd](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/cmp/derive.PartialOrd.html), [Ord](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/cmp/derive.Ord.html), [Hash](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/hash/macros/derive.Hash.html))]

# KeyFile in glib - Rust

Source: https://gtk-rs.org/gtk-rs-core/stable/latest/docs/glib/struct.KeyFile.html

`pub struct KeyFile { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

`GKeyFile` parses .ini-like config files.

`GKeyFile` lets you parse, edit or create files containing groups of
key-value pairs, which we call ‘key files’ for lack of a better name.
Several freedesktop.org specifications use key files. For example, the
[Desktop Entry Specification](https://specifications.freedesktop.org/desktop-entry-spec/latest/)
and the [Icon Theme Specification](https://specifications.freedesktop.org/icon-theme-spec/latest/).

The syntax of key files is described in detail in the
[Desktop Entry Specification](https://specifications.freedesktop.org/desktop-entry-spec/latest/),
here is a quick summary: Key files consists of groups of key-value pairs, interspersed
with comments.

**⚠️ The following code is in txt ⚠️**

```
# this is just an example
# there can be comments before the first group
[First Group]
Name=Key File Example\tthis value shows\nescaping
# localized strings are stored in multiple key-value pairs
Welcome=Hello
Welcome[de]=Hallo
Welcome[fr_FR]=Bonjour
Welcome[it]=Ciao
[Another Group]
Numbers=2;20;-200;0
Booleans=true;false;true;true
```
Lines beginning with a `#` and blank lines are considered comments.

Groups are started by a header line containing the group name enclosed
in `[` and `]`, and ended implicitly by the start of the next group or
the end of the file. Each key-value pair must be contained in a group.

Key-value pairs generally have the form `key=value`, with the exception
of localized strings, which have the form `key[locale]=value`, with a
locale identifier of the form `lang_COUNTRY@MODIFIER` where `COUNTRY`
and `MODIFIER` are optional. As a special case, the locale `C` is associated
with the untranslated pair `key=value` (since GLib 2.84). Space before and
after the `=` character is ignored. Newline, tab, carriage return and
backslash characters in value are escaped as `\n`, `\t`, `\r`, and `\\\\`,
respectively. To preserve leading spaces in values, these can also be escaped
as `\s`.

Key files can store strings (possibly with localized variants), integers,
booleans and lists of these. Lists are separated by a separator character,
typically `;` or `,`. To use the list separator character in a value in
a list, it has to be escaped by prefixing it with a backslash.

This syntax is obviously inspired by the .ini files commonly met on Windows, but there are some important differences:

-
.ini files use the `;`character to begin comments, key files use the`#`character.
-
Key files do not allow for ungrouped keys meaning only comments can precede the first group.
-
Key files are always encoded in UTF-8.
-
Key and Group names are case-sensitive. For example, a group called `[GROUP]`is a different from`[group]`.
-
.ini files don’t have a strongly typed boolean entry type, they only have `GetProfileInt()`. In key files, only`true`and`false`(in lower case) are allowed.

Note that in contrast to the
[Desktop Entry Specification](https://specifications.freedesktop.org/desktop-entry-spec/latest/),
groups in key files may contain the same key multiple times; the last entry wins.
Key files may also contain multiple groups with the same name; they are merged
together. Another difference is that keys and group names in key files are not
restricted to ASCII characters.

Here is an example of loading a key file and reading a value:

**⚠️ The following code is in c ⚠️**

```
g_autoptr(GError) error = NULL;
g_autoptr(GKeyFile) key_file = g_key_file_new ();
if (!g_key_file_load_from_file (key_file, "key-file.ini", flags, &error))
  {
    if (!g_error_matches (error, G_FILE_ERROR, G_FILE_ERROR_NOENT))
      g_warning ("Error loading key file: %s", error->message);
    return;
  }
g_autofree gchar *val = g_key_file_get_string (key_file, "Group Name", "SomeKey", &error);
if (val == NULL &&
    !g_error_matches (error, G_KEY_FILE_ERROR, G_KEY_FILE_ERROR_KEY_NOT_FOUND))
  {
    g_warning ("Error finding key in key file: %s", error->message);
    return;
  }
else if (val == NULL)
  {
    // Fall back to a default value.
    val = g_strdup ("default-value");
  }
```
Here is an example of creating and saving a key file:

**⚠️ The following code is in c ⚠️**

```
g_autoptr(GKeyFile) key_file = g_key_file_new ();
const gchar *val = …;
g_autoptr(GError) error = NULL;
g_key_file_set_string (key_file, "Group Name", "SomeKey", val);
// Save as a file.
if (!g_key_file_save_to_file (key_file, "key-file.ini", &error))
  {
    g_warning ("Error saving key file: %s", error->message);
    return;
  }
// Or store to a GBytes for use elsewhere.
gsize data_len;
g_autofree guint8 *data = (guint8 *) g_key_file_to_data (key_file, &data_len, &error);
if (data == NULL)
  {
    g_warning ("Error saving key file: %s", error->message);
    return;
  }
g_autoptr(GBytes) bytes = g_bytes_new_take (g_steal_pointer (&data), data_len);
```
GLib type: Shared boxed type with reference counted clone semantics.

Retrieves a comment above @key from @group_name.

If @key is `NULL` then @comment will be read from above
@group_name. If both @key and @group_name are `NULL`, then
@comment will be read from above the first group in the file.

Note that the returned string does not include the `#` comment markers,
but does include any whitespace after them (on each line). It includes
the line breaks between lines, but does not include the final line break.

If @key cannot be found then [error@GLib.KeyFileError.KEY_NOT_FOUND] is returned. Likewise, if the value associated with @key cannot be interpreted as a double then [error@GLib.KeyFileError.INVALID_VALUE] is returned.

) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<[PathBuf](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/path/struct.PathBuf.html), [Error](https://gtk-rs.org/error/struct.Error.html)>

[Source](https://gtk-rs.org/src/glib/key_file.rs.html#118-144)

#### pub fn [load_from_dirs](https://gtk-rs.org#method.load_from_dirs)<T: [AsRef](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/convert/trait.AsRef.html)<[Path](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/path/struct.Path.html)>, U: [AsRef](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/convert/trait.AsRef.html)<[Path](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/path/struct.Path.html)>>(
    &self,
    file: T,
    search_dirs: &[[U]](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.slice.html),
    flags: [KeyFileFlags](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.KeyFileFlags.html),
) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<[PathBuf](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/path/struct.PathBuf.html), [Error](https://gtk-rs.org/error/struct.Error.html)>

Looks for a key file named @file in the paths specified in @search_dirs, loads the file into @self and returns the file’s full path in @full_path.

@search_dirs are checked in the order listed in the array, with the highest
priority directory listed first. Within each directory, @file is looked for.
If it’s not found, `-` characters in @file are progressively replaced with
directory separators to search subdirectories of the search directory. If the
file has not been found after all `-` characters have been replaced, the next
search directory in @search_dirs is checked.

If the file could not be found in any of the @search_dirs,
[error@GLib.KeyFileError.NOT_FOUND] is returned. If
the file is found but the OS returns an error when opening or reading the
file, a [ FileError](https://gtk-rs.org/enum.FileError.html) is returned. If there is a problem parsing the
file, a

[is returned.](https://gtk-rs.org/enum.KeyFileError.html)

`KeyFileError`[§](https://gtk-rs.org#file-2)`file`

a relative path to a filename to open and parse

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#search_dirs)`search_dirs`

`NULL`-terminated
array of directories to search

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#flags-4)`flags`

flags from `KeyFileFlags`

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#returns-21)Returns

true if a key file could be loaded, false otherwise

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#full_path-1)`full_path`

return location for a string
containing the full path of the file, or `NULL` to ignore

Returns the value associated with @key under @group_name translated in the given @locale if available.

If @locale is `C` then the untranslated value is returned (since GLib 2.84).

If @locale is `NULL` then the current locale is assumed.

If @locale is to be non-`NULL`, or if the current locale will change over
the lifetime of the [ KeyFile](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.KeyFile.html), it must be loaded with
[flags@GLib.KeyFileFlags.KEEP_TRANSLATIONS] in order to load strings for all
locales.

If @key cannot be found then [error@GLib.KeyFileError.KEY_NOT_FOUND] is returned. If the value associated with @key cannot be interpreted or no suitable translation can be found then the untranslated value is returned.

[105](https://gtk-rs.org#105)    /// Runs a single iteration for the given main loop.
[106](https://gtk-rs.org#106)    ///
[107](https://gtk-rs.org#107)    /// This involves
[108](https://gtk-rs.org#108)    /// checking to see if any event sources are ready to be processed,
[109](https://gtk-rs.org#109)    /// then if no events sources are ready and @may_block is true, waiting
[110](https://gtk-rs.org#110)    /// for a source to become ready, then dispatching the highest priority
[111](https://gtk-rs.org#111)    /// events sources that are ready. Otherwise, if @may_block is false,
[112](https://gtk-rs.org#112)    /// this function does not wait for sources to become ready, and only the highest
[113](https://gtk-rs.org#113)    /// priority sources which are already ready (if any) will be dispatched.
[114](https://gtk-rs.org#114)    ///
[115](https://gtk-rs.org#115)    /// Note that even when @may_block is true, it is still possible for
[116](https://gtk-rs.org#116)    /// [`iteration()`][Self::iteration()] to return false, since the wait may
[117](https://gtk-rs.org#117)    /// be interrupted for other reasons than an event source becoming ready.
[118](https://gtk-rs.org#118)    /// ## `may_block`

[120](https://gtk-rs.org#120)    ///

[122](https://gtk-rs.org#122)    ///

# MainContext in glib - Rust

Source: https://gtk-rs.org/gtk-rs-core/stable/latest/docs/glib/struct.MainContext.html

`pub struct MainContext { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

The `GMainContext` struct is an opaque data
type representing a set of sources to be handled in a main loop.

GLib type: Shared boxed type with reference counted clone semantics.

## Implementations[§](https://gtk-rs.org#implementations)

`v2_72`Determines whether this thread holds the (recursive)
ownership of this [ MainContext](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.MainContext.html).

This is useful to know before waiting on another thread that may be blocking to get ownership of @self.

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#returns-2)Returns

true if current thread is owner of @self, false otherwise

Runs a single iteration for the given main loop.

This involves checking to see if any event sources are ready to be processed, then if no events sources are ready and @may_block is true, waiting for a source to become ready, then dispatching the highest priority events sources that are ready. Otherwise, if @may_block is false, this function does not wait for sources to become ready, and only the highest priority sources which are already ready (if any) will be dispatched.

Note that even when @may_block is true, it is still possible for
[ iteration()](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.MainContext.html#method.iteration) to return false, since the wait may
be interrupted for other reasons than an event source becoming ready.

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#may_block)`may_block`

whether the call may block

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#returns-3)Returns

true if events were dispatched, false otherwise

Wake up @self if it’s currently blocking in
[ iteration()](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.MainContext.html#method.iteration), causing it to stop blocking.

The @self could be blocking waiting for a source to become ready.
Otherwise, if @self is not currently blocking, this function causes the
next invocation of [ iteration()](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.MainContext.html#method.iteration) to return without
blocking.

This API is useful for low-level control over [ MainContext](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.MainContext.html); for
example, integrating it with main loop implementations such as

[.](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.MainLoop.html)

`MainLoop`Another related use for this function is when implementing a main loop with a termination condition, computed from multiple threads:

**⚠️ The following code is in c ⚠️**

```
  #define NUM_TASKS 10
  static gint tasks_remaining = NUM_TASKS;  // (atomic)
  ...
  while (g_atomic_int_get (&tasks_remaining) != 0)
    g_main_context_iteration (NULL, TRUE);
```
Then in a thread:
**⚠️ The following code is in c ⚠️**

```
  perform_work ();
  if (g_atomic_int_dec_and_test (&tasks_remaining))
    g_main_context_wakeup (NULL);
```

### impl [MainContext](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.MainContext.html)

Prepares to poll sources within a main loop.

The resulting information
for polling is determined by calling `GLib::MainContext::query()`.

You must have successfully acquired the context with
[ acquire()](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.MainContext.html#method.acquire) before you may call this function.

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#returns-8)Returns

true if some source is ready to be dispatched prior to polling, false otherwise

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#priority)`priority`

location to store priority of highest priority source already ready

[Source](https://gtk-rs.org/src/glib/main_context.rs.html#59-66)#### pub fn [find_source_by_id](https://gtk-rs.org#method.find_source_by_id)(&self, source_id: &[SourceId](https://gtk-rs.org/source/struct.SourceId.html)) -> [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<[Source](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.Source.html)>

[Source](https://gtk-rs.org/src/glib/main_context.rs.html#59-66)

#### pub fn [find_source_by_id](https://gtk-rs.org#method.find_source_by_id)(&self, source_id: &[SourceId](https://gtk-rs.org/source/struct.SourceId.html)) -> [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<[Source](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.Source.html)>

Finds a [ Source](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.Source.html) given a pair of context and ID.

It is a programmer error to attempt to look up a non-existent source.

More specifically: source IDs can be reissued after a source has been
destroyed and therefore it is never valid to use this function with a
source ID which may have already been removed.  An example is when
scheduling an idle to run in another thread with `idle_add()`: the
idle may already have run and been removed by the time this function
is called on its (now invalid) source ID.  This source ID may have
been reissued, leading to the operation being performed against the
wrong source.

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#source_id)`source_id`

the source ID, as returned by `GLib::Source::get_id()`

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#returns-9)Returns

the source

Invokes `func` on the main context.

If the current thread is the owner of the main context or the main context currently has no
owner then `func` will be called directly from inside this function. If this behaviour is
not desired and `func` should always be called asynchronously then use `MainContext::spawn`[ glib::idle_add](https://gtk-rs.org/source/fn.idle_add.html) instead.
Invokes a function in such a way that @self is owned during the
invocation of @function.

If @self is `NULL` then the global-default main context — as
returned by [ default()](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.MainContext.html#method.default) — is used.

If @self is owned by the current thread, @function is called
directly.  Otherwise, if @self is the thread-default main context
of the current thread and [ acquire()](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.MainContext.html#method.acquire) succeeds,
then @function is called and [

`release()`][Self::release()] is called
afterwards.In any other case, an idle source is created to call @function and
that source is attached to @self (presumably to be run in another
thread).  The idle source is attached with `GLib::PRIORITY_DEFAULT`
priority.  If you want a different priority, use
[`invoke_full()`][Self::invoke_full()].

Note that, as with normal idle functions, @function should probably return
`GLib::SOURCE_REMOVE`.  If it returns `GLib::SOURCE_CONTINUE`, it
will be continuously run in a loop (and may prevent this call from returning).

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#function)`function`

function to call

#### pub fn [invoke_local](https://gtk-rs.org#method.invoke_local)<F>(&self, func: F)

Invokes `func` on the main context.

Different to `invoke()`, this does not require `func` to be
`Send` but can only be called from the thread that owns the main context.

This function panics if called from a different thread than the one that owns the main context.

Note that this effectively means that `func` is called directly from inside this function
or otherwise panics immediately. If this behaviour is not desired and `func` should always
be called asynchronously then use `MainContext::spawn_local`[ glib::idle_add_local](https://gtk-rs.org/source/fn.idle_add_local.html) instead.

[Source](https://gtk-rs.org/src/glib/main_context.rs.html#257-264)#### pub fn [with_thread_default](https://gtk-rs.org#method.with_thread_default)<R, F: [FnOnce](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/ops/function/trait.FnOnce.html)() -> R + [Sized](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/marker/trait.Sized.html)>(

#### pub fn [with_thread_default](https://gtk-rs.org#method.with_thread_default)<R, F: [FnOnce](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/ops/function/trait.FnOnce.html)() -> R + [Sized](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/marker/trait.Sized.html)>(

Call closure with the main context configured as the thread default one.

The thread default main context is changed in a panic-safe manner before calling `func` and
released again afterwards regardless of whether closure panicked or not.

This will fail if the main context is owned already by another thread.
Acquires @self and sets it as the thread-default context for the
current thread. This will cause certain asynchronous operations
(such as most [Gio](https://gtk-rs.org/gio/index.html)-based I/O) which are
started in this thread to run under @self and deliver their
results to its main loop, rather than running under the global
default main context in the main thread. Note that calling this function
changes the context returned by [ thread_default()](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.MainContext.html#method.thread_default),
not the one returned by

[, so it does not affect the context used by functions like](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.MainContext.html#method.default)

`default()``idle_add()`.Normally you would call this function shortly after creating a new
thread, passing it a [ MainContext](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.MainContext.html) which will be run by a

[in that thread, to set a new default context for all async operations in that thread. In this case you may not need to ever call [](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.MainLoop.html)

`MainLoop``pop_thread_default()`][Self::pop_thread_default()], assuming you want
the new [to be the default for the whole lifecycle of the thread.](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.MainContext.html)

`MainContext`If you don’t have control over how the new thread was created (e.g.
in the new thread isn’t newly created, or if the thread life
cycle is managed by a #GThreadPool), it is always suggested to wrap
the logic that needs to use the new [ MainContext](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.MainContext.html) inside a

[/ [](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.MainContext.html#method.with_thread_default)

`with_thread_default()``pop_thread_default()`][Self::pop_thread_default()] pair, otherwise threads that
are re-used will end up never explicitly releasing the
[reference they hold.](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.MainContext.html)

`MainContext`In some cases you may want to schedule a single operation in a
non-default context, or temporarily use a non-default context in
the main thread. In that case, you can wrap the call to the
asynchronous operation inside a
[ with_thread_default()](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.MainContext.html#method.with_thread_default) /
[

`pop_thread_default()`][Self::pop_thread_default()] pair, but it is up to you to
ensure that no other asynchronous operations accidentally get
started while the non-default context is active.Beware that libraries that predate this function may not correctly
handle being used from a thread with a thread-default context. For example,
see `g_file_supports_thread_contexts()`.

[Source](https://gtk-rs.org/src/glib/main_context.rs.html#293-304)#### pub fn [acquire](https://gtk-rs.org#method.acquire)(&self) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<[MainContextAcquireGuard](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.MainContextAcquireGuard.html)<'_>, [BoolError](https://gtk-rs.org/error/struct.BoolError.html)>

[Source](https://gtk-rs.org/src/glib/main_context.rs.html#293-304)

#### pub fn [acquire](https://gtk-rs.org#method.acquire)(&self) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<[MainContextAcquireGuard](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.MainContextAcquireGuard.html)<'_>, [BoolError](https://gtk-rs.org/error/struct.BoolError.html)>

Acquire ownership of the main context.

Ownership will automatically be released again once the returned acquire guard is dropped.

This will fail if the main context is owned already by another thread. Tries to become the owner of the specified context.

If some other thread is the owner of the context,
returns false immediately. Ownership is properly
recursive: the owner can require ownership again
and will release ownership when [`release()`][Self::release()]
is called as many times as [ acquire()](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.MainContext.html#method.acquire).

You must be the owner of a context before you
can call [ prepare()](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.MainContext.html#method.prepare),

`GLib::MainContext::query()`,
`GLib::MainContext::check()`, [, [](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.MainContext.html#method.dispatch)

`dispatch()``release()`][Self::release()].Since 2.76 @self can be `NULL` to use the global-default
main context.

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#returns-10)Returns

true if this thread is now the owner of @self, false otherwise

**crate feature**only.

`futures`Spawn a new infallible `Future` on the main context from inside the main context.

The given `Future` does not have to be `Send` but the closure to spawn it has to be.

This can be called only from any thread.

Runs a new, infallible `Future` on the main context and block until it finished, returning
the result of the `Future`.

The given `Future` does not have to be `Send` or `'static`.

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#panics)Panics

This panics if the main context can’t be acquired on this thread and can’t be made the thread default, which means that some other thread currently owns it.

`pub struct MainLoop { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

The `GMainLoop` struct is an opaque data type
representing the main event loop of a GLib or GTK application.

GLib type: Shared boxed type with reference counted clone semantics.

[265](https://gtk-rs.org#265)    /// Feed some data to the #GMarkupParseContext.
[266](https://gtk-rs.org#266)    ///
[267](https://gtk-rs.org#267)    /// The data need not be valid UTF-8; an error will be signaled if
[268](https://gtk-rs.org#268)    /// it's invalid. The data need not be an entire document; you can
[269](https://gtk-rs.org#269)    /// feed a document into the parser incrementally, via multiple calls
[270](https://gtk-rs.org#270)    /// to this function. Typically, as you receive data from a network
[271](https://gtk-rs.org#271)    /// connection or file, you feed each received chunk of data into this
[272](https://gtk-rs.org#272)    /// function, aborting the process if an error occurs. Once an error
[273](https://gtk-rs.org#273)    /// is reported, no further data may be fed to the #GMarkupParseContext;
[274](https://gtk-rs.org#274)    /// all errors are fatal.
[275](https://gtk-rs.org#275)    /// ## `text`
[276](https://gtk-rs.org#276)    /// chunk of text to parse
[277](https://gtk-rs.org#277)    /// ## `text_len`
[278](https://gtk-rs.org#278)    /// length of @text in bytes
[279](https://gtk-rs.org#279)    ///
[280](https://gtk-rs.org#280)    /// # Returns
[281](https://gtk-rs.org#281)    ///
[282](https://gtk-rs.org#282)    /// [`false`] if an error occurred, [`true`] on success

# MarkupParseContext in glib - Rust

Source: https://gtk-rs.org/gtk-rs-core/stable/latest/docs/glib/struct.MarkupParseContext.html

`pub struct MarkupParseContext { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

A parse context is used to parse a stream of bytes that you expect to contain marked-up text.

See g_markup_parse_context_new(), #GMarkupParser, and so on for more details.

GLib type: Shared boxed type with reference counted clone semantics.

## Implementations[§](https://gtk-rs.org#implementations)

**crate feature**only.

`v2_90`Retrieves the start and end positions of an attribute assignment in a start tag.

This function can be used in the `start_element` callback to
obtain location information for error reporting.

Calling it outside of the `start_element` callback
has undefined results.

Note that @line_number and @char_number are intended for human readable error messages and are therefore 1-based and in Unicode characters. @offset on the other hand is meant for programmatic use, and thus is 0-based and in bytes.

The information is meant to accompany the values returned by
[ position()](https://gtk-rs.org/struct.MarkupParseContext.html#method.position), and comes with the
same accuracy guarantees.

Retrieves the element stack from the internal state of the parser.

The returned #GSList is a list of strings where the first item is the currently open tag (as would be returned by g_markup_parse_context_get_element()) and the next item is its immediate parent.

This function is intended to be used in the start_element and end_element handlers where g_markup_parse_context_get_element() would merely return the name of the element that is being processed.

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#returns-3)Returns

the element stack, which must not be modified

the offset

Retrieves the current line number and the number of the character on that line. Intended for use in error messages; there are no strict semantics for what constitutes the “current” line number other than “the best number we could come up with for error messages.”

[§](https://gtk-rs.org#returns-5)Returns
